meanings: about the only ~; ~ is just about the only one
structure: Verb［plain form］＋のは＋Noun＋くらいのものだ
explanation: 〜くらいのものだ narrows things down to essentially a single case — 'that's about the only one'. こんなことを言うのは彼くらいのものだ = he's about the only one who'd say such a thing. It attaches to a noun (often after a 〜のは clause), and the くらい softens a flat 'only' into 'more or less the sole case'. The tone is one of resigned or wry observation that scarcely anyone else qualifies.

synonyms.note: だけ states 'only' flatly; くらいのものだ softens it to 'about the only one', with a resigned or wry undertone.
にすぎない downplays something as 'no more than'; くらいのものだ limits the field to essentially a single case.

meanings: can't afford to stay ~; can't just keep ~ing
explanation: てはいられない is the negative potential of ている plus は — 'cannot remain in this state'. It says the speaker cannot afford to keep doing something or stay as they are because circumstances demand action — のんびりしてはいられない = 'I can't afford to take it easy'. It conveys urgency or emotional pressure to stop and act.

synonyms.note: てばかりはいられない adds ばかり ('only'), stressing you can't do just that one thing forever; てはいられない is the plain 'can't stay as I am'.

meanings: of all people; someone who is supposed to be ~
structure: Noun［person of status／role］＋ともあろうものが
explanation: 〜ともあろうものが attaches to a person of standing or a respected role and voices criticism or disbelief that someone in that position acted unworthily — 'for someone who is supposed to be ~ to do that'. 教師ともあろう者が = a person who is supposedly a teacher, of all people. The clause that follows expresses disappointment that their reputation should have prevented the behavior. 者 may also appear as 者が or the ending as ものだ.

synonyms.note: としたことが notes an out-of-character blunder, often one's own; ともあろうものが judges someone by their lofty role.

related.note: まじき labels conduct as unbefitting a role (〜にあるまじき); ともあろうものが names the person and expresses the disbelief directly.
とは voices the bare surprise; ともあろうものが frames that surprise around a person's status.

meanings: at least this much; to do all one can of
structure: Verb［dictionary form］ ＋ だけは ＋ （Verb）［same verb repeated］
explanation: だけは singles out one thing as a guaranteed minimum — whatever else happens, at least this holds or gets done. A common shape repeats the verb: やるだけはやる = 'do at least all I can'. It stresses that one point, and only that, is assured, often staying non-committal about the outcome.

related.note: だけ is the base 'only/just'; だけは adds the sense of a singled-out, guaranteed minimum.
限り marks 'as much as / to the limit of' (できる限り); it overlaps with the やれるだけ effort sense of だけは.

meanings: if by any chance; in the unlikely event; just in case
structure: 万が一 ＋ Verb［たら／ば／なら］
万が一 ＋ に備える／のこと
explanation: 万が一 (literally 'one in ten thousand') introduces a remote, usually undesirable possibility — 'if by some chance / in the unlikely event'. As an adverb it pairs with a conditional (たら/ば/なら) and often prepares for the worst. It can also work as a noun: 万が一に備える ('prepare for any eventuality').

synonyms.note: もし marks any hypothetical; 万が一 adds that the case is remote and usually unwelcome.

related.note: たとえ〜ても concedes 'even if'; 万が一 sets up a rare possibility to prepare for, not to concede.

meanings: otherwise; or else
explanation: さもないと follows a command, warning, or statement of what must be done, and spells out the bad consequence of not complying: 早くしなさい。さもないと遅れるよ = hurry up — otherwise you'll be late. Literally 'if it is not so', it always points to an undesirable outcome, which makes it a natural partner for warnings. さもなければ and the stiffer さもなくば mean the same; in casual speech, そうしないと is more common.

related.note: ないと puts the same warning inside one sentence (急がないと遅れる); さもないと starts a new sentence with 'otherwise'.

meanings: not (classical negative, = ない)
structure: する → せぬ ／ 来る → 来ぬ（こぬ）
explanation: 〜ぬ is the classical negative ending, equivalent to modern 〜ない. It attaches to the same stem as ない (知らぬ = 知らない, 思わぬ = 思わない), with the irregular せぬ for する and 来ぬ(こぬ) for 来る. Today it survives mainly in set phrases, proverbs, and a stiff literary or archaic tone (見知らぬ人, 思わぬ結果).

synonyms.note: 〜ざる is the classical negative used attributively before a noun; ぬ is its plain sentence-ending counterpart, overlapping closely.

related.note: ずに 'without doing' comes from the same classical negative ず; ぬ is the counterpart meaning simply 'not'.

meanings: whether ~ or ~ (I can't tell which)
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋のやら＋Sentence［plain form］＋のやら
explanation: 〜のやら〜のやら pairs two possibilities — often opposites — to say the speaker can't tell which is the case. 本当なのやら嘘なのやら = whether it's true or a lie, no telling. It joins two plain-form clauses and frequently takes the shape 〜のやら〜ないのやら ('whether ~ or not'). The tone conveys genuine puzzlement or resignation.

synonyms.note: the single 〜のやら／ものやら expresses one unresolved question; the paired 〜のやら〜のやら weighs two possibilities against each other.

meanings: above all; more than anything; best of all
structure: 何より（も） ＋ predicate ［above all else］
〜（て／で）何よりだ ［nothing could be better; so glad］
explanation: 何より(も) means 'more than anything else', marking what is most important or valued — 健康が何より大切だ = 'health matters above all'. As the set phrase 〜が何よりだ, it expresses relief or gladness that nothing could be better: ご無事で何よりです = 'I'm so glad you're safe'.

synonyms.note: 何といっても also singles out the top point 'after all'; 何より more plainly ranks one thing as most important or best.

related.note: 一番 is the everyday superlative 'the most / number one'; 何より is a more emphatic 'more than anything else'.

meanings: a particle kept before の to modify a following noun (からの, での, との…)
structure: Noun ＋ 助詞（から／で／と／へ／まで…）＋ の ＋ Noun
explanation: When a phrase marked by a particle like から, で, と, or へ needs to modify a noun, you keep that particle and add の — 母からの手紙 = "a letter from mother," 東京での生活 = "life in Tokyo." The particle keeps its normal meaning (from / at / with…) and の links the whole phrase to the noun.

related.note: Plain の joins two nouns directly (私の本); 助詞＋の keeps a meaning-particle in front of the の.

meanings: gotta do; must do (casual)
structure: Verb［ない → なくては］→ なくちゃ
Verb［ない → なければ］→ なきゃ
explanation: Casual spoken contractions of the 'must do' forms: なくちゃ shortens なくては and なきゃ shortens なければ. Both say "I've gotta do it". The いけない/ならない ending is usually left off, so the contraction alone carries the sense of obligation in relaxed conversation.

synonyms.note: The full form なくては behind なくちゃ, used when speaking more carefully.
Another everyday way to express the same obligation.

related.note: The なければ/ならない forms these contractions come from, more formal in tone.

meanings: isn't it?; hey, it's ~! (agreement or surprise)
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋ じゃないか
explanation: じゃないか tacks onto a statement to seek agreement or to voice surprise at something just noticed: 君の傘じゃないか = 'hey, isn't this your umbrella?'. Despite containing ない, it usually asserts the statement rather than negating it.

synonyms.note: ではないか is the formal, written counterpart of the same assertion-question.

related.note: ね softly invites agreement; じゃないか pushes for it more forcefully.
じゃない (N5) is the plain negative that this pattern is built on.

meanings: contrary to what one thought; one would think ~, but actually
explanation: 〜かと思いきや sets up an expectation and then overturns it: you thought A, but in fact the opposite or something quite different turned out to be the case. 思いきや is a fixed classical form and gives the phrase a slightly literary, sometimes wry tone. It attaches to a plain-form clause (a noun or な-adjective may drop だ). The reality after it always contradicts the assumption before it.

related.note: に反して neutrally states a result running counter to an expectation or standard; かと思いきや dramatizes the speaker's own assumption being upended.
とはいえ concedes a point then qualifies it; かと思いきや reveals that the anticipated situation was simply wrong.

meanings: no sooner had ~ than; the moment ~; barely had X happened when Y
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋ か ＋ Verb［ない form］＋ か ＋ のうちに
explanation: This pattern repeats one verb — first in the dictionary form, then in the ない form — to say that a second event happens almost the very instant the first does: 'X had barely happened when Y'. The two events are nearly simultaneous, and Y typically follows on immediately.

synonyms.note: た途端 also marks 'the moment after', but follows a past-tense verb; this pattern stresses that the first action had barely finished.
が早いか is a more literary 'as soon as'; か〜ないかのうちに emphasizes the two events overlapping almost to the instant.

related.note: かと思ったら also links two quick events, but adds surprise that the second is unexpected; this pattern is purely about timing.

meanings: judging from the fact that ~
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋ ところを見ると
explanation: ところを見ると draws an inference from an observed fact — 'judging from the fact that ~'. 笑っているところを見ると、うまくいったのだろう = 'judging from the fact that she's smiling, it must have gone well'. The speaker reasons from visible evidence to a likely conclusion, usually ending in a conjecture.

synonyms.note: から見ると can mean 'judging from' too, but also 'from the viewpoint of'; ところを見ると specifically reasons from an observed fact.

related.note: からして also reasons 'judging from' a single telling detail; ところを見ると points to an observed scene as the evidence.

meanings: (more) than ~; rather than ~ (comparison, with emphasis)
explanation: よりも is より 'than' with emphatic も, marking the standard of comparison and stressing the gap — 去年よりも暑い = even hotter than last year. The thing being compared against comes before よりも (Aよりも B = B, more than A).

synonyms.note: より is the plain 'than'; よりも is the same with emphasis on the difference.

related.note: 〜より〜ほうが frames a two-way choice ('B is more ~ than A'); よりも just marks the standard being beaten.
というより corrects a description ('rather than say A, it's B'); よりも compares degrees or preferences.

meanings: to no avail; in vain, despite one's efforts
structure: Verb［plain form／た form］＋甲斐もなく
explanation: 〜甲斐もなく says that despite the effort or care put in, it brought no worthwhile result — 'for all one's ~, it was in vain'. 看病の甲斐もなく = despite all the nursing, to no avail; 努力の甲斐もなく不合格だった = for all the effort, still failed. meanings: according to (a source) ~
structure: Noun ＋ によると／によれば ＋ Sentence ＋ そうだ／らしい
explanation: によると (or によれば) names the source of information you are passing on — 天気予報によると = according to the weather forecast. The sentence it introduces is reported speech, so it usually ends in a hearsay marker like そうだ, らしい, or だろう. Use it to make clear you got the information from somewhere else rather than from your own direct knowledge.

related.note: そうだ reports what you heard; によると names the source it came from — the two often appear together.
によって marks means, cause, or agent; によると marks the source of reported information.
って casually quotes or reports something; によると introduces the source more explicitly and politely.

meanings: seems like; looks like; apparently
structure: Verb ／ い-adjective［plain form］＋ みたいだ
explanation: みたいだ voices a guess or impression from what the speaker sees, hears, or senses — 'it seems / looks like ~'. It's the casual, conversational counterpart of ようだ. It attaches straight to plain forms and to nouns with no の: 雨みたいだ (looks like rain).

みたいな・みたいに is the same word used to say 'like/similar to'; みたいだ ends a sentence as a guess.

meanings: nothing (at all); no need to go so far as to ~

explanation: 何も with a negative predicate has two uses. Plainly it means 'nothing / not anything at all' — 何も残っていない = 'nothing is left'. Emphatically, 何も〜ことはない / 〜なくてもいい means 'there's no need to go so far as to ~', pushing back on an overreaction: 何もそこまで怒ることはない = 'no need to get that angry'.

meanings: because (of the special circumstance); given that
explanation: 〜とあって presents a special or noteworthy circumstance as the reason a fitting consequence follows naturally — 'because it's ~, given that ~'. 連休とあって = it being a long holiday (so naturally...), 人気店とあって = as it's a popular shop. The situation is unusual or newsworthy enough that the result comes as a matter of course. It is common in reportage and in describing others' situations objectively.

synonyms.note: だけあって praises a result as living up to what a quality would lead you to expect; とあって simply gives a special situation as the reason a natural result follows.
こととて offers a reason in a soft, apologetic, literary tone; とあって states a notable circumstance behind an unremarkable-to-expect result.

related.note: だけに stresses 'precisely because ~, all the more'; とあって leans on the situation being special or newsworthy.

meanings: sure enough; just as expected; really ~? (intensifying doubt in a question)
structure: 果たして ＋ Sentence［statement: 'as expected' sense］
果たして ＋ Sentence［question with か／のだろうか: 'really ~?' sense］
explanation: 果たして is an adverb with two related uses. Before a statement it means 'sure enough / just as one expected', confirming that a prediction came true. In a question — typically with か or のだろうか — it sharpens the doubt, 'really…? / I wonder if it truly…'. It belongs to careful, somewhat written or formal speech.

related.note: 果たして…のだろうか pairs だろう with 'really?' emphasis; だろう alone is plain conjecture without that pointed doubt.

surface: でできる・からできる
reading: でできる・からできる
meanings: to be made of; to be made from
structure: Noun［material］＋ で ＋ できている
Noun［material］＋ から ＋ できる／作る
explanation: Two ways to state what something is made of. Noun＋で marks a material that is still recognizable in the product (木でできた机 = a desk made of wood). Noun＋から marks a raw material that has been transformed so it's no longer obvious (ワインはぶどうから). できている ('is made of') is used for the resulting state.

synonyms.note: から作る actively says 'make from'; からできる says the result 'is made from' that material.

meanings: as long as; as far as; within the limits of
structure: Verb［dictionary form／ない form］＋ 限り
explanation: 限り sets a boundary on a statement. Its main senses are 'as long as / so long as' a condition holds (Vる・Nである限り), and 'as far as' the speaker's information reaches (見る限り, 知る限り). The core idea is that the main clause is true only within the limit or scope named.

related.note: に限る comes from the same root but means 'nothing beats ~ / be limited to ~'; 限り sets the scope of a condition or judgment.
とは限らない, also from 限る, means 'not necessarily'; 限り marks the boundary within which a statement is valid.

meanings: always; usually
explanation: いつも is an adverb meaning 'always' or 'usually' — it says an action or state holds all or most of the time. It normally comes before the verb it describes: いつも早く起きます = I always get up early. It describes a habit, not one particular occasion.

meanings: apparently; it seems that
structure: どうやら ＋ Sentence（〜らしい／ようだ／みたいだ）
explanation: どうやら is an adverb that flags a tentative inference from available signs — 'apparently / it seems'. It typically pairs with a conjectural ending like らしい, ようだ, or みたいだ (どうやら風邪をひいたようだ). It softens a guess the speaker is fairly, but not fully, sure of.

related.note: らしい is the conjecture ending どうやら commonly leads into; どうやら is the adverb that flags the inference.
ようだ likewise expresses an evidence-based guess; どうやら pairs with it to underline that the conclusion is tentative.

I said ~! ; come on, ~ (impatient insistence or exasperation)
explanation: Both are colloquial sentence-enders that add impatience or exasperation. ってば reasserts something the listener didn't heed — もう行くってば = I said I'm going! ったら similarly nags or scolds, and after a person's name expresses exasperated fondness or complaint — お父さんったら = oh, Dad, honestly… They belong to casual spoken Japanese and always carry clear emotion.

meanings: whether A or B; be it A or B (it makes no difference)
explanation: Placing であれ after each of two (or more) nouns lists them as alternatives that don't change the outcome — 'whether A or B'. 大人であれ子どもであれ、ルールは同じだ = whether adult or child, the rules are the same. であれ is the concessive form of である, so the register is formal or written. The main clause states something that holds across every listed case.

synonyms.note: single であれ pairs with a question word ('no matter what/who'); であれ〜であれ lists two specific named alternatives.
にしろ〜にしろ also lists 'whether A or B' alternatives; であれ〜であれ is a touch more formal and literary.

related.note: ようが〜ようが lists contrasting verb or adjective cases ('whether one does or not'); であれ〜であれ lists noun alternatives.

meanings: even; even though; although one may say ~
explanation: 〜といえども concedes a point and then states something that holds despite it — 'even ~, even though it is ~'. プロといえども = even a professional, 子供といえども = even though they're just a child. It grants that the subject is X, yet the following clause runs against the expectation X would create. It is formal, somewhat literary, and often pairs with a sweeping generalization.

synonyms.note: ても is the everyday 'even if / even though'; といえども says the same with a formal, literary, concessive weight.

related.note: ものの concedes an established fact then notes it fell short of expectation; といえども concedes a category ('even a ~') before a contrary rule.
ながらも marks 'although, despite ~' between two facts of one subject; といえども concedes a generalized case.

meanings: although; even though; despite ~
explanation: ながらも is a concessive connector: it links two clauses that clash, meaning 'although / despite'. It attaches to a verb ます-stem, an い-adjective, a な-adjective, or a noun — 忙しいと言いながらも ('although he says he's busy'), 狭いながらも ('cramped though it is'). The も makes the contrast explicit, so what follows goes against what the first part leads you to expect.

synonyms.note: Plain concessive ながら carries the same 'although'; ながらも just states the contrast more firmly.
ものの also means 'although' but is more written; ながらも attaches tightly to a stem or adjective.

related.note: のに often adds complaint or dissatisfaction; ながらも is a neutral concessive.

meanings: right in the middle of; in the very midst of
explanation: 最中に marks the peak of an ongoing action, often the moment something cuts in — 食事の最中に (right in the middle of dinner), 話している最中に (right as I was talking). It stresses that the action was at full swing when interruption or an event occurred.

related.note: ているところ marks the stage of an action ('in the middle of doing'); 最中に stresses its very peak, often interrupted.
間に marks a span during which something happens; 最中に zooms in on the height of one ongoing action.
うちに means 'while a state lasts / before it changes'; 最中に is 'right at the peak of an action.'

meanings: based on; taking ~ into account
explanation: 〜を踏まえて means taking established facts, results, or opinions as the grounds for the next judgment or action: 現状を踏まえて対策を立てる = draw up measures taking the current situation into account; 前回の反省を踏まえて = building on the lessons of last time. 踏まえる means 'to base oneself on', so the reference is something already known and considered, not a future hypothetical. It is formal and common in discussion and policy.

synonyms.note: をもとに uses X as source material to produce something; を踏まえて takes X into consideration as grounds for a judgment.

related.note: を前提に assumes a condition as given going forward; を踏まえて builds on facts already established.

meanings: while doing; concurrently; on the side
explanation: 〜かたわら presents two ongoing pursuits: while doing A as one's main occupation, one also does B on the side over the same period. 傍ら literally means 'beside', and the figure is of B running parallel to a central activity — 仕事のかたわら (alongside one's work), 教えるかたわら (while teaching). It attaches to a dictionary-form verb or a noun + の, and belongs to written, somewhat literary style.

meanings: there's nothing better than; it's best to ~
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋ に越したことはない
い-adjective ＋ に越したことはない
Noun／な-adjective ＋（である）＋ に越したことはない
explanation: に越したことはない says a certain state is the ideal one to have, even if not strictly required — 用心するに越したことはない ('you can't go wrong being cautious'). It gently recommends the best option while allowing that the less-ideal alternative is still acceptable.

synonyms.note: に限る flatly declares N the best; に越したことはない softly recommends it while leaving room for other options.

related.note: ほうがいい gives a plain 'you'd better'; に越したことはない frames it as 'nothing beats it, though it isn't a must'.

meanings: in the same way as; just as; exactly as
explanation: とおり(に) says an action happens exactly the way something else describes or predicts. After a verb it uses the plain form — 私が言ったとおりになった = it turned out just as I said; 書いてあるとおりに作る = make it just as it is written. After a noun, join with の — 地図のとおりに行く = go exactly as the map shows. The に is often dropped with no change in meaning.

related.note: まま keeps a state unchanged while you do something else; とおり(に) matches an action to a model or instruction.

meanings: it's true that ~, but; ~, yes, but ~ (partial concession)
structure: ［plain form］＋ ことは ＋ ［same word, plain form］＋ が／けれど ＋ Sentence
explanation: By repeating the same predicate around ことは and following with が, you concede a point partway before qualifying it — 話せることは話せるが (I can speak it, sure, but…). It admits the first half is true, then adds a reservation.

related.note: けど simply joins a 'but' clause; ことは〜が specifically concedes the point half-heartedly before qualifying it.
ものの concedes an established fact then adds a contrary result; ことは〜が repeats the predicate to grant it only partly.
とはいえ is a formal 'that said'; ことは〜が is a colloquial 'true, but' built by repeating the word.

meanings: while (still) ~; before ~ changes
explanation: 〜うちに picks out a window of time and says to act within it. After a plain state it means 'while ~ still holds' (熱いうちに = while it's still hot); after a ない-form it means 'before ~ happens' (忘れないうちに = before I forget). The nuance is that the window will close, so do it now.

related.note: 〜間に marks a defined span and something happening within it; 〜うちに adds the sense that the state may change, so act now.
〜ないうちに is the negative pattern of this point — 'before ~ happens'; plain 〜うちに is 'while ~ still lasts'.
〜前に just says 'before' a point in time; 〜ないうちに adds 'while it hasn't yet happened, take the chance'.

meanings: honorific prefixes お / ご
explanation: お and ご are polite prefixes placed on the front of nouns (and some adjectives) to make speech sound more refined or to show respect toward the listener or the thing's owner. As a rough rule, お joins native Japanese words (お金, お花) and ご joins words of Chinese origin (ご家族, ご住所). Some very common Chinese-origin words take お anyway by convention (お茶, お電話), so treat this as a starting guideline, not a strict rule.

related.note: お＋stem＋する is a humble verb pattern that reuses the same お prefix.
お＋stem＋ください makes a polite request using the same お prefix.
ございます is the polite existence verb often paired with お/ご speech.

meanings: not only ~ but even ~
explanation: 〜ばかりか means 'not only ~ but even ~' — it states one thing and then adds a second, usually more extreme or surprising, that goes beyond it. 手伝ってくれないばかりか、邪魔までした = not only did he not help, he even got in the way. The added part often takes も or さえ. It attaches to nouns and plain-form clauses.

synonyms.note: だけでなく 'not only ~ but also' is neutral; ばかりか adds a stronger, often surprising second point.
のみならず is the formal 'not only ~ but also'; ばかりか highlights an escalating, often unexpected addition.
どころか 'far from ~, on the contrary'; ばかりか adds to the first fact, while どころか overturns it.

related.note: さえ 'even'; ばかりか frequently pairs with も／さえ in the added clause to mark the extra element.

variants.explanation: 〜ばかりか means 'not only ~ but even ~' — it states one thing and then adds a second, usually more extreme or surprising, that goes beyond it. 手伝ってくれないばかりか、邪魔までした = not only did he not help, he even got in the way. The added part often takes も or さえ. It attaches to nouns and plain-form clauses.

synonyms.note: だけでなく 'not only ~ but also' is neutral; ばかりか adds a stronger, often surprising second point.

meanings: before ~ happens; while ~ has not yet occurred
explanation: Verb［ない form］＋ うちに means 'do something before an (often unwelcome) change sets in' — 暗くならないうちに帰ろう = let's head home before it gets dark; 忘れないうちにメモする = jot it down before I forget. You act during the window while the change has not yet happened, usually to get ahead of it.

related.note: plain うちに is 'while a state still holds'; ないうちに is 'before that state changes / before it happens'.
前に simply marks 'before' an event; ないうちに adds the sense of a limited window before an unwanted change.

meanings: especially; above all; in particular
explanation: とりわけ singles out one item as exceptional among a group that already shares some quality — 'above all, in particular'. 今年の夏はとりわけ暑い = this summer is especially hot. It is a touch more emphatic and formal than 特に, and can attach to a whole clause or directly qualify an adjective. Use it to pull one case out of many as standing head and shoulders above the rest.

meanings: do things like A and B
structure: Verb［た form］＋ り ＋ Verb［た form］＋ り ＋ する

surface: では・それでは・じゃあ
reading: では・それでは・じゃあ
meanings: well then; in that case; all right then
structure: では／それでは／じゃあ ＋ Sentence
explanation: では, それでは, and the casual じゃあ open a new move in a conversation — wrapping something up, starting off, or drawing a conclusion from what came before. 'Well then / in that case / all right then.' では is more formal; じゃあ (and じゃ) is casual.

related.note: それで means 'and so, because of that,' giving a result; それでは means 'well then,' shifting to the next move.
なら attaches to a clause as 'if that's the case'; それでは stands alone as 'well then, in that case.'

surface: ではあるまいし・じゃあるまいし
reading: ではあるまいし・じゃあるまいし
meanings: it's not as if ~; ~ is not the case, so (you should…)
structure: Noun＋ではあるまいし／じゃあるまいし
Verb［plain form］＋のではあるまいし
explanation: 〜ではあるまいし dismisses a scenario as clearly untrue and uses that to justify a criticism, complaint, or piece of advice in the following clause. 子供じゃあるまいし、それくらい自分でやりなさい = you're not a child, so do that much yourself. あるまい gives 'surely it isn't ~', and し adds 'and so…'. The じゃあるまいし form is conversational, and the tone is often reproachful or exasperated.

related.note: まい supplies the negative conjecture あるまい ('surely not ~'); ではあるまいし turns that into grounds for the criticism that follows.

meanings: go on, try doing; (please) look
explanation: 〜てごらん is a soft, encouraging way to tell someone to try doing something — warmer than a plain command, and typically used by adults toward children or by a senior toward a junior. It comes from ご覧なさい (look/see). 食べてごらん = go on, try eating it.

synonyms.note: てみる is the neutral 'try doing'; てごらん turns it into a gentle 'go ahead and try' command.

related.note: なさい is a firm command; てごらん is softer and more encouraging.
てください is a polite request usable with anyone; てごらん is casual and aimed at juniors or children.

surface: とおなじで・とちがって
reading: とおなじで・とちがって
meanings: like, the same as (と同じで); unlike, different from (と違って)
explanation: This pair sets up a comparison as the background to a statement. Noun ＋ と同じで means 'just like ~, (so) ...' — 兄と同じで、私も甘いものが好きだ = like my brother, I love sweets too. Noun ＋ と違って means 'unlike ~, ...' — 去年と違って、今年は涼しい = unlike last year, this year is cool. The first half names what you compare with; the main point comes after.

synonyms.note: と同じくらい measures two things as roughly equal in degree; と同じで just flags a likeness to lead into a point.

related.note: に比べて frames an explicit contrast of amounts; と違って simply says 'not like ~' as a setup for the main clause.

meanings: is both ~ and ~; is at once ~ and ~
explanation: 〜でもあり〜でもある presents two qualities or roles that hold at the same time — X is both A and B. 彼は研究者でもあり、教育者でもある = he is both a researcher and an educator. meanings: not even a little; not at all

meanings: ~ of course, and also ~; not to mention ~; not only ~ but also ~
structure: Noun＋ はもちろん（のこと）、〜も
explanation: はもちろん presents X as the obvious, taken-for-granted case and then adds a further, more noteworthy item Y, usually marked with も — 'X goes without saying, and Y as well.' It attaches to a noun and often appears as はもちろんのこと. The point being added after it is the one that carries the real information.

synonyms.note: だけでなく ('not only') is more general and attaches to verbs and clauses; はもちろん takes a noun and frames it as the obvious case.

related.note: はおろか is stronger ('let alone') and usually pairs with a negative or extreme; はもちろん is neutral and simply adds a second item.
もまた marks 'also, too' for one added item; はもちろん frames the first as obvious before adding the notable one.

meanings: just as ~; right when ~ (an event breaks in)
structure: Verb［dictionary／ている／た form］＋ ところに／ところへ
い-adjective ＋ ところに／ところへ
explanation: ところに / ところへ marks the precise moment one situation is unfolding when another event breaks in — 'just as ~ / right when ~'. 出かけようとしたところに電話が来た = 'just as I was about to leave, the phone rang'. The second event typically interrupts or coincides with the first.

related.note: たところ marks the point an action has just finished; ところに／ところへ marks a moment interrupted by another event.

meanings: at most; at best; no more than
structure: せいぜい ＋ Verb（as much as one can）
explanation: せいぜい caps an amount — "at most," "at best," no more than that — often hinting that it's less than you might expect. 集まってもせいぜい十人だろう = at most about ten people. It can also mean "as much as one can" (せいぜい頑張って), which sometimes sounds faintly sarcastic.

antonyms.note: 少なくとも sets a lower limit ("at least this much"); せいぜい sets an upper limit ("at most this much").

related.note: せめて is the minimum you'd wish for ("at least"); せいぜい is the maximum you can expect ("at most").
たったの stresses "only, as few as"; せいぜい caps the count as an upper limit.

meanings: one who is (in the position of) ~ should; befitting one who is ~
explanation: たる is a literary copula (equivalent to である) used attributively. 〜たるもの(は) names someone in a certain role and states how a person in that position ought to behave — 指導者たるもの、模範を示すべきだ = one who is a leader should set an example. It is formal and written, and the following clause typically expresses duty or expectation. たる can also directly modify a noun (堂々たる態度).

synonyms.note: ともあろうものが reproaches someone in a high position for a lapse; たるもの prescribes how such a person should act.
として states a role or capacity neutrally ('as a ~'); たるもの is formal and adds the weight of expected conduct.

meanings: must do; have to do
structure: Verb［ない form］ ＋ ［ない → なければいけない］
い-adjective ＋ ［くない → くなければいけない］
Noun／な-adjective ＋ でなければいけない
explanation: なければいけない expresses obligation — 'must do' or 'have to do'. Take the ない form, drop ない, and add なければいけない: 行かない → 行かなければいけない. Literally it says 'if you don't do it, it won't do', so it points to a specific duty the speaker feels bound to. In speech it is often shortened to なきゃ.

synonyms.note: なければならない is nearly identical; it feels a touch more formal and written.
なくてはいけない says the same 'must' with the なくては shape instead of なければ.
ないといけない is a more conversational way to say the same obligation.

antonyms.note: なくてもいい is the flip side: 'you don't have to do it'.

related.note: なくちゃ・なきゃ are the casual spoken contractions of this obligation pattern.

meanings: to think that ~!; the very idea that ~
explanation: In its emotive use, 〜とは reacts with surprise, shock, admiration, or dismay to a fact — 'to think that ~!'. まさか彼が犯人だったとは = to think he was the culprit. The sentence often trails off after とは, leaving the reaction (驚いた, 情けない...) unspoken. It is a little more formal or written than the colloquial なんて. Separately, とは also serves as a defining marker ('X とは Y' = X means Y).

synonyms.note: なんて is the colloquial 'to think that ~!'; とは carries a slightly more formal, written tone.

related.note: ことか exclaims over a degree ('how very ~!'); とは reacts with surprise that a fact is even the case.

meanings: to do ~ (honorific)
structure: ご ＋ Noun［する-verb］ ＋ になる
explanation: お＋verb stem＋になる is the general honorific (sonkeigo) pattern for a respected person's action. お帰りになる = (they) go home; お書きになる = (they) write. It raises the subject, so you use it about a customer, boss or teacher — not about yourself.

antonyms.note: お～する humbly lowers your own action; お～になる honorifically raises someone else's.

related.note: いらっしゃる is a ready-made honorific verb; お～になる turns ordinary verbs honorific.
お～ください requests an action; お～になる simply describes a respected person doing it.

meanings: a little more than; just over (suffix on a quantity)
explanation: Placed right after a number or amount, 〜強 means 'a bit more than that figure'. It rounds down to a round number and signals that the true value sits slightly above it — 二年強 = just over two years, 五割強 = a little over 50%. Common in statistics, reports, and news.

antonyms.note: 〜弱 is the mirror suffix, marking a value slightly below the stated figure.

related.note: 以上 means 'that amount or more' inclusively; 〜強 means a bit above a rounded-down figure.

meanings: setting ~ aside; regardless of ~; never mind ~, the point is
structure: Noun ＋ はともかく（として）
Sentence ＋ か ＋ はともかく（として）
explanation: 〜はともかく sets a topic aside as not the point right now, shifting the focus to what follows — 'never mind X, the real issue is Y'. Often 〜はともかく(として). X is downplayed as secondary here, not dismissed as unimportant in general.

related.note: を問わず means 'regardless of any value of X'; はともかく sets one specific X aside to focus on Y.

meanings: though there may be ~; there is ~, but
explanation: 〜こそあれ concedes that A does exist or is the case, then goes on to a contrasting statement that discounts its importance — 'there may indeed be A, but ~'. 多少の違いこそあれ、本質は同じだ = there may be slight differences, but the essence is the same. It attaches to a noun (a な-adjective takes で before it) and uses the classical あれ. The tone is formal and literary, and the following clause often negates or minimizes.

synonyms.note: こそすれ builds on a verb ('may well ~, but certainly not ...'); こそあれ builds on a noun ('there may be ~, but ...').
とはいえ concedes a whole statement then qualifies it; こそあれ concedes the existence of a specific thing then downplays it.

related.note: 〜こそ〜が concedes a point then contrasts it with a heavier main claim; こそあれ concedes existence then minimizes its weight.

meanings: for example
explanation: 例えば introduces a concrete example of a general statement, usually followed by a pause. After stating something broad, you use 例えば to name a specific case that illustrates it. It often teams up with listing words like 〜や, 〜とか, or 〜など.

related.note: など follows the examples that 例えば introduces.
〜とか lists casual examples; 例えば announces that one is coming.

meanings: to notice; to realize
structure: Sentence［plain form］ ＋ こと ＋ に気がつく
explanation: に気がつく means to notice or realize something. The thing you become aware of is marked with に: 間違いに気がつく = to notice a mistake. To realize a whole fact, nominalize the clause with こと first: 〜ことに気がつく. It describes the moment awareness dawns, often something you hadn't been conscious of before.

related.note: The に here is the target-marking particle; it points at what you become aware of.

meanings: as a result (of that)
explanation: その結果 opens a sentence to present the outcome that the previous sentence led to — "as a result." It frames what happened as the natural consequence of what came before, and is common in explanations and reports.

related.note: 結果 is the noun 'result' used within a clause; その結果 is the fixed connector 'as a result' that opens a sentence.
そこで introduces a deliberate response; その結果 introduces an outcome that followed automatically.
そのため(に) points to a cause; その結果 points to the effect that came out of it.

meanings: hard to do (often uncomfortable or a strain for the doer)
explanation: 〜づらい attaches to the ます-stem and means an action is hard or uncomfortable to do — often because doing it puts some strain or awkwardness on the speaker. 言いづらい = hard to bring myself to say; 歩きづらい = hard to walk. The compound behaves like an い-adjective (づらかった, づらくない).

synonyms.note: 〜にくい is the neutral 'hard to'; 〜づらい adds that the difficulty is uncomfortable for the doer.
〜がたい is stronger — 'nearly impossible to' — and more formal or literary.

antonyms.note: 〜やすい means easy or comfortable to do — the opposite of 〜づらい.

meanings: cannot rule out that ~; it's not impossible that ~ might happen
structure: Verb［ない form］＋とも限らない
explanation: 〜ないとも限らない stacks two negatives (a negated predicate plus 〜とも限らない, 'it is not limited to') to make a cautious positive: 'one cannot say for certain that ~ won't happen', i.e. 'there is a chance it might'. 事故が起きないとも限らない = we can't rule out that an accident might occur. It typically raises the possibility of an undesirable outcome as a reason to stay careful, and belongs to formal or written registers.

synonyms.note: とは限らない plainly denies that something is always true; ないとも限らない adds a layer of negation to warn that the unwanted case might still occur.

related.note: ないでもない grudgingly admits 'it's kind of the case'; ないとも限らない instead flags a lingering possibility as a caution.

meanings: rarely; hardly ever (paired with a negative)
explanation: めったに is an adverb that teams up with a negative ending to say something almost never happens — めったに怒らない = hardly ever gets angry. The negative ない／ません is obligatory; めったに carries the 'rarely' meaning only when it points at a negative predicate.

synonyms.note: あまり〜ない is 'not very often'; めったに〜ない is much stronger — nearly never.

related.note: なかなか〜ない is 'not easily / not for a while'; めったに〜ない is about low frequency.
決して〜ない is an absolute 'never (I promise)'; めったに〜ない leaves room for rare exceptions.

meanings: to be made from (a raw material)
structure: Noun［material］＋ から ＋ 作る／作られる
explanation: Noun＋から作る／作られる describes making something out of a raw material that changes form in the process, so the original is no longer obvious in the product. 米から作る = made from rice. The passive 〜から作られる ('is made from') is common when stating what something is produced out of.

synonyms.note: でできる・からできる also says 'is made from', using intransitive できる rather than 作る.

related.note: This is から's 'starting point' sense applied to the material a thing comes from.

meanings: precisely because ~; it is only because ~
explanation: 〜ばこそ gives the true, emphatic reason behind a result — 'it is precisely because ~ that…'. 君を思えばこそ = it is precisely because I care about you. It attaches to the ば-conditional form (であればこそ after a noun or な-adjective), and the reason is usually a positive or heartfelt one. This is formal, somewhat literary Japanese, more elevated than からこそ.

synonyms.note: からこそ is the everyday emphatic 'precisely because'; ばこそ is more formal and literary.
こそ alone emphasizes a noun ('this very ~'); ばこそ emphasizes a reason clause ('precisely because ~').

meanings: regarding; concerning; about ~ (formal)
explanation: に関して marks the topic something concerns — 'regarding / about ~' — in a formal or written register. その事件に関して調べる ('investigate regarding that incident'). Before a noun, use に関する — 環境に関する本 ('a book about the environment').

synonyms.note: について is the everyday 'about ~'; に関して is the more formal equivalent.

related.note: に対して aims an action or feeling at a target ('toward'); に関して marks the topic.

meanings: that kind of; like that
explanation: そういう before a noun means 'that kind of ~', pointing at a type that has just come up in the conversation: そういう話 = 'a story like that'. It belongs to the こういう・そういう・ああいう・どういう family of kind-pointing words.

meanings: the fact that ~; that ~ (nominalizer)
explanation: ということ turns a whole sentence into a noun meaning 'the fact/matter that ~'. It lets a full statement work as the subject or object of another clause — handy for talking about information, meaning, or what was said.

synonyms.note: plain こと nominalizes an action; ということ wraps a whole statement or fact.

related.note: の also turns a clause into a noun, but for concrete events rather than reported statements.
〜ということだ ends a sentence with 'it means that' or reported 'I hear that'.

meanings: regardless of; irrespective of
explanation: を問わず attaches to a noun to say something applies without regard to that factor — 'regardless of, irrespective of'. It typically follows a noun naming a variable (年齢, 経験) or a pair of opposites (男女, 昼夜), and the statement then holds true across all of them. It is formal in tone.

synonyms.note: にかかわらず also means 'regardless of' but attaches more freely, including to plain forms and か-questions.
いかんにかかわらず means 'regardless of what X is'; it is more formal and rigid than を問わず.

meanings: cannot help feeling; unable to restrain
might; may; perhaps
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋ かもしれない
explanation: かもしれない marks something as a real possibility — 'might' or 'perhaps'. It attaches to the plain form of verbs and い-adjectives, and to nouns and な-adjectives with no だ. The polite version is かもしれません. It signals genuine uncertainty, weaker than a confident guess.

related.note: だろう is a fairly confident guess; かもしれない admits it could easily be otherwise.
はずだ says you expect it on solid grounds; かもしれない is only a loose possibility.
かな just wonders out loud; かもしれない actually puts a possibility on the table.

meanings: when; on the occasion of; at the time of
explanation: 際に is a formal 'when' for notable occasions or special situations — applying for something, visiting on business, a ceremony. You meet it often in written notices and polite speech; in everyday conversation とき does the same job more plainly.

related.note: とき is the neutral, everyday 'when'; 際に is its formal counterpart for notable occasions.
最中に means 'right in the middle of an ongoing action'; 際に marks the occasion or moment when you do something.

meanings: on top of that; what's more; to make matters worse
explanation: おまけに is a conjunction that adds a further point piling onto what was just said — usually in the same direction, so a second bad thing on top of a bad one (or a second good thing on top of a good one). It often carries the flavor 'and to make matters worse'. It links whole statements, not nouns.

synonyms.note: その上 also means 'on top of that'; おまけに is more colloquial and often tinged with 'to make things worse'.
しかも is a more formal 'moreover'; おまけに sounds casual and everyday.

related.note: さらに adds and intensifies ('furthermore, even more'); おまけに simply tacks on an extra circumstance.

meanings: probably; ~right?
explanation: Expresses a guess or conjecture in plain speech: だろう means "probably" or, with rising intonation, "~right?" when seeking agreement. Attach it to a plain-form verb, an い-adjective, or a noun. でしょう is its polite twin.

synonyms.note: でしょう is the polite version of the same conjecture; だろう is plain.

related.note: かもしれない ("maybe") is less certain than だろう ("probably").
はずだ expects something based on reasoning; だろう is a looser guess.

variants.explanation: Expresses a guess or conjecture in plain speech: だろう means "probably" or, with rising intonation, "~right?" when seeking agreement. Attach it to a plain-form verb, an い-adjective, or a noun. でしょう is its polite twin.

synonyms.note: でしょう is the polite version of the same conjecture; だろう is plain.

related.note: かもしれない ("maybe") is less certain than だろう ("probably").
はずだ expects something based on reasoning; だろう is a looser guess.

meanings: the whole ~; -wide; everyone/everything included
explanation: 〜ぐるみ is a suffix meaning 'the whole ~ together, involving everyone in it'. It attaches to a limited set of nouns: 家族ぐるみ (the whole family), 会社ぐるみ (company-wide), 町ぐるみ (the whole town), 地域ぐるみ, and 身ぐるみ (everything one owns). The image is of the named group acting or being involved as a single unit, with no member left out.

surface: てもしょうがない・てもしかたがない
reading: てもしょうがない・てもしかたがない
meanings: there's no use ~ing; no point even if you ~
structure: Verb［て form］＋ もしょうがない／もしかたがない
explanation: 〜てもしょうがない (also てもしかたがない) says that even if you do X, it won't help — expressing resignation or futility. 悔やんでもしょうがない = there's no use regretting it. The も is essential: it frames X as a pointless action.

synonyms.note: ても始まらない stresses that the action produces no progress; てもしょうがない stresses that it simply can't be helped.

related.note: Without も, てしょうがない means 'can't help feeling / extremely', not futility — an easy pair to confuse.

surface: をぜんていとして・をぜんていに
reading: をぜんていとして・をぜんていに
meanings: on the premise/assumption of
structure: Noun＋を前提として／を前提に
explanation: 〜を前提として / 〜を前提に marks something as a precondition assumed to hold before proceeding: 結婚を前提に付き合う = date with marriage as the premise; 予算の確保を前提とする = premised on securing the budget. A clause is nominalized with こと first (〜ことを前提に). It is formal, common in planning, agreements, and business, and states an assumed basis rather than a mere hope.

synonyms.note: を踏まえて builds on facts already established; を前提に assumes a condition as given before moving ahead.

related.note: をもとに uses X as source material for making something; を前提に treats X as a condition assumed to hold.

meanings: volitional form: let's ~ / I'll ~ (plain)
structure: Verb［u-verb：〜う → 〜おう］（書く → 書こう）
Verb［ru-verb：〜る → 〜よう］（食べる → 食べよう）
する → しよう ／ 来る → こよう
explanation: The volitional form is the plain 'let's ~' or 'I'll ~' ending — the casual counterpart of ましょう. For う-verbs, change the final -u sound to -ou (行く → 行こう); for る-verbs, drop る and add よう (食べる → 食べよう). It expresses a suggestion to a friend or your own resolve to do something.

synonyms.note: ましょう is the polite version of this same 'let's ~'; the volitional is its plain form.

related.note: ようと思う adds と思う to the volitional to say 'I'm thinking of ~ing'.
つもり states a settled plan; the volitional voices a suggestion or on-the-spot resolve.

meanings: should be; ought to be; supposed to be
structure: Verb ／ い-adjective［plain form］＋ はずだ
explanation: はずだ states a conclusion the speaker expects to be true based on reason or evidence — 'it should be the case that ~'. It reflects what logically follows from what you know, not a personal wish. It attaches to plain forms, with な-adjective＋な and noun＋の.

antonyms.note: はずがない denies the expectation ('no way'); はずだ affirms it ('should be').

related.note: だろう is a looser 'probably'; はずだ rests on concrete grounds for the expectation.
ようだ reports how something seems from direct evidence; はずだ reasons out what ought to be true.

meanings: could you please ~? (very polite request)
structure: Verb［て form］＋ いただけませんか
explanation: A very polite, softened way to ask someone to do something for you. It is built on the humble いただく (to receive) in its negative-potential-question shape, literally 'couldn't I receive the favor of your ~ing?' — which lands as a respectful 'could you please ~?'. Reach for it with superiors, customers, and strangers.

synonyms.note: ～てもらえない／～てくれない are the plain, casual versions of this same request.

related.note: ていただく is the humble equivalent of てもらう (receiving the favor of an action).
てください is a plainer, more direct 'please do'; ていただけませんか is far more deferential.

meanings: having said that; that said; nevertheless
explanation: とはいうものの concedes what was just stated and then presents a reality that runs against the expectation it creates — 'having said that, ...'. 春とはいうものの、まだ寒い = it may be spring, but it's still cold. It can join clauses within a sentence or open a new one after a full stop. The contrast clause describes an actual situation, not a hypothetical one.

synonyms.note: とはいえ carries the same 'that said' meaning in a more compact, formal shape.
ものの joins a concession and its counter within one sentence ('although'); とはいうものの more often stands as its own connective clause.

related.note: と言っても downplays or qualifies a preceding claim; とはいうものの fully concedes it, then contrasts.

meanings: if only ~; as long as (just) ~
explanation: さえ〜ば names the one and only condition needed for a result — 'just do X, and that's all it takes.' A noun takes さえ plus a ば-clause (お金さえあれば), while a verb becomes stem + さえすれば (押しさえすれば). It says nothing else is required.

related.note: ば states a general condition; さえ〜ば narrows it to the single sufficient one.
だけで means 'just with / just by' doing something; さえ〜ば frames that one thing as the only condition needed.
Plain さえ highlights an extreme example ('even'); さえ〜ば turns さえ into a sole-condition pattern.

meanings: than; compared to
structure: A ＋ は ＋ B ＋ より ＋ adjective
explanation: より marks the standard you compare against — the 'than X' in a comparison. It attaches right after the noun used as the yardstick: 去年より暑い = 'hotter than last year'. The thing that comes out higher is usually marked with は or のほうが.

related.note: より〜のほうが is the fuller 'B is more ~ than A' frame built on this より.
一番 picks the single best of three or more; より compares just two things.
の中で names the group; pair it with 一番, not より, for the outright top.

meanings: while doing ~; even though ~ (concessive つつも)
explanation: つつ attaches to the ます-stem and has two uses. Plain つつ means 'while doing ~', marking two actions the same person does at once (a formal, written equivalent of ながら). つつも adds a concessive twist — 'even though / despite ~' — where the two clauses clash, as in 悪いと知りつつも = 'even though I know it's wrong'. Both belong to a literary, formal register.

synonyms.note: ながら is the everyday word for doing two things at once; つつ is its formal, written counterpart.
ながらも matches the concessive つつも ('even though'); ながらも is somewhat less literary.

related.note: つつある uses the same つつ but means 'in the process of ~', describing gradual change, not two simultaneous actions.

meanings: and; what's more (listing reasons)
explanation: し links clauses that each give a reason or supporting point, with the feeling that the list could go on: 安いし、おいしいし = 'it's cheap, it's tasty (and more besides)'. Attach it to the plain form; nouns and な-adjectives take だし.

related.note: から gives one explicit reason; し piles up several and implies there are more.
それに adds a further point as a separate sentence; し chains reasons inside one.
The て form lists actions neutrally, without the 'reasons, and more' flavor of し.

meanings: only ~ and nothing else (with a negative slant) ~
explanation: 〜ばかりで presents a situation as nothing but one thing, usually with a critical or dissatisfied tone about what is missing — 文句を言うばかりで、何もしない = he only complains and doesn't do anything. The ばかり limits it to that single thing, and で leads into the resulting lack or problem.

related.note: 〜ばかりだ marks a one-way change; 〜ばかりで sets up 'only this' before pointing out what's missing.
〜ばかりでなく adds 'not only… but also…'; 〜ばかりで complains that there is only the one thing.
〜だけ neutrally limits things to 'only'; ばかりで adds a critical 'nothing but this' tone.

meanings: in one go; all at once; in one breath
explanation: 一気に says an action is carried out in a single continuous burst, without pausing along the way — 一気に飲む = drink in one gulp, 一気に読む = read straight through. It stresses momentum and the absence of any interruption, often conveying vigor or a sudden surge. Use it when something is done from start to finish in one unbroken stretch.

synonyms.note: 一度に stresses simultaneity ('all at the same time'); 一気に stresses momentum with no pause.

meanings: no more than; merely; just
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋ に過ぎない
explanation: に過ぎない downplays something as being nothing more than what precedes it — ただの噂に過ぎない ('it's nothing but a rumor'). It minimizes the scale or importance of the thing, often to push back against an overestimation.

synonyms.note: のみ is a formal 'only' limiting quantity; に過ぎない adds the judgment that it's unimportantly small.
だけ neutrally marks 'only'; に過ぎない spins that 'only' as a dismissive 'merely, nothing more'.

related.note: にほかならない emphatically insists something is precisely X; に過ぎない dismisses it as no more than X.

related.note: でも starts a new sentence; けど joins two clauses within one sentence.

meanings: in terms of ~; the respect/point that ~

explanation: 〜点 uses 点 as an abstract 'point/respect' to name the angle from which something is judged — usually as 〜という点で ('in the respect that') or 〜点で(は) ('in terms of'). 値段が安いという点で = in terms of being cheap. It pins down which aspect you're evaluating.

related.note: という labels or names a clause; 〜という点で uses it to single out the specific aspect under discussion.

meanings: half-done; not yet finished; on the point of ~ing
explanation: 〜かける attaches to the ます-stem to mean an action is only half carried out or is just about to happen — 言いかける = start to say, 倒れかける = be on the verge of falling. The noun form 〜かけ describes a left-unfinished thing — 食べかけ = half-eaten, 読みかけ = half-read. Either way, the action is not seen through to the end.

antonyms.note: 〜終わる is an action carried all the way to the finish; 〜かけ・かける is one left half-done.

related.note: 〜切る is doing something thoroughly to the very end; 〜かける is stopping partway or only starting.
〜途中で marks being partway through on the way somewhere; 〜かけ marks a thing itself left half-finished.

meanings: must ~; have to ~ (unless you do, it won't do)
structure: Verb［ない form］＋ と ＋ （いけない／だめ）［often dropped］
explanation: 〜ないと states an obligation by leaving a conditional hanging: literally 'if you don't ~, (it won't do)'. The consequence いけない／だめ is usually left unsaid, so 〜ないと by itself means 'I have to ~' or 'you must ~'.

related.note: 〜なければならない is the formal, written way to say the same obligation.

explanation: 〜のだろうか expresses a thoughtful, often inward-directed 'I wonder...' — the speaker turning a question over in their own mind rather than asking someone. 本当にこれでいいのだろうか = I wonder if this is really okay. The の gives it a searching, reflective tone; だろうか is the musing question.

meanings: without doing ~
explanation: Links two actions where the first one does not happen: attach で to the ない form of a verb to say "do B without doing A". The clause before ないで names the action that is skipped, and the verb after it carries the sentence. Reach for it when you want to describe doing one thing while leaving another undone.

related.note: Add でください to ないで to turn it into a polite request not to do something.
なくて also links a negative clause but usually states a cause or reason rather than an accompanying non-action.

meanings: so ~ that words fail; incredibly ~
explanation: 〜のなんのって is a very colloquial way to exaggerate a degree — 寒いのなんのって = it was so unbelievably cold, words can't capture it. This belongs to casual, spoken Japanese and carries a lively, emphatic tone.

meanings: to do (humble form of する)
structure: ご ＋ Noun［する-verb］ ＋ いたす
explanation: いたす is the humble (kenjougo) verb for する. You use it to lower your own actions before someone you are being polite to, usually as いたします: 私がいたします = I'll do it. It also builds the humble お＋stem＋いたす pattern (お送りいたします), which is a notch more formal than お～する.

synonyms.note: お～する is the general humble pattern; いたす is the humble する itself, and お～いたす is its more formal version.

related.note: いらっしゃる is honorific (raises the listener); いたす is humble (lowers yourself).

meanings: or; alternatively (formal)
explanation: もしくは is a formal conjunction presenting alternatives — 'A or B'. It links nouns or clauses in written and official contexts: 郵送もしくはメールで = by post or by email. It is more formal than the everyday または, and in careful legal or technical writing the two are sometimes used at different levels (または for the larger split, もしくは for a sub-choice within one side). In ordinary speech, plain か or または is more natural.

synonyms.note: または is the standard 'or' for alternatives; もしくは is more formal and, in strict legal writing, marks a lower-level sub-choice.

meanings: in order to; for the sake of (literary)
structure: Verb［ない form, drop ない］＋んがために
Verb［ない form, drop ない］＋んがための＋Noun
explanation: 〜んがために is a literary equivalent of ために that expresses a strong, deliberate purpose — 'in order to ~'. It attaches to the same base as a verb's ない-form: 勝たんがために (in order to win), 生き延びんがために (in order to survive). The subject actively wants the goal, so the following clause states what was done to reach it. Modifying a noun it becomes んがための. This is bookish, formal language; ordinary speech uses ために.

synonyms.note: べく is likewise a literary 'in order to'; んがために foregrounds the subject's strong desire for the goal, while べく reads more as a stated objective.
ため(に) is the everyday 'in order to'; んがために is its bookish, emphatic counterpart.

meanings: only at/when (a notable stage); and at the same time; being both ~ and ~
explanation: 〜にして is a formal, literary connector with two main senses. One marks a notable stage or degree — 五十歳にして = at (the age of) fifty, 今にして思えば = now that I look back. The other joins two qualities in one subject — 学者にして詩人 = a scholar and at the same time a poet. In both, にして links a noun to what is remarkable about that point or pairing. Context tells the senses apart.

related.note: にしては means 'for ~, considering ~' and judges against a standard; the bare にして marks a notable stage or a pairing of qualities.
こそ singles out and emphasizes a word; にして in its 'only at ~' sense likewise highlights a stage as pivotal, but formally and with a noun.

meanings: to finish doing something completely; to carry an action through to completion
explanation: 〜上げる and 〜上がる attach to the ます-stem to say an action is carried all the way to completion, often producing a finished result — 書き上げる = finish writing, 作り上げる = build/complete, 出来上がる = be finished. 〜上げる is transitive (you complete it); 〜上がる is intransitive (it comes to be finished). This is a compound suffix, unrelated to the N5 verb あげる 'to give'.

antonyms.note: 〜かけ・かける is an action left half-done; 〜上げる・上がる is one carried through to a finished result.

related.note: 〜終わる neutrally marks finishing an action; 〜上げる adds the sense of completing it into a finished product.
〜切る stresses doing something thoroughly to the very end; 〜上げる stresses arriving at a completed result.

meanings: to leave (a matter) up to; to entrust (something) to (someone)
explanation: 任せる assigns responsibility for something to another person or faculty: the thing entrusted is marked with を and the person or thing you leave it to with に. 仕事を彼に任せる = leave the work to him, 判断を現場に任せる = leave the decision to the people on site. meanings: even ~; even if ~ (literary)
explanation: 〜とて is a literary particle with two related senses. After a noun it means 'even ~', singling out a case you might think exempt: 子供とて許されない = even a child is not excused. After a verb it means 'even if / even though', usually with a futile or negative outcome: 悔やんだとて、もう遅い = even if you regret it, it's too late now. It belongs to formal or written Japanese; in speech でも or ても does the same work.

synonyms.note: ても is the everyday 'even if / even though'; とて is its literary, formal-writing equivalent.

related.note: であれ・であろうと concedes across alternatives ('whatever it be'); とて concedes a single case as 'even ~ / even if ~'.
たって is the casual spoken 'even if'; とて sits at the opposite, literary end of the register scale.

structure: 疑問詞（どこ・だれ・何…）＋ … ＋ か ＋ Verb
explanation: A question word (どこ・だれ・何・いつ・どう…) plus か wraps a wh-question into a noun-like clause that a larger sentence can act on: どこに行くか分からない = I don't know where to go. The main verb (know, ask, decide, tell…) then works on that embedded question. It's the wh-question partner of かどうか.

related.note: かどうか embeds a yes/no question; 疑問詞＋か embeds a which/where/who one.
だれか・どこか use the same 疑問詞＋か shape to make indefinites (someone, somewhere).

meanings: there is a risk/danger that (something undesirable may happen)
structure: Noun ＋ の ＋ 恐れがある
explanation: 恐れがある follows a verb (dictionary form) or a noun + の and warns that there is a real risk of an undesirable outcome. It is formal and largely written — common in news reports, warnings, and forecasts. 恐れ literally means 'fear', so it points to something one would rather avoid.

synonyms.note: かねない also flags a possible bad outcome but attaches to a verb stem and is less formal; 恐れがある reads as an objective warning.

related.note: かもしれない is a neutral 'might', for good or bad; 恐れがある specifically warns of an undesirable risk.

meanings: before even ~; more basic than the question of ~
explanation: Beyond its plain sense of 'before (a time)', 〜以前 (often 〜以前の問題) marks that something is too basic to even reach the stated issue — 'before we even get to ~'. マナー以前の問題だ = it's a problem that comes before manners even enter into it; 好き嫌い以前に = before it's even a matter of liking or not. meanings: not at all; not in the least

surface: をもって・をもちまして
reading: をもって・をもちまして
meanings: with; by means of; as of (a set time or point)
structure: Noun［point in time］＋をもって／をもちまして
explanation: 〜をもって attaches to a noun in two formal senses. As 'by means of / with' it names the means, standard, or quality through which something is done — 誠意をもって対応する (deal with it in good faith), 書面をもって通知する (notify in writing). As 'as of / effective from' it marks a fixed point that draws a line — 本日をもって (as of today), 五時をもって (as of five o'clock) — after which a state ends or begins. をもちまして is the politer form heard in announcements and ceremonies. Both belong to written and formal spoken register, not casual で.

synonyms.note: にて is a formal で for means or place; をもって in its 'by means of' sense is even more formal and often names a quality or standard.

related.note: を限りに also sets a final cut-off point in time, but stresses that something ends there; をもって can mark either an ending or a starting boundary.

meanings: even if; granted that; whether ~ or ~
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋ にせよ／にしろ
explanation: にせよ (and its variant にしろ) concedes a case — 'even if; granted that' — then states something that holds regardless. どんな理由があるにせよ暴力は許されない ('whatever the reason, violence is not allowed'). にせよ is the formal, written form; paired as AにせよBにせよ it means 'whether A or B'.

synonyms.note: にしろ〜にしろ pairs two cases; にせよ is the same word and can stand alone as 'even if / granted that'.
としても is the everyday 'even if / even supposing'; にせよ is its more formal, written-style counterpart.

related.note: いずれにせよ concludes 'in any case, either way'; にせよ concedes a single case ('even if it's X').

surface: というものではない・というものでもない
reading: というものではない・というものでもない
meanings: it's not necessarily the case that; it's not as simple as
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋ というものではない
Sentence［plain form］＋ というものでもない
explanation: というものではない denies that something is absolutely or universally true — 'it's not necessarily the case that ~ / it's not as simple as ~'. It pushes back on an over-generalized assumption, often that doing X automatically brings a good result: お金があれば幸せというものではない. The でもない variant is a slightly softer 'nor is it that'.

synonyms.note: とは限らない also means 'not necessarily so'; というものではない specifically rejects an 'if X, then always Y' generalization.
必ずしも is the adverb 'not always' that pairs with a negative; というものではない is the full clause-ending pattern expressing it.

antonyms.note: というものだ asserts strongly that something truly is a certain way; というものではない denies it holds absolutely.

related.note: というわけではない softly denies a specific inferred conclusion; というものではない denies a general rule.

meanings: when it comes to ~ (with exasperation); as for ~
explanation: 〜ときたら singles out a topic — usually a person or thing close to the speaker — and leads into a complaint or exasperated remark about it. うちの息子ときたら = as for my son (honestly...), この天気ときたら = this weather, of all things. It sets up the topic with a fed-up, critical attitude, so the following comment is typically negative. It is colloquial and emotive.

synonyms.note: とは reacts with surprise or evaluation to a fact ('to think that ~'); ときたら fixes a familiar topic and grumbles about it.

related.note: ときている piles on an extra clinching reason; ときたら opens a topic to complain about.

meanings: regardless of; irrespective of; not depending on

It often appears in the fixed frame 〜のいかんによらず ('whatever the ~ may be'). This is formal, written Japanese, common in rules, policies, and official statements.

surface: たはずみに・たひょうしに

explanation: 弾み (はずみ) and 拍子 (ひょうし) both mean 'the momentary instant of' an action, after which an unintended, reflexive result follows — 転んだ拍子に手をついた = the moment I fell, I threw out my hand. meanings: doing ~ and ~ over and over (repeated alternating actions)
explanation: Pairing two て-form verbs with は describes a set of actions repeated in alternation — 書いては消し、書いては消し = 'writing and erasing, over and over'. The two verbs are usually opposite or complementary, and the pattern paints a vivid picture of the same cycle happening again and again.

meanings: to force (a situation); to make (something) unavoidable
explanation: 〜を余儀なくさせる is the causative side of this pair: an impersonal cause — a circumstance, event, or condition — is the subject and forces some outcome to happen. The forced outcome is a noun of action (中止, 撤退, 変更) marked with を, and the person pushed into it takes に. 不況が事業の縮小を余儀なくさせた = the recession forced a scaling-back of the business. It is stiff, written register typical of news and reports.

related.note: The passive counterpart: 〜を余儀なくされる puts the forced person in the subject slot, while 〜を余儀なくさせる puts the cause there.

meanings: cannot bring oneself to; too painful (out of pity or attachment) to ~
explanation: 〜に忍びない expresses that one cannot bring oneself to do something because it is too heartbreaking or pitiful — 'cannot bear to ~'. 捨てるに忍びない = can't bear to throw away, 見るに忍びない = too pitiful to watch. surface: かのように・かのようだ
reading: かのように・かのようだ
meanings: as if; as though (when it is actually not so)
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋ かのように／かのようだ
Noun／な-adjective ＋ である ＋ かのように／かのようだ
explanation: [plain form] + かのように / かのようだ compares a situation to something it is not really — 'as if'. It is stronger and more literary than plain ようだ, and stresses that the likeness is contrary to fact. かのように modifies a following verb or clause; かのようだ ends the sentence.

synonyms.note: まるで pairs with ようだ for 'just as if'; かのように carries the same figurative sense but is more literary and does not need まるで.
ようだ states a likeness or inference that may well be true; かのように adds the sense that it is not actually so.

related.note: みたいだ is the casual 'like / as if'; かのように is the formal, written counterpart with a contrary-to-fact nuance.

meanings: isn't it perhaps that ~? ; might it not be the case that ~?
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋のではあるまいか
explanation: 〜ではあるまいか is a formal, literary way to float a tentative supposition — 'might it not be ~? / perhaps it is ~'. あるまい is the classical negative conjecture of ある, so this equals a bookish ではないだろうか. 何か誤解があるのではあるまいか = might there not be some misunderstanding? The speaker advances a guess while leaving room for doubt, in an essayistic or formal register.

synonyms.note: 〜のではないだろうか is the standard 'isn't it that ~?'; ではあるまいか is its formal, literary equivalent built on classical あるまい.
〜ではないか asserts 'isn't it ~!' with some force; ではあるまいか stays tentative and reflective ('perhaps ~?').

related.note: まい is the classical negative conjecture behind あるまい ('surely won't be'); ではあるまいか packages it into a softened supposition.

meanings: nominalizer: turns a verb or clause into a noun
explanation: こと turns a verb or a whole clause into a noun so it can act as a subject or object: 泳ぐこと = swimming, 早く寝ること = going to bed early. The verb stays in plain form right before こと. It's the tool for talking about actions and facts as things — hobbies, what's important, what you like.

synonyms.note: の nominalizes too, but favors concrete, perceived actions; こと favors abstract facts.

related.note: ことができる is this こと plus ができる to express ability.
ことがある builds on this こと to say something happens on occasion.

meanings: to get used to; to grow accustomed to ~
explanation: に慣れる means you have grown accustomed to something through repeated experience, so it no longer feels new or hard. The thing you get used to is marked with に — 新しい仕事に慣れる = get used to a new job. To make an action the target, nominalize it first with の: 早く起きるのに慣れる. The form 慣れている describes the settled state of already being used to something.

related.note: ようになる marks reaching a new ability or habit; に慣れる marks that something no longer feels unfamiliar.

meanings: moreover; what's more; and on top of that
explanation: しかも adds a further point that reinforces the previous one, usually making it more striking — 'and what's more'. 安くて、しかもおいしい = cheap, and on top of that delicious. The added fact points the same direction as the first (both good, or both bad), heightening the effect.

synonyms.note: その上 is a very close 'on top of that'; しかも can feel a touch more emphatic.
〜上に attaches within a clause ('in addition to ~ing'); しかも links whole sentences.
ばかりか is 'not only ~ but even ~', with escalation to a surprising point; しかも simply piles on a reinforcing fact.

meanings: if only ~; it would be ... if (regret, wish) ~
structure: Verb［ば form］／い-adjective ＋ ければ ＋ … のに
explanation: The ば〜のに pattern voices a regret or wish about something that is not the case — もっとお金があれば、旅行できるのに = if only I had more money, I could travel. The ば clause sets an unmet condition, and のに adds the disappointed 'but (it isn't so)' feeling. It is how you say 'if only… / it would be nice, but it isn't'.

related.note: 〜ばよかった regrets a past action you wish you had taken; ば〜のに regrets a present situation that isn't so.
のに on its own means 'even though' between two real facts; ば〜のに colors an unreal condition with regret.
なら supposes a case and gives advice; ば〜のに laments a condition that is not met.

meanings: while; during; the whole time; between
explanation: 間 marks a stretch of time and says the main action continues for that whole stretch. Whatever comes before 間 sets the period (母が寝ている間 = the whole time my mother is asleep), and the main clause holds true throughout it, running in parallel. It also has a spatial 'between' sense, but the everyday N4 use is this 'the whole time that ~' meaning.

related.note: 間に marks a point inside the period where one thing happens; 間 means the action lasts the entire period.
ながら links two actions by one person at once; 間 sets a period during which a separate action continues.
うちに (N3) stresses doing something before a period ends; 間 just spans the whole period.

meanings: must; have to (formal, literary)
structure: Verb［ない-stem］＋ ねばならない
する → せねばならない
explanation: 〜ねばならない is a formal, somewhat literary way to say 'must / have to.' It attaches to the same stem as ない, plus ねばならない (行かねばならない = 行かなければならない), with せねばならない for する. It is the stiff, written counterpart of なければならない, common in editorials, speeches, and formal prose. It can shorten to ねばならぬ or just ねば.

synonyms.note: なければならない is the everyday 'must'; ねばならない is its formal, written equivalent.
なくてはならない also means 'must'; ねばならない is stiffer and more literary.

related.note: ざるを得ない means 'have no choice but to'; ねばならない states an obligation rather than reluctant inevitability.

structure: Godan verb［ない form: ない → せる］
Ichidan verb［ない form: ない → させる］

explanation: せる・させる turns a verb causative: someone causes another person to act, whether by forcing ('make') or by allowing ('let'): 帰らせる = 'make/let someone go home'. The causer is the subject; the person who acts takes に with transitive verbs and usually を with intransitive ones.

surface: ずにはおかない・ないではおかない
reading: ずにはおかない・ないではおかない
meanings: will inevitably cause; will not rest until
structure: Verb［ない stem］＋ずにはおかない
Verb［ない form］＋ではおかない
explanation: 〜ずにはおかない declares that a force will not let things end without the verb happening. With causative or emotive verbs, the subject is often a thing whose power inevitably affects people: 聴く人を感動させずにはおかない = it cannot fail to move listeners. With a personal subject it voices fierce determination: 謝らせずにはおかない = I won't rest until I make him apologize. It is emphatic, formal, and written in flavor; する becomes せずにはおかない.

related.note: ずにはいられない is an internal urge you cannot suppress; ずにはおかない is an outcome the force of things will not fail to produce.
ずには済まない says circumstances oblige you to act; ずにはおかない says the action will inevitably be brought about.

With a personal subject it voices fierce determination: 謝らせずにはおかない = I won't rest until I make him apologize. It is emphatic, formal, and written in flavor; する becomes せずにはおかない.

related.note: ずにはいられない is an internal urge you cannot suppress; ずにはおかない is an outcome the force of things will not fail to produce.

meanings: passive: to be done (to someone or something)
structure: Verb Group 1: ［あ-row stem］＋ れる（読む → 読まれる）
Verb Group 2: ［stem］＋ られる（見る → 見られる）
する → される／来る → 来られる
explanation: The passive れる・られる recasts a sentence so the receiver of an action becomes the subject. Group 1 verbs take the あ-row ＋ れる (読む → 読まれる), Group 2 take られる (食べる → 食べられる). The doer, when mentioned, is marked with に. Japanese often uses the passive to spotlight the affected person, including the 'suffering passive'.

related.note: Group 2 shares the られる shape but means 'can do'; context distinguishes them.
せる・させる is the causative 'make / let do'; the passive is 'be done to'.
てある also centers a result, but from a deliberate action and without naming a passive agent.

meanings: potential: can; be able to
structure: Verb Group 1: ［え-row］＋ る（泳ぐ → 泳げる）
Verb Group 2: ［stem］＋ られる（見る → 見られる）

meanings: can't help but ~; can't keep oneself from ~
structure: Verb［ない form］＋ではいられない
explanation: 〜ないではいられない describes an urge or emotion so strong that you cannot stop yourself from acting on it — 泣かないではいられない = 'I can't help but cry'. The doubled negative (can't-not-do) conveys that the action is spontaneous and beyond the speaker's control, usually driven by feeling. It is most natural in the first person or when describing someone's nature.

synonyms.note: ずにはいられない means the same thing in a slightly more formal, written register.
てならない says a feeling wells up uncontrollably; ないではいられない says you can't stop yourself from acting on it.

related.note: ざるを得ない is being forced by circumstances with no choice; ないではいられない is an inner emotional urge.

structure: Verb［ない form］ ＋ ［ない → なければならない］

explanation: なければならない means 'must do / have to do', built the same way as なければいけない: ない form minus ない, plus なければならない. The ならない half suggests the obligation comes from a rule, social norm, or the nature of things rather than a personal whim, so it is common in written and formal contexts.

antonyms.note: なくてもいい lifts the obligation: 'you don't have to'.

related.note: 必要がある also states a need ('it's necessary to'), a softer relative of this strong 'must'.

meanings: after (much) ~; finally, at the end of
explanation: 末に marks a long or difficult process that finally leads to a result — 'after much ~, in the end...'. It stresses that the outcome came only after considerable effort, hesitation, or hardship. The result may be good or bad, but the focus is the drawn-out road to it.

synonyms.note: あげく also means 'in the end after ~', but almost always leads to a bad or unwanted outcome; 末に is neutral.

related.note: 結果 focuses on the outcome '(as) a result of'; 末に stresses the long process that led there.

meanings: thank you for ~ing
structure: Verb［て form］＋ くれてありがとう
Verb［て form］＋ くださってありがとうございます［polite］
explanation: Thanks someone for doing something for you. It joins てくれる (someone does a favor for me) with ありがとう. Because it rests on てくれる, the action being thanked benefits the speaker. Polite: 〜てくれてありがとうございます, or with the honorific 〜てくださってありがとうございます.

related.note: てくれる (does a favor for me) is exactly what this phrase thanks the other person for.
てすみません apologizes for an action; てくれてありがとう thanks for one — parallel structures.

meanings: whether ~ or ~
structure: Noun／Verb［plain form］＋ にしろ ＋ Noun／Verb［plain form］＋ にしろ

meanings: around; about (a point in time)
explanation: ころ／ごろ marks an approximate point in time — 'around'. Voiced ごろ attaches to a specific clock time or date (八時ごろ = around eight), while ころ follows periods or events (子どものころ = when I was a child). It pins down 'roughly when', not 'how long'.

related.note: くらい／ぐらい gives an approximate amount or degree; ごろ gives an approximate time point.
とき names the occasion 'when' something happens; ころ softens it to 'around the time'.

meanings: swapping が and の in modifying clauses
explanation: Inside a clause that modifies a noun (a relative clause), the subject can be marked with either が or の with no change in meaning: 母が作った料理 = 母の作った料理 (the food my mother made). の is common in shorter modifying clauses and can sound a touch softer. This swap works only inside noun-modifying clauses, never in a main sentence.

related.note: が is the plain subject marker; this point lets it become の in modifying clauses.
This modifying-clause の overlaps in form with the linking/possessive の.
は cannot be used inside such clauses — the subject there is が (or の), not は.

meanings: never; by no means; not at all (strong, firm denial)
explanation: 決して sets up an emphatic negative that follows later in the sentence, expressing the speaker's firm will or an absolute denial — 'never, no matter what.' It is stronger and more formal than ぜんぜん and often signals a promise or conviction.

synonyms.note: ぜんぜん〜ない is a neutral, conversational 'not at all'; 決して〜ない adds firm will and a formal, categorical tone.

related.note: 必ずしも〜ない softens to 'not necessarily'; 決して〜ない is an absolute 'never.'
なかなか〜ない means 'not easily / not readily'; 決して〜ない is a flat denial regardless of effort.

meanings: don't ~ (blunt prohibition)
explanation: Forbids an action bluntly: attach な to the dictionary form of a verb to say 'don't do that'. It is strong, direct, and rather rough, heard in commands, warnings, and emphatic speech, mostly among men or in urgent situations.

antonyms.note: The imperative form orders someone TO do something; な orders them NOT to.

related.note: てはいけない is the calmer, explanatory 'must not'; な is the blunt spoken 'don't'.
〜ないでください is the polite 'please don't'; な is its rough, abrupt counterpart.

meanings: won't be settled with just ~; ~ won't be the end of it

explanation: せいで pins a bad outcome on a cause — "because of ~, (something unwanted happened)." 電車が遅れたせいで、遅刻した = I was late because the train was delayed. The result is undesirable, and せいで often assigns fault. Its positive-outcome counterpart is おかげで.

related.note: ので is a neutral "because" with no blame; せいで adds fault for an unwanted outcome.

explanation: さも intensifies how convincingly something looks or sounds a certain way, pairing with appearance expressions like 〜そうに and 〜かのように: さも気持ちよさそうに = looking utterly content; さも見てきたかのように = for all the world as if he'd seen it himself. meanings: during; throughout; within (by the end of)
structure: Time／period ＋ 中に（ちゅうに）、＋ Sentence
explanation: 中 after a noun means "during / throughout," but the reading shifts the sense. ちゅう marks an ongoing action or a deadline (電話中 = mid-call, 今日中に = by the end of today); じゅう marks a whole span of time or space (一日中 = all day long, 世界中 = all over the world).
