meanings: if; when; after
explanation: 〜たら is the everyday conditional: take the plain past (た form) and add ら. Depending on context it means 'if ~,' 'when ~,' or 'after ~.' Its big strength is that the main clause can be a request, command, or wish, which many other conditionals block.

synonyms.note: 〜ば is a more formal 'if'; 〜たら is the everyday conditional and also means 'when/after.'
〜と is for automatic, always-true results; 〜たら allows requests and one-off cases.
〜なら responds to a supposition someone raised; 〜たら sets up your own condition.

related.note: 〜たらどう suggests 'why don't you,' built on the 〜たら conditional.

meanings: the one who/that ~ is X (it is X that ~)
structure: Verb［plain form］／Sentence ＋ のは ＋ Noun ＋ の方だ
explanation: This pattern singles out which side something is really true of, out of two possibilities. のは names the situation, and 〜の方だ points to the party or option it actually applies to — 謝るのはあなたの方だ = the one who should apologize is you. It often corrects or clarifies who or which is really the case, against a mistaken assumption.

related.note: 〜方がいい recommends one option over another; 〜のは〜の方だ points out which side something is actually true of.
nominalizing の turns a clause into a noun; this cleft uses that の to spotlight which party a statement applies to.

meanings: doubling as; also serving the purpose of

meanings: to assume; to take it that; to firmly believe that
explanation: 〜ものと思う expresses a settled assumption or expectation — 'I take it that ~, I assume that ~'. It is firmer and more formal than a plain と思う, presenting the belief as a reasoned premise rather than a passing thought: 全員が了承したものと思う = I take it everyone has consented. It attaches to a plain-form clause and is common in polite, deliberate speech and writing.

synonyms.note: と思う is the everyday 'I think'; ものと思う is more formal and presents the belief as a firm assumption.
ものと思われる is the objective passive 'it is thought that'; ものと思う states the speaker's own assumption.

related.note: はずだ draws a logical 'ought to be' from grounds; ものと思う states a settled assumption without stressing the reasoning.

related.note: ごとに counts every unit (毎回); おきに counts the gaps between, giving 'every other'.

meanings: so much ~ that; out of an excess of (a feeling)
explanation: 〜のあまり (after a noun of feeling) or 〜あまり (after a verb) means an emotion or state was so extreme that it caused the result that follows — 緊張のあまり = out of too much nervousness, 心配のあまり = from worrying too much. related.note: 〜ほど also builds 'so ~ that' by giving a yardstick; 〜のあまり frames an excess of feeling as the cause.

meanings: just as expected; sure enough; as feared
explanation: 案の定 marks that something turned out exactly as the speaker had anticipated — typically an unwelcome or worrying outcome. 案の定、失敗した = sure enough, it failed. meanings: 's; of (noun-linking)
explanation: The particle の joins two nouns so the first one describes or owns the second, like English "'s" or "of". It covers possession, belonging, and general relationships, and the describing noun always comes first: 私の本 is "my book".

related.note: The same の can stand in for a noun as "one", dropping the second noun.
の also turns a whole verb clause into a noun, a different job from linking two nouns.
Inside a noun-modifying clause, this same の can replace が as the subject marker.

meanings: casual explanatory の (question or statement)
variants.explanation: In casual speech, ending a sentence with の shows warm interest or offers an explanation. Rising intonation turns it into a question asking what's going on (どうしたの？), while falling intonation softly explains or states a reason. It is the relaxed, spoken cousin of んですか／んです, so you use it with friends and family rather than in formal situations.

synonyms.note: んです／のです is the polite full form; casual speech drops it to just の.

related.note: Same particle の, but here it colors a whole sentence — question or soft statement — rather than turning a clause into a noun.
か is a neutral question marker; explanatory の asks "tell me the reason/story".

meanings: the act of ~ (nominalizer)
variants.explanation: Placing の after a plain verb or clause turns that whole idea into a noun, so it can then take particles like が, を, or は. You reach for it to talk about doing something as a thing in itself, especially with verbs of perception such as 見る and 聞く.

synonyms.note: こと also nominalizes; の suits perceived, concrete events while こと suits abstract or stated ones.

related.note: のが好き is built on this nominalizing の plus が好き.

meanings: intended for; aimed at; made for (a target audience)

related.note: 向き is a natural fit ('suits beginners'); 向け is deliberate targeting ('made for beginners').

variants.explanation: 〜中を・〜中で(は) marks a surrounding situation — often busy, difficult, or inconvenient — against which something is nonetheless done. Here 中 is figurative ('amid such circumstances'), not a literal inside. 中を tends to accompany an action carried out despite the conditions, as in the set polite phrase お忙しい中を ('amid your busy schedule'); 中で(は) frames the prevailing situation.

related.note: 最中に pinpoints the exact moment an action is underway; 中を・中では frames a broader surrounding condition.
うちに means 'while a state lasts (before it changes)'; 中で(は) simply sets the prevailing circumstances.

surface: ないものか・ないものだろうか
reading: ないものか・ないものだろうか
meanings: isn't there some way to ~?; I do wish ~ could happen
structure: Verb［potential negative］＋ものか／ものだろうか
explanation: 〜ないものか voices a strong, half-rhetorical wish that something could be brought about: 'can't ~ somehow be done?'. なんとか解決できないものか = isn't there some way to solve this? It commonly follows a potential-negative verb (〜できない, 〜られない) and expresses yearning or frustrated hope rather than a real question. The だろうか version softens it into wistful pondering.

synonyms.note: ないものだろうか is the same wish with a musing, self-directed tone; ないものか alone can sound more pointed or impatient.

meanings: at least ~ (a minimum estimate)
explanation: は after a quantity marks it as a floor — 'at least that much': 二十分はかかる = 'it takes at least twenty minutes'. The speaker guesses the real figure is that big or bigger.

related.note: The everyday topic marker は; after quantities は shifts to 'at least'.
数字＋も says the amount IS large; 数量＋は only sets a lower bound.
くらい gives a rough 'about'; 数量＋は commits to a minimum.

meanings: as many as ~; (with negative) not even one
structure: 一 ＋ Counter ＋ も ＋ Verb［ない form］
explanation: After a number plus counter, も signals that the speaker finds the amount remarkably large: 五杯も飲んだ = 'drank as many as five cups'. With 一＋counter and a negative verb it flips to total absence: 一つもない = 'not even one'.

antonyms.note: 数量＋しか〜ない paints the amount as too small; 数字＋も paints it as strikingly large.

related.note: Plain も means 'also, too'; after numbers it becomes an amount-emphasizer.
少しも〜ない denies even a small degree, much as 一つも〜ない denies even one item.

meanings: to want someone (else) to do ~
structure: Noun［person］＋ に ＋ Verb［て form］＋ ほしい
Verb［ない form］＋ でほしい［negative］
explanation: てほしい expresses wanting another person to do something. The person you want to act is marked with に, and ほしい inflects like an い-adjective. The negative 'want you NOT to' is 〜ないでほしい.

related.note: がほしい wants an object; てほしい wants an action from someone.
〜たい is wanting to do something yourself; てほしい is wanting someone else to do it.
ように〜てほしい softens the request, often for outcomes not fully in the person's control.

meanings: on the occasion of; when (the chance arises)
explanation: 〜折に(は) marks a particular occasion or opportune moment for doing something — 'when, on the occasion of'. 上京の折には = when you come up to Tokyo; お近くにお越しの折は = should you happen to be nearby. It attaches to a noun + の or a plain-form verb and belongs to polite, somewhat formal speech, often in greetings and invitations. It tends to mark a good or fitting occasion.

synonyms.note: 〜際に is a formal 'on the occasion of / when'; 折に is similarly polite but favors welcome, opportune occasions and set greetings.

related.note: 〜にあたって marks 'on the occasion of' a significant, one-off undertaking; 折に marks a fitting moment, often social or recurring.

meanings: when; at the time of ~
explanation: Marks the time or occasion when something happens: place とき after a verb, adjective, or noun phrase to mean 'when ~'. The form and tense of the word before とき shows whether the action is before, during, or after the main event.

related.note: まえに pins the action to just before an event; とき marks the general time it happens.
あとで marks 'after'; とき marks the moment 'when' something is the case.
あいだ covers a whole span 'while'; とき points to a particular time or occasion.

surface: にかかっては・にかかったら・にかかると
reading: にかかっては・にかかったら・にかかると
meanings: in the hands of ~; once ~ takes it on (things inevitably go a certain way)
structure: Noun［person］＋にかかっては／にかかったら／にかかると
explanation: 〜にかかっては marks that once a certain formidable or skilled person gets involved, a particular result becomes unavoidable — 'in the hands of ~'. あの弁護士にかかっては = in the hands of that lawyer, どんな難事件も解決してしまう. The person is marked with に, and the main clause states what inevitably happens once they take charge, often with a touch of admiration or resignation. It is conversational.

related.note: にかかっている states that an outcome depends on a factor; にかかっては describes what a certain person inevitably brings about.
にかけては praises someone as unmatched in a skill; にかかっては stresses the inevitable result once they take something on.

meanings: without; leaving out; setting aside
structure: Noun ＋ 抜きで／抜きにして
Noun ＋ を抜きにしては ＋ ～ない
explanation: 〜抜きで and 〜抜きにして mean doing something while leaving out a normally-expected element. 朝食抜きで = without breakfast; 冗談抜きで = joking aside. 〜は抜きにして ('let's leave ~ out') often opens a suggestion to set something aside. It attaches to a noun. The related 〜を抜きにしては + negative means the following would be impossible without it.

synonyms.note: 〜なし simply states a noun's absence ('without ~'); 抜き stresses deliberately leaving out something normally included.
なしに・なしで also means 'without'; 抜きにして often carries the nuance 'let's set aside / omit on purpose'.

related.note: など lists examples 'and so on'; か何か offers one vague alternative 'or something like it'.

meanings: looking ~; with an air of ~ (seeming)
explanation: 〜げ attaches to an adjective stem, or to the stem of 〜たい, to form a な-adjective/adverb meaning 'looking ~, with an air of ~'. 寂しげ = looking lonely, 自慢げ = with a boastful air, 言いたげ = as if wanting to say something. It describes the outward impression a person gives off, usually about their feelings.

synonyms.note: そうな reports how something looks generally; 〜げ centers on the air a person gives off, especially about feelings.
っぽい says something has a ~ quality or tendency; 〜げ is specifically 'seeming / looking'.

meanings: casual yes/no question marker
explanation: かい is a casual sentence-ending particle that turns a plain statement into a friendly yes/no question. 元気かい = You doing okay? It sounds softer and warmer than a bare rising-intonation question, and carries a slightly older, masculine flavour, often used toward friends or children.

related.note: か is the neutral, polite question particle; かい is its casual, friendly yes/no cousin.
かしら wonders to oneself; かい asks the listener directly.

meanings: from the viewpoint of; seen from; judging from
structure: Noun ＋ から見ると／から見れば／から見て
explanation: Noun + から見ると / から見れば / から見て takes a standpoint or a body of evidence and states how things appear from there — 'seen from X's perspective' or 'judging by X'. 見る ('to look') frames a point of view, whether a person's perspective or the grounds for a judgment.

synonyms.note: からすると / からすれば expresses the same 'judging from / from the standpoint of' with little difference in meaning.
からして shares the 'judging from' sense but also has a separate 'even (to begin with)' use.

related.note: にとって marks whom or what something matters to ('for ~'); から見ると frames the viewpoint from which a judgment is made.

meanings: to pretend; to act as if; to put on an act of ~
structure: Verb［plain form］／い-adjective＋ ふりをする
な-adjective＋ な／Noun＋ の ＋ ふりをする
explanation: ふりをする means to pretend or put on an act — to behave as if something were true when it isn't. 寝ているふりをする = pretend to be asleep; 知らないふりをする = pretend not to know. Verbs and い-adjectives attach plainly, while nouns and な-adjectives take の／な first.

related.note: かのように describes an action as if something were the case; ふりをする is deliberately faking a state or behavior.
まるで sets up a 'just like' comparison; ふりをする is putting on a false act on purpose.

meanings: can be seen; can be viewed
explanation: 見られる is the potential form of 見る: 'can see' or 'can watch', in the sense that the opportunity is there. With が marking what you're able to see, it fits places or events where a sight is available — 桜が見られる = you can see the cherry blossoms. It implies you get the chance to look, not that the view simply falls into your eyes.

related.note: 見える is a sight coming into view on its own; 見られる is having the chance to view it.
聞こえる is the hearing counterpart — sound that reaches you spontaneously.
見られる is just the potential form of 見る built with 〜られる.

meanings: and (listing nouns)
structure: Noun ＋ と ＋ Noun［repeatable with と］
explanation: Joins nouns into a complete list: place と between nouns to connect them, like 'and' in English. It presents the listed items as the full set, implying nothing else is included.

related.note: や lists a few representative examples; と lists the items exhaustively.
The same particle と in its other core use, 'together with' someone.
など ('etc.') marks an open-ended list; と marks a closed, complete one.

meanings: with; together with
structure: Noun ＋ と ＋ 一緒に ＋ Verb
variants.explanation: Marks the person or thing you do something together with: place と after a noun to show a companion or partner in the action. It answers 'with whom?' and often pairs with 一緒に for emphasis.

related.note: 一緒に ('together') often teams up with と to stress doing the action jointly.
The same particle と in its listing use, 'A and B'.

meanings: quotation marker (~ that; ~ so)
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋ と ＋ 言う／思う／書く
variants.explanation: と marks the content of speech or thought and hands it to a reporting verb like 言う (say), 思う (think), or 書く (write). The quoted part stays in plain form, and と links it to what someone said, thought, or wrote.

synonyms.note: って is the casual spoken version of quotative と.

related.note: 〜と思う is this quotative と with 思う, marking your opinion.
〜という uses the same と to attach a name or label to a noun.
Conditional と means 'when/if'; don't confuse it with this quotative と.

meanings: whenever/if A, then B (natural result)
variants.explanation: と joins two clauses to say that whenever A happens, B follows automatically. It's for predictable, natural consequences — how machines work, directions, habits, and cause-and-effect that always plays out the same way.

synonyms.note: たら is the most flexible 'if/when' and allows requests in the result; と is limited to automatic results.
ば is a general conditional; と stresses that B always follows A.

related.note: なら reacts to a topic just raised; と states a repeatable, automatic consequence.

meanings: A or B
explanation: Putting か after each of two (or more) options presents them as alternatives — 'A or B'. The final か just before the verb is often dropped in speech: コーヒーか紅茶（か）。 Use it to offer a choice or to ask which of several things applies.

related.note: The single sentence-final か asks a question; か〜か lays out choices.
と lists items that all apply together; か〜か offers one option or another.
や lists examples ('and things like'); か〜か presents an either/or choice.

meanings: truly; indeed; just like; every bit the ~
explanation: いかにも emphasizes that something looks or feels exactly as one would expect of its type — 'truly, indeed, every bit the ~'. いかにも高級そうだ = looks every bit as upscale as you'd imagine, いかにも彼らしい = so typical of him. It often pairs with 〜そう or 〜らしい and conveys that appearances strongly match a stereotype. It can also simply intensify, meaning 'truly / really'.

synonyms.note: さすが praises something for living up to its reputation; いかにも neutrally notes that appearance matches the expected type.

related.note: 〜らしい says something is typical of its kind; いかにも often reinforces it ('so very ~-like').

meanings: along with; on a par with; ranking alongside; as ... as
explanation: Literally 'standing in a row with', Noun ＋ と並んで is mostly used figuratively to rank two things at the same level — この寺は京都と並んで有名だ = this temple is famous, on a par with Kyoto. It presents the two as comparable in standing or reputation. It has a formal, evaluative tone, common when praising or ranking things.

synonyms.note: と同じくらい measures two things as roughly equal in a stated degree; と並んで ranks them at the same level of standing.

related.note: と共に is 'together with / at the same time'; と並んで places two things side by side as equals in rank.

explanation: 〜ようにも〜ない says that even if you had the will to do something, external circumstances make it impossible. meanings: 〜く + は (contrast or qualified negation)

explanation: Adding は to the adverbial 〜く form of an い-adjective sets that quality apart for contrast or partial denial, most often before a negative: 高くはない = it's not exactly expensive (as for being pricey, no). meanings: if it were ~ that would be one thing, but ~
explanation: 〜ならまだしも grants that one case would be comparatively acceptable, so as to condemn the actual, worse case: 一度だけならまだしも = if it were just once that would be tolerable, but... meanings: everything; each and every thing; from A to Z
explanation: 何から何まで is a set phrase meaning 'absolutely everything, down to every detail'. The words are fixed and don't vary. It stresses the full extent of something — often in gratitude (何から何までお世話になりました) but also in complaint. It functions adverbially before the verb or as a predicate.

synonyms.note: ことごとく means 'every one without exception' in a more formal, written tone; 何から何まで is a set colloquial phrase for 'the whole lot'.

related.note: に至るまで stresses that the range extends even to an extreme point; 何から何まで simply asserts 'all of it, every part'.

meanings: conversely; on the contrary; if anything, the opposite
explanation: 逆に is an adverb meaning 'the other way around / conversely'. It flags that what follows runs counter to what was just said or to what you would expect — you tried for one result and got the reverse, or you turn to look at the opposite case. 励ますつもりが逆に怒らせた = meant to encourage, but instead made them angry.

反面 weighs the other side of the same thing; 逆に marks a straight reversal or contrary outcome.

related.note: 一方で lays out the other of two coexisting sides neutrally; 逆に emphasizes that the second point overturns the first.

explanation: すら singles out an extreme example to imply that if even this holds, the rest goes without saying — 専門家ですら分からない = even experts don't understand (so of course others don't). だに also means 'even', but is archaic and limited to set phrases; すら is freer to use.

meanings: on the way; partway; in the middle of (doing something)
explanation: 途中で marks a point partway through a movement or an action, often where something interrupts it — 家に帰る途中で友達に会った = I met a friend on the way home; 会議の途中で電話が鳴った = the phone rang in the middle of the meeting. After a verb use the dictionary form; after a noun join with の. で is the usual particle, marking where the mid-point event occurs.

related.note: あいだに frames a whole stretch of time in which you do something; 途中で pinpoints a single moment partway through.
うちに is 'while a state still holds'; 途中で is 'at a point midway through an action or trip'.

meanings: how should I put it; or perhaps I should say ~
explanation: 〜といおうか introduces a description offered tentatively as the speaker reaches for the fitting words — 'what should I call it, or perhaps ~'. It often comes in pairs (〜といおうか〜といおうか) or just before a rephrasing, marking that the chosen word is only approximate. It is a shade more literary and reflective than 〜というか, and conveys genuine hesitation over how to characterize something.

synonyms.note: というか〜というか does the same word-searching in an everyday, conversational tone; といおうか is more literary and reflective.

meanings: if only ~; and yet (regret or reproach)
explanation: 〜ものを expresses regret or reproach that reality turned out differently from what could or should have been. It typically follows a hypothetical (〜ば／〜たら) describing the better outcome that failed to happen: 一言言ってくれればよかったものを = if only you'd said something. The tone is emotional and often faintly accusatory, and the sentence may trail off after ものを, leaving the complaint implied. It is literary and expressive.

related.note: くせに reproaches a person for acting against what their situation warrants; ものを laments a better outcome that a hypothetical could have secured.

It almost always pairs with 〜も or 〜でも to form 'no matter what ~': いかなる理由があっても = whatever the reason, いかなる困難も = any hardship whatsoever. It modifies a noun directly and belongs to written, legal, or ceremonial registers.

synonyms.note: どんな is the everyday 'what kind of'; いかなる is its formal, written counterpart.

related.note: どんなに〜ても stresses degree ('however much'); いかなる〜も ranges over kinds ('whatever ~').
を問わず means 'regardless of ~'; いかなる〜も makes a similar sweep adnominally before a noun.

surface: をかえりみず・もかえりみず
reading: をかえりみず・もかえりみず
meanings: without regard for; heedless of
explanation: 〜を顧みず means acting without giving thought to something one arguably should heed — danger, one's own body, or one's family. 危険を顧みず火の中へ = plunging into the fire heedless of danger; 家庭を顧みない = neglectful of one's family. 顧みる literally means 'to look back on / pay heed to', so 顧みず is 'without heeding'. It is formal and largely written, and the も variant adds a 'not even' shading (身の危険も顧みず).

synonyms.note: をものともせずに praises bravely overcoming a hardship; を顧みず emphasizes simply not giving thought to what one should heed.

related.note: もかまわず = not minding/caring about something; を顧みず specifically frames it as failing to give due heed to danger or one's own welfare.

meanings: of all people, ~ (an out-of-character blunder)
structure: Noun［person, usually 私］＋としたことが
explanation: 〜としたことが expresses dismay that a normally reliable person did something so unlike them. It attaches to a person (very often 私), and the clause that follows admits an uncharacteristic mistake or lapse: 私としたことが、うっかりしていた = of all people, I was being careless. The tone is self-reproach or gentle astonishment that someone who should have known better slipped up.

synonyms.note: ともあろうものが criticizes someone by their lofty role or title; としたことが centers on behavior that is out of character, often one's own.

related.note: とは voices bare surprise that a fact is even true; としたことが adds that the person responsible should have known better.

surface: いずれにしても・いずれにしろ・いずれにせよ
reading: いずれにしても・いずれにしろ・いずれにせよ
meanings: in any case; either way; whichever it is
structure: （Options）＋いずれにしても／いずれにしろ／いずれにせよ、＋Sentence
explanation: いずれにしても (also いずれにしろ／いずれにせよ) sets aside which of several possibilities holds and moves to a conclusion that applies to all of them — 'either way, in any case'. 賛成でも反対でも、いずれにせよ理由を聞きたい = for or against, either way I want to hear your reasons. It works as a transition, dismissing the alternatives as not changing what follows. にせよ／にしろ are more formal than にしても.

synonyms.note: 〜にしても〜にしても lays out the specific options ('whether A or B'); いずれにしても bundles them into a single 'either way'.

related.note: 〜はともかく sets an issue aside to focus elsewhere; いずれにしても concludes that the alternatives don't change the result.

variants.explanation: ようにする says you deliberately arrange your behavior so a certain thing happens (or does not). It expresses making an effort or keeping a conscious habit: 毎日運動するようにする = 'make a point of exercising daily'. With ている (ようにしている) it stresses an ongoing habit you keep up.

related.note: ようになる is the change coming about on its own; ようにする is the effort you make.
ことにする is a firm decision to do something; ようにする is ongoing effort or habit.
The same purpose ように, here completed by する into a personal effort.

meanings: with ~; having ~; ~ included
explanation: 〜あり is a noun-like suffix built from ある that labels something as 'having ~' or 'with ~' — 駐車場あり = parking available, わけあり = with (special) circumstances. You see it on notices, listings, and menus. Its opposite is 〜なし ('without ~').

antonyms.note: 〜なし is the exact opposite — 'without ~'; 〜あり marks that something is present or included.

meanings: almost every ~; practically every ~
structure: 毎 ＋ Noun［time period］＋ のように
explanation: 毎 means 'every', and 毎〜のように adds 'as if', giving 'almost every ~'. It attaches to time words such as 日 (day), 週 (week), or 年 (year): 毎日のように = practically every day. The のように softens 毎 from a strict 'every' into 'so often it might as well be every'.

related.note: ごとに marks a regular interval ('every X'); 毎〜のように means 'almost, but not strictly, every'.
たびに means 'every time (an event) happens'; 毎〜のように counts recurring time periods.

meanings: only by doing ~; it is precisely because one does ~
explanation: てこそ combines the て-form with the emphatic particle こそ to single out an action as the essential condition for a valued result — 努力してこそ成功する = 'it is only through effort that one succeeds'. The clause after it is normally positive and desirable: the point is that the good outcome is possible only because of the highlighted action.

synonyms.note: て初めて means 'not until ~ did ...', stressing a first realization; てこそ stresses the essential condition for a good result.

related.note: こそ is the underlying emphatic particle ('precisely'); てこそ applies it to a verb as the key condition.
ばこそ ('precisely because') is a more formal, literary way to stress a reason; てこそ focuses on an enabling action.

surface: をおして・をおしきって
reading: をおして・をおしきって
meanings: doing something despite opposition or one's own poor condition
explanation: 〜を押して and 〜を押し切って mean forging ahead despite an obstacle. を押し切って stresses forcibly overriding others' resistance — 周囲の反対を押し切って結婚した = married in the face of everyone's objections. を押して is often used of acting despite one's own condition — 病を押して出席する = attend despite illness. The object is the obstacle being overcome (opposition, illness), not a physical thing.

related.note: をものともせずに = undaunted by hardship, admiring the resolve; を押し切って highlights the act of forcibly overriding resistance.
を顧みず = without giving thought to danger/consequences; を押して = pressing on despite an obstacle one is clearly aware of.

surface: たことにする・たことになる
reading: たことにする・たことになる
meanings: to pretend/treat as if ~ happened; to be regarded as if ~ happened
explanation: 〜たことにする means someone decides to treat something as if it happened (or, with なかった, as if it didn't), often contrary to fact — 聞かなかったことにする = pretend I didn't hear it. 〜たことになる is the passive counterpart: it ends up officially or effectively counting as having happened — サインすれば受け取ったことになる = signing counts as having received it. Both build on the た-form.

synonyms.note: ふりをする is to put on an act in the moment; たことにする sets up a fact to be treated as settled afterward.

meanings: now that; since; given that (so one should ~)
structure: Noun／な-adjective ＋ である ＋ からには
explanation: [plain form] + からには means 'now that / since X is the case', and because it is so, the speaker draws a firm consequence: the main clause states a resolve, an obligation, or a natural expectation (should, must, of course). It commits the speaker more strongly than a plain から.

synonyms.note: 以上は means much the same 'now that / since', and is nearly interchangeable; からには sounds a touch more conversational.
上は also means 'now that', but is more formal and written; からには is the everyday choice.

related.note: Plain から just gives a reason; からには adds that, given the premise, a matching resolve or obligation follows.

meanings: -al; -ic; relating to; turns a noun into a な-adjective or adverb
explanation: 的 attaches to a noun to make an adjective-like word meaning 'relating to / -al / -ic' — 一般的 = general, 科学的 = scientific, 積極的 = proactive. Add な before a noun (的な考え) and に to use it adverbially (的に説明する). It's extremely common in both writing and speech.

related.note: っぽい is a casual '-ish' added to everyday words; 的 forms categorical '-al/-ic' adjectives from kanji compounds.

surface: くらいなら・ぐらいなら
reading: くらいなら・ぐらいなら
meanings: rather than (do something that unpleasant); if it comes to ~, I'd sooner
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋くらいなら＋（むしろ）～ほうがましだ／～たい
explanation: 〜くらいなら weighs the first option as something so unpleasant that the speaker would sooner take another, often drastic, alternative — 'rather than A, I'd rather B'. 途中でやめるくらいなら、最初からやらない = rather than quit halfway, I'd not start at all. It attaches to a dictionary-form verb and frequently pairs with むしろ or 〜ほうがましだ. It is a pointed comparison, not a neutral one.

synonyms.note: むしろ marks the 'rather / sooner' side of the choice and often co-occurs; くらいなら packages the rejected option as an unbearable one.

related.note: より makes a plain comparison ('than'); くらいなら adds that the first option is bad enough to reject outright.

meanings: ought to be ~; it is only natural/proper that ~; deserves to be ~
explanation: 〜てしかるべきだ says something is proper and to be expected — it ought to be so as a matter of course. 努力は評価されてしかるべきだ = such effort ought to be, and deserves to be, recognized. しかるべき means 'appropriate / as it should be', so the phrase asserts that the state described by the て-form is the natural, reasonable thing. It is formal and often argues that something rightly should happen.

synonyms.note: plain 〜べきだ states a direct 'should / ought to'; てしかるべきだ frames it as what is only natural and proper, often more measured and formal.
〜て当然だ ('naturally ~; no wonder ~') also says something is to be expected; てしかるべきだ adds the sense that it is the proper, deserved thing.

meanings: please do ~ (soft, casual request)
explanation: てちょうだい follows the て-form to make a gentle, casual request — 取ってちょうだい = 'pass it to me, would you'. It is softer and more familiar than てください, and is used mainly among family and close acquaintances, often by women or when speaking to children. It carries a warm, coaxing tone rather than a formal one.

synonyms.note: てください is the standard polite request; てちょうだい is softer, casual, and more intimate.

related.note: てほしい states a wish for someone to act ('I want you to ~'); てちょうだい directly makes the request.

meanings: to depend on; to hinge on; to rest on
structure: Noun／Sentence［〜かどうか］＋は＋Noun＋にかかっている
explanation: 〜にかかっている says that an outcome rests entirely on one deciding factor — 'it all depends on ~, it hinges on ~'. The uncertain result is usually phrased with 〜かどうか or a question word, and the factor it turns on is marked with に: 成功するかどうかは君の努力にかかっている = whether it succeeds depends on your effort. It stresses that everything comes down to that one thing.

synonyms.note: 次第だ names the deciding factor formally ('depending on ~'); にかかっている stresses that the whole outcome rests on it.

related.note: によって marks a means or cause; にかかっている frames one factor as the thing an entire outcome hangs on.
にかかっては describes what inevitably happens once a certain person takes charge; にかかっている states that an outcome depends on a factor.

meanings: there is a possibility that; it is possible that
structure: Noun＋の／である＋可能性がある
explanation: 〜可能性がある states that some outcome is objectively possible — 'there is a possibility that ~'. It attaches to a plain-form verb or adjective, or to a noun via の / である. 中止になる可能性がある = there is a chance it will be called off. The degree can be tuned with 高い or 低い (可能性が高い = a strong possibility). Compared with かもしれない it is more analytical and neutral, suited to reports and formal explanation.

synonyms.note: かもしれない voices the speaker's own conjecture; 可能性がある frames the same chance as an objective, measurable one.
かねない warns that a bad outcome could happen; 可能性がある is neutral about whether the outcome is good or bad.

related.note: 恐れがある reserves itself for the risk of an undesirable result; 可能性がある covers any outcome.

meanings: without even doing ~
explanation: Inserting も into the negative 〜しないで gives 〜もしないで, 'without even doing ~'. The も adds 'even', so it reproaches someone for skipping a basic, expected action: 確認もしないで = without even checking, 聞きもしないで = without even listening. For する-verbs it is Noun ＋ もしないで (確認もしないで); for other verbs it is the verb stem ＋ もしないで (見もしないで, 聞きもしないで). It typically carries criticism or exasperation.

synonyms.note: 〜ないで is neutral 'without doing ~'; 〜もしないで inserts も to mean 'without even ~' and adds reproach.
〜ずに is a more formal 'without doing'; もしないで is emphatic and critical about a skipped basic step.

explanation: Intensifies an adjective or adverb: put とても before it to say 'very'. It is a neutral, everyday booster that works in both polite and casual speech, and it is one of the first intensifiers a learner uses.

meanings: regardless of; whether or not; irrespective of
structure: Verb／い-adjective［affirmative + negative pair］＋にかかわらず
explanation: 〜にかかわらず means a result holds no matter which of the possibilities applies. It attaches to a noun (天候にかかわらず) or to a paired affirmative-and-negative (参加するしないにかかわらず, 有無にかかわらず). The point is that variation in the condition makes no difference to the outcome.

synonyms.note: を問わず also means 'regardless of / irrespective of'; both are formal, with を問わず common in notices (年齢を問わず).

related.note: にもかかわらず means 'despite', conceding a real fact; にかかわらず means 'no matter which', with no fact conceded.
によらず likewise means 'regardless of / not depending on'; にかかわらず often pairs opposite options for 'either way'.

meanings: undaunted by; in defiance of (a hardship or danger)
explanation: 〜をものともせず（に） attaches to a noun naming a difficulty, danger, or setback and says the subject pressed on without being cowed by it — 困難をものともせず (undaunted by hardship), 荒波をものともせず (in defiance of the rough seas). The tone is admiring: it praises someone for bravely facing down an obstacle, so it usually describes other people's courage rather than one's own trivial troubles.

synonyms.note: にもかかわらず neutrally states 'despite'; をものともせず adds that the subject bravely overpowered the obstacle.

related.note: をよそに also means acting in the face of something, but coolly disregards concern one ought to heed; をものともせず courageously overcomes a hardship.

meanings: by means of; due to; depending on; passive agent
it is true that ~, but; ~ indeed, yet
explanation: In the 〜こそ〜が pattern, こそ emphasizes a point that is then conceded, while が (or けれど) introduces the contrasting main claim. The shape is 'A こそ ~, が B' = 'A may indeed be the case, but B'. 規模こそ小さいが = small in scale it may be, but... The real weight of the sentence falls on the clause after が; the こそ part is granted only to be set against it.

related.note: こそ on its own simply emphasizes ('it is precisely ~'); 〜こそ〜が uses that emphasis to set up a concession before a contrast.
こそあれ concedes that A exists then downplays it; 〜こそ〜が concedes A then contrasts it with a weightier main claim.

explanation: 〜べく expresses purpose in a formal, written register — 'in order to ~, so as to ~'. 目標を達成すべく = in order to achieve the goal. meanings: in order to; for the purpose of (formal)
in order to ~; so as to ~ (literary)
variants.explanation: 〜べく expresses purpose in a formal, written register — 'in order to ~, so as to ~'. 目標を達成すべく = in order to achieve the goal. It follows a dictionary-form verb (する → すべく or するべく), and the main clause describes a deliberate action taken toward that aim. It is the literary cousin of ように and ために.

synonyms.note: ために is the everyday 'in order to'; べく expresses the same purpose in a literary register.

related.note: べくして (as was bound to happen) uses the same べく root but expresses inevitability, not purpose.

meanings: only; nothing but (with a negative)
structure: Noun ＋ しか ＋ Verb［ない form］
explanation: しか follows a noun and pairs with a negative predicate to mean 'nothing but': 卵しかない = 'there's nothing but eggs'. Unlike だけ, it frames what remains as less than hoped or expected.

synonyms.note: だけ states 'only' neutrally with an affirmative verb; しか〜ない adds a sense of insufficiency.

related.note: The same pattern applied to amounts: 三時間しか寝ていない.
だけしか combines both words for extra emphasis, still with a negative.
Verb＋しかない (N3) is a different point: 'there is no choice but to ~'.

meanings: have no choice but to (do)
variants.explanation: しかない after a dictionary-form verb means there's no option left but to do that action — "have no choice but to." Literally "there is nothing except doing X." It usually carries a note of reluctant acceptance: this is the only path available, so you take it.

synonyms.note: 〜よりほかない means the same "nothing for it but to," in a stiffer, more written tone.
〜よりしかたがない also means "no way but to," stressing there's no other method.

related.note: 〜ざるを得ない is a formal "be forced to," stressing outside pressure; しかない is the plainer "no choice but to."
The noun-attaching しか〜ない means "only"; this verb-attaching しかない means "no choice but to."

meanings: only; nothing but (emphatic)
structure: Noun ＋ だけしか ＋ Verb［ない form］
Number＋Counter ＋ だけしか ＋ Verb［ない form］
explanation: だけしか stacks だけ onto しか to drive home "only / nothing but," and like plain しか it must be followed by a negative verb. The doubling makes the limitation sound stronger, and often more regretful, than だけ on its own.

synonyms.note: しか〜ない is the base 'only ... not' pattern; だけしか adds だけ for extra emphasis on the limit.

related.note: だけ takes a positive verb and is neutral; だけしか demands a negative and stresses how little there is.
のみ is a formal, written 'only'; だけしか is emphatic and colloquial with a regretful tone.

meanings: with much effort; a precious/long-awaited chance (so it'd be a shame to waste it)
structure: せっかく ＋ Verb／Noun（… のに／… だから）
explanation: せっかく marks something as the fruit of special effort or a rare opportunity, so it would be a shame to let it go to waste. It often pairs with のに (regret that the effort or chance was wasted) or だから (so let's make the most of it): せっかく作ったのに = I went to all that trouble to make it, yet…

related.note: わざわざ stresses going out of one's way to do something deliberately; せっかく stresses that the effort or chance shouldn't be wasted.
せっかく often leads into のに to voice regret that the effort came to nothing.

meanings: to (humbly) do ~ for someone
explanation: お＋verb stem＋する is the humble (kenjougo) pattern for your own action when it touches someone you respect. お持ちします = I'll carry it (for you); お送りします = I'll see you off. It lowers you to raise the other person. する-verbs of Chinese origin take ご instead: ご案内する.

synonyms.note: お～いたす swaps する for the humble いたす — the same pattern, one step more formal.

antonyms.note: お～になる raises the other person's action; お～する humbly lowers your own.

related.note: お～ください asks the listener to act; お～する is you acting humbly for them.

meanings: both ~ and ~; (with negatives) neither ~ nor ~
structure: Noun ＋ も ＋ Verb／い-adjective［ば form］、Noun ＋ も 〜
explanation: も〜ば〜も lists two parallel facts about one topic, using the ば conditional on the first predicate — 歌も歌えばギターも弾く = both sings and plays guitar. With negatives it becomes 'neither...nor'. It piles up matching items rather than stating a real condition.

related.note: だけでなく adds a second point onto a first; も〜ば〜も sets two items side by side as a balanced pair.
ばかりでなく is 'not only...but also'; も〜ば〜も simply lists two coexisting facts.

meanings: to; toward
explanation: へ marks the direction of movement, pointing the verb toward a place, like "to" or "toward". With motion verbs it is very close to に, but へ stresses the heading or direction rather than the exact arrival point.

synonyms.note: に marks the destination or arrival point; へ emphasizes the direction you move in.

related.note: へ行く is the common set phrase of this particle with the verb 行く.
まで marks the end point "as far as / up to"; へ just points toward a direction.

meanings: things like ~; such as ~ (often dismissive or emphatic)
explanation: なんか and なんて are casual, emotional versions of など. After a noun they mean 'things like ~ / such as ~', usually with a dismissive or belittling tone — スポーツなんか興味がない ('no interest in stuff like sports'). なんて can also follow a whole clause to show surprise or disbelief — 負けるなんて ('to think you'd lose!'). The feeling behind them is what sets them apart from plain など.

synonyms.note: など is the neutral 'such as / and so on'; なんか・なんて add a casual, often dismissive feeling.

meanings: -ness; turns an adjective into a noun of degree
explanation: さ attaches to the stem of an adjective and turns the quality into a noun, usually one you can measure or compare: 高い → 高さ (height), 便利 → 便利さ (convenience). Reach for it when you want to talk about the degree of a quality — how deep, how important, how convenient something is.

synonyms.note: 〜み also nominalizes adjectives, but adds a subjective, felt flavor and works with a limited set of words.

related.note: の turns whole clauses into nouns; さ works only on adjective stems.

meanings: well now; come on; all right (prompting)
variants.explanation: Used at the start of an utterance (often lengthened to さあ), this さ urges or invites — 'come on,' 'all right, let's…,' 'now then.' It rallies the listener toward the next action rather than adding meaning to the sentence.

related.note: The filler さ drops into the middle of casual speech; this さ opens an utterance to urge someone on.
Sentence-final さ asserts casually; sentence-initial さ prompts action.

meanings: like; you know; I mean (casual filler)
structure: …さ、… （inserted after a phrase in casual speech）
variants.explanation: In casual talk, さ can be dropped in after phrases to buy a beat or keep the listener's attention — much like English 'like' or 'you know.' It adds no meaning; it softens the flow and marks the rhythm of chatty speech.

related.note: The opening さ(あ) urges someone to act; the filler さ just keeps casual speech flowing.
Sentence-final さ closes a line with a light assertion; the filler さ sits mid-sentence.

meanings: casual sentence-final particle; a light, offhand よ
variants.explanation: At the end of a sentence, さ makes a relaxed, offhand assertion — a softer, more casual cousin of よ. It states a view or reassures in a light, matter-of-fact way, and has a somewhat masculine, easygoing feel.

related.note: Sentence-initial さ(あ) prompts action; this sentence-final さ makes a casual assertion.
The filler さ sits mid-sentence and adds no meaning; this さ closes a line with a light claim.
The N4 suffix さ turns an adjective into a noun (高さ, height); this さ is a sentence-final particle — same spelling, different job.

meanings: godan (う-verb) conjugation
structure: Dictionary ＋ 書く・飲む・話す［ends in an う-row kana］
Negative: final kana → あ-row ＋ ない — 書く→書かない
Past: 書く→書いた／飲む→飲んだ／話す→話した
Negative-past: あ-row ＋ なかった — 書く→書かなかった
explanation: う-verbs (godan verbs) are the verb group whose final -u kana shifts across a whole row of the kana chart when you conjugate. For the plain negative, change the final -u kana to its -a row form and add ない (書く→書かない); the past uses the sound-change た／だ endings (飲む→飲んだ); the negative-past ends in なかった. Recognising this group is the first big step to conjugating Japanese verbs.

related.note: る-verbs (ichidan) conjugate more simply — just drop る and add the ending.
する is irregular and follows neither the う- nor る-verb pattern.
くる is irregular, changing its stem vowel (きます・こない) unlike regular groups.

meanings: no matter what/how; even if; regardless of ~
explanation: A single volitional followed by が or と means 'no matter ~ / even if ~': 何を言われようが = no matter what I'm told, どうなろうと = no matter what happens. It concedes any possibility and states that the main clause holds all the same. With adjectives it uses かろう (どんなに苦しかろうと), and with nouns/な-adjectives であろう (誰であろうと). It is emphatic and more formal than ても.

synonyms.note: ても is the everyday 'even if ~'; 〜ようと／ようが is more emphatic and formal, stressing 'no matter what'.
doubling it (ようが〜ようが) lists two specific alternatives; the single form concedes any possibility at all.

related.note: もかまわず means 'without regard for ~ (and acting anyway)'; 〜ようと states that the outcome holds no matter the case.

meanings: -ish; -like; has the quality of; tends to
explanation: っぽい tacks onto a noun, adjective stem, or verb stem to say something has the quality or tendency of that word — 子供っぽい = childish, 忘れっぽい = forgetful, 安っぽい = cheap-looking. The whole compound behaves like an い-adjective. It's colloquial and often carries a mildly critical tone.

synonyms.note: みたいだ says something resembles or looks like another thing; っぽい says it has that quality or tendency, more casually.

related.note: がち is about how often an event tends to happen; っぽい 'tends to' describes a lasting quality or trait.
らしい means 'befitting / typical of'; っぽい often means the opposite — merely -ish, or not quite befitting.

meanings: apt to; prone to; liable to
structure: ともすれば＋Sentence（〜がち／〜やすい／〜かねない）
explanation: ともすれば sets up a tendency to slip easily into a state — usually an undesirable one — under the right conditions. It pairs naturally with 〜がち, 〜やすい, or 〜かねない: ともすれば油断しがちだ = one is apt to grow careless. The variant ともすると has the same meaning. It flags a pull toward a certain (often negative) outcome, not a one-time event.

synonyms.note: がち is the suffix 'tends to ~' on a verb or noun; ともすれば is the adverb that sets up such a tendency, often with がち itself.
嫌いがある states that something has a (negative) tendency as a trait; ともすれば frames a liability to slip that way under certain conditions.

related.note: 〜やすい says an action is easy to do or happen; ともすれば adds the sense of a worrying pull toward it.

meanings: is (formally) set as; has become; stands as ~
structure: Topic ＋ は ＋ Noun ＋ となっている
Sentence［plain form］＋ こととなっている
explanation: 〜となっている presents something as an established, official state — a rule, schedule, or settled result — in a formal, impersonal tone. 受付は10時からとなっております = reception is set from 10. It is like になっている but more formal, and is common in announcements, documents, and signs. The 〜は marks what the arrangement is about.

related.note: なる marks a change into a new state; 〜となっている presents the resulting state as an established, formal arrangement.
ことになる settles that something has been decided; 〜となっている states the standing arrangement in formal, notice-like language.
〜ている marks an ongoing state; となっている is that state framed formally as an official arrangement.

explanation: Politely suggests doing something together, or offers to do something. Replace the ます of a verb's polite form with ましょう. It invites the listener into an action you assume they will happily agree to, so it sounds confident and upbeat.

meanings: daringly; deliberately; going out of one's way (to do something difficult or usually avoided)
structure: 敢えて＋Verb［plain negative］［choose not to; not bother to ~］
explanation: 敢えて marks that the speaker knowingly does something difficult, risky, or normally avoided, choosing it on purpose despite reasons not to. あえて言う = dare to say it (even if unwelcome), あえて反対する = deliberately raise an objection. Paired with a negative, あえて〜ない means 'not go out of one's way to ~ / not bother': あえて口を出さない = choose not to interfere. The core nuance is a conscious decision against the easier or expected course.

synonyms.note: わざと is 'deliberately, on purpose' (often to produce an effect on someone); あえて is 'daring to' do something difficult or normally avoided.

variants.explanation: Verb stem + かねる means the speaker cannot, or finds it difficult to, do something. It very often works as a polite refusal — お答えしかねます softens a 'no'. It is not physical impossibility but an inability or reluctance given the circumstances, and it belongs to formal, business-like speech.

synonyms.note: がたい also means 'hard to do' (理解しがたい), often about judgment or emotion; かねる leans toward being unable to, and to polite refusals.

related.note: かねない is the negation of かねる but has shifted to mean 'might well (do something bad)' rather than 'be unable to'.
にくい describes something being physically hard to do (書きにくい); かねる is more about inability or reluctance in a situation.

meanings: I'll do ~ (and show them); to demonstrate by actually doing ~
explanation: 〜てみせる has two related senses. Literally it means performing an action to show someone how — お手本を書いてみせる = write it out to demonstrate. More pointedly, with volitional force it declares firm determination to accomplish something, often to prove others wrong: 必ず成功してみせる = I'll succeed, just you watch. The determination reading is emphatic and self-assertive, common in resolutions and challenges.

synonyms.note: 〜てやる can also express defiant determination ('I'll show them / just you wait'); てみせる adds the nuance of proving it before others' eyes.

related.note: 〜てみる is 'try doing ~ (to see how it goes)'; てみせる is 'do ~ to show someone' or 'vow to pull it off' — resolve, not tentative trying.

meanings: when it comes to ~; if it comes to the point that ~
structure: Verb［plain form］＋となると／となれば
explanation: 〜となると・〜となれば marks that once a matter becomes a real or serious prospect, a fitting reaction or consequence follows — 'when it actually comes to ~'. 留学するとなると、費用がかかる = if it comes to studying abroad, it costs money. It attaches to a noun, a plain-form verb, or a whole clause. The nuance is that raising the matter to a concrete stage changes what is required or how one feels about it.

synonyms.note: ともなると・にもなると adds that the level or rank reached is notably high; となると is the neutral 'when it comes to'.

related.note: と言えば raises a topic by association ('speaking of ~'); となると focuses on the consequences of a matter becoming real.

meanings: again; once more; a second time
explanation: 再び is an adverb meaning 'again' or 'once more'. It is more formal and written than the everyday また, and often appears in narration, news, or serious contexts. Place it before the verb or clause that repeats.

related.note: また can mean everyday 'again' as well as 'moreover'; 再び is the more formal, written word specifically for 'once more'.
もう一度 means 'one more time' as a fresh repetition; 再び is a single adverb for 'once more', often after a long gap.

meanings: B is more ~ than A
structure: Noun-A ＋ より ＋ Noun-B ＋ のほうが ＋ い-adjective／な-adjective
Noun-B ＋ のほうが ＋ Noun-A ＋ より ＋ い-adjective／な-adjective
explanation: Compares two things and states which one has more of a quality: "compared to A, B is more ~". A takes より ("than") and B takes のほうが ("the ~ side is more"). The order of the two parts is flexible, but the item marked のほうが is always the one that wins the comparison.

synonyms.note: は〜より…です makes the same comparison with A as the topic instead of のほうが on B.

related.note: より on its own is the "than" that this fuller pattern is built around.
一番 picks the single most out of three or more, not a two-way comparison.
〜の中で〜が一番 says which is the most within a group; this compares just two.

surface: までもない・までもなく
reading: までもない・までもなく
meanings: there is no need to go so far as to ~; it goes without saying
explanation: 〜までもない says an action isn't worth taking because the matter is too obvious or minor to require it — 'there's no need to go so far as to ~'. 言うまでもない = it goes without saying, わざわざ確認するまでもない = no need to bother checking. The 〜までもなく form links to a following clause: 説明するまでもなく = without even needing to explain.

synonyms.note: ことはない says 'there's no need to ~'; までもない adds that it isn't worth going so far because the point is obvious.
ほどのことではない downplays how serious a matter is; までもない says an action is superfluous given how self-evident the point is.

related.note: までだ ('merely ~') is a different までだ construction expressing resolve or justification.

meanings: in stark contrast to; unlike
explanation: 〜に引き換え sets two things side by side and draws a sharp, often evaluative contrast — one side clearly better or worse than the other. 兄に引き換え弟は… = unlike the older brother, the younger one… It attaches to a noun (or なの＋に引き換え after a clause). Unlike the neutral に対して, 〜に引き換え carries the speaker's judgment that the two differ markedly.

synonyms.note: に反して means 'contrary to (an expectation)'; に引き換え contrasts two comparable things with an evaluative slant.
に対して is a neutral 'whereas / in contrast'; に引き換え adds the speaker's judgment that one side compares poorly.

meanings: without a doubt; there is no mistaking
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋ に相違ない
explanation: に相違ない expresses the speaker's firm, reasoned conviction that something must be true — 'without a doubt; there's no mistaking it'. It is the formal, written-style counterpart of に違いない, common in essays, legal, and literary contexts.

synonyms.note: に違いない is the ordinary 'must be, no doubt'; に相違ない is its formal, written-register twin.
に決まっている is a casual, emotional 'obviously'; に相違ない is a formal, reasoned 'without a doubt'.

related.note: はずだ is a logical expectation open to revision; に相違ない asserts near-certainty with no room for doubt.

meanings: not hard to (imagine, guess, surmise)
explanation: 〜に難くない means that something takes no effort to imagine or infer — 'it is not hard to ~'. In practice it combines with only a few verbs, above all 想像する and 察する: 想像に難くない = not hard to imagine, 察するに難くない = not hard to surmise. It is used to say that a feeling or situation can readily be understood. The register is formal and literary.

meanings: about; concerning; regarding
explanation: について marks the topic you speak, write, or think about — 'about / concerning ~'. この町の歴史について調べる ('research about this town's history'). Before a noun, add の — その問題についての意見 ('an opinion about that problem'). It is the everyday way to name a subject.

meanings: namely; that is to say; in other words
explanation: すなわち restates what came just before, more precisely — "namely," "that is," "in other words." It equates two things, where the second is a clearer or more exact version of the first. It's formal and common in writing, explanations, and definitions.

synonyms.note: つまり sums up or rephrases in a casual tone; すなわち equates the two precisely and more formally.

related.note: 要するに boils a long point down to its gist; すなわち restates one thing as an equivalent.

meanings: have no choice but to ~; cannot help ~ing
structure: Verb［ない form, drop ない］＋ ざるを得ない
する → せざるを得ない
explanation: 〜ざるを得ない attaches to a verb's ない-form base to say the speaker is forced by circumstances into the action, often reluctantly — 認めざるを得ない = have no choice but to admit it. Formal in tone, with する → せざるを得ない.

synonyms.note: よりほかない also means 'nothing to do but'; ざるを得ない stresses reluctant compulsion by circumstance.
ないわけにはいかない is 'can't not do', driven by duty or social obligation; ざるを得ない is driven by unavoidable circumstances.
〜しかない is a plainer, more colloquial 'have no choice but'; ざるを得ない is more formal.

related.note: 〜ざる is the classical negative base on which this fixed pattern is built.

structure: Verb［た form］＋ 甲斐がある
Noun ＋ の ＋ 甲斐がある
explanation: 甲斐がある says that an effort was worthwhile because it produced a good result. It commonly attaches to a past-tense verb or a noun + の, and often appears in the connective form 甲斐があって ('thanks to the effort, ...'). かい means the worth or reward of what one put in.

meanings: to continue doing; to keep doing
explanation: 〜続ける attaches to the ます-stem to say an action keeps going without stopping — 走り続ける = keep running, 待ち続ける = keep waiting. It focuses on carrying one action on and on. The compound conjugates like a る-verb (続けた, 続けて).

antonyms.note: 〜続ける keeps an action going; 〜終わる ends it once it's done.

related.note: 〜始める marks the start of the action that 〜続ける then keeps going.

meanings: to do all the way through; to see through to the end (despite hardship)
explanation: 〜抜く attaches to the ます-stem and says an action was carried all the way to the end, usually against difficulty — 走り抜く = run all the way through, 考え抜く = think something through completely, やり抜く = see it through to the finish. The nuance is persistence and endurance, not mere completion. It conjugates as an う-verb (抜いた, 抜いて).

〜通す means 'keep doing all the way through'; 抜く adds the sense of pushing through difficulty to the end.

related.note: 〜終わる neutrally marks finishing an action; 抜く adds the effort and endurance of reaching the end.

meanings: to the extent that; so ~ that; about (an amount)
explanation: ほど marks a degree or extent — it sets a vivid yardstick for how far a state goes: 立てないほど疲れた = 'so tired I couldn't stand.' The clause before ほど paints how extreme the situation is. After a number, ほど means 'about' (三十分ほど), much like くらい.

synonyms.note: くらい／ぐらい also marks extent and approximate amount and often swaps in for ほど; ほど is favored for a striking upper-limit yardstick.

related.note: ば〜ほど is 'the more... the more'; plain ほど here marks a single degree or extent.
ほど〜ない uses the same word in a comparison to mean 'not as... as'.

surface: からすると・からすれば
reading: からすると・からすれば
meanings: judging from; from the standpoint of; considering
structure: Noun ＋ からすると／からすれば
explanation: Noun + からすると / からすれば presents the basis or standpoint of a judgment — 'going by X' or 'from X's point of view'. It may take a piece of evidence (この様子からすると) or a person's perspective (親からすれば), and the main clause states the conclusion drawn from it.

synonyms.note: から見ると frames the same idea as a viewpoint one 'looks from'; からすると is essentially interchangeable in the 'judging from' sense.
からして also means 'judging from', but additionally has an 'even (to begin with)' use that からすると does not.

related.note: によると cites a source of information ('according to'); からすると draws the speaker's own inference from evidence or a standpoint.

meanings: now that; since; given that
explanation: 〜以上は presents an established fact as firm grounds, so that a fitting resolve, duty, or natural conclusion follows — 'now that ~, since ~'. 引き受けた以上は = now that I've taken it on, 約束した以上は = since I promised. The second clause typically expresses determination, obligation, or an inevitable consequence rather than a neutral remark.

synonyms.note: からには is very close in meaning and more common in speech; 以上は is somewhat more formal.
上は also means 'now that', but is more literary and follows a verb of decision or action already taken.

variants.explanation: 〜を禁じ得ない takes an emotion noun and says one cannot forbid it welling up: 涙を禁じ得ない = can't hold back tears; 怒りを禁じ得ない = can't suppress anger. 禁じ得ない literally means 'cannot forbid (in oneself)'. It is distinctly formal, appearing in written and formal-spoken contexts, and describes a feeling that arises naturally in the speaker or as a general human reaction.

synonyms.note: ざるを得ない = have no choice but to (do an action); を禁じ得ない = cannot suppress (an emotion) — different objects.

related.note: 〜に堪えない (感慨に堪えない) also expresses an overwhelming feeling; を禁じ得ない specifically frames it as an emotion one cannot hold back.

meanings: to tell / ask someone to do ~
structure: Verb［dictionary form］／Verb［ない form］＋ ように ＋ 言う／頼む／伝える
explanation: ように言う reports an instruction or request passed to someone: the ように clause holds what they were told to do, and 言う (or 頼む, 伝える) delivers it. It is the standard way to relay a command indirectly, without quoting the exact words.

related.note: ように〜てほしい voices your own wish; ように言う reports an instruction given to someone.
ように祈る hopes for an outcome; ように言う relays a command.

meanings: without ~; without doing ~
explanation: 〜なしに and 〜なしで attach to a noun to mean 'without ~': 予告なしに = without warning, 許可なしで = without permission. With a verb they take こと first (〜することなしに). なしに tends to feel a little more formal or written than the everyday なしで, but both simply state that the expected thing was absent from the action.

synonyms.note: 〜なし is the bare noun suffix ('no ~'); なしに／なしで turn it into an adverbial 'without ~' modifying the action.
ことなしに is exactly the verb-taking form of this pattern ('without doing ~').

related.note: なくしては makes the same 'without' emphatic and ties it to an impossible result; なしに／なしで stay neutral.

meanings: as if!; there's no way ~; I'll never ~ (emphatic denial)
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋ ものか／もんか
な-adjective／Noun ＋ な ＋ ものか／もんか
explanation: 〜ものか (casual もんか) is an emphatic rhetorical negation — the speaker forcefully denies or refuses. 負けるものか = 'as if I'd lose! / I'll never lose'. It expresses defiant determination or scorn, roughly 'there's no way that…'. It is a spoken pattern; もんか is the most colloquial.

synonyms.note: わけがない objectively states 'there's no way'; ものか adds the speaker's defiant emotion and refusal.
はずがない denies on logical grounds; ものか is a heated, personal 'as if!'.

meanings: particle: to, at, in (destination, time, location)
explanation: One of the busiest N5 particles. に marks a point in time when something happens, the destination of movement, and the place where a person or thing exists. In every case it pins the sentence to a specific point — a moment, an endpoint, or a location of being.

related.note: へ also marks a destination and is often interchangeable with に for 'to a place'.
で marks where an action takes place; に marks existence or a destination.
Counting how often within a period (週に二回) is a separate N4 use of に.

meanings: per; in (X times per a period)
variants.explanation: This に marks a period of time as the base for a frequency: 'X times per that period'. The pattern is [time span] に [number + counter]: 一週間に三回 = three times a week, 一日に二回 = twice a day. The time span comes first with に, then the count of how often within it.

related.note: ごとに means 'every / at each ~'; the frequency に states how many times within one period.
おきに sets the interval between occurrences; this に sets how often per a fixed period.
The base particle に has many roles; this is its 'per (period)' frequency sense.

meanings: for (a whole stretch of ~); over the entire period of
explanation: When 〜というもの follows a length of time, it stresses that throughout that whole span a state continued — 'for the entire ~, all through ~'. ここ一か月というもの = all through this past month, ここ十年というもの = for these ten years now. It emphasizes how long and unbroken the period felt, usually alongside a description of an ongoing state or feeling, and it attaches to time expressions, often with ここ or この.

related.note: というものだ passes an emphatic 'that's just how ~ is' judgment; というもの after a time span instead stresses the unbroken length of the period.
間 neutrally marks 'during / while'; というもの adds emotional emphasis on how long that whole stretch dragged on.

meanings: while also; combining the purpose of; partly in order to
explanation: 〜かたがた marks that a single action serves two purposes at once — the main one, plus the かたがた one done along with it. It attaches to a noun, almost always a formal social act such as 挨拶かたがた (partly to pay one's respects), お礼かたがた (partly to say thanks), or お詫びかたがた (partly to apologize). The tone is stiff and old-fashioned, at home in letters and polite visits. One deed accomplishes both aims.

synonyms.note: がてら does two things on one outing too, but is more casual and often involves physically going somewhere; かたがた is formal and noun-only.

related.note: ついでに frames the second action as an afterthought taken while doing the first; かたがた presents both purposes as intended together, in stiffer register.
かたわら pairs two sustained activities over a long span; かたがた joins two purposes in one single act.

meanings: therefore; consequently; accordingly (formal)
explanation: したがって is a formal conjunction that draws a logical conclusion from what precedes — 'therefore, accordingly'. 需要が増えた。したがって、価格も上がった = demand rose; therefore prices went up too. Common in academic and business writing.

synonyms.note: ゆえに is an even more literary 'therefore'; したがって is standard formal register.

related.note: しかしながら is the formal contrastive conjunction ('however'); したがって is its conclusive counterpart.

meanings: and so; because of that; so then?
explanation: それで opens a sentence and links it to the previous one as its result: 熱があった。それで、休んだ = 'I had a fever. So I stayed home.' In conversation a bare それで？ nudges the other person to continue the story: 'and then?'.

related.note: それから is plain time sequence ('after that'); それで is cause and result.
ので joins reason and result inside one sentence; それで links them across two.
そして simply continues the story; それで says the next part happened because of the last.

meanings: in the case that ~; in the event of ~
explanation: 場合 means 'case' or 'situation', and 〜場合は presents a hypothetical situation and states what to do if it arises. It attaches to plain forms of verbs and adjectives, な-adjective＋な, and noun＋の. Common in rules, manuals, and official notices: 'in the case that A, (do) B'.

related.note: たら is the everyday 'if/when'; 場合は is the formal wording used in rules and notices.
とき marks the time an event actually happens; 場合は sets up a hypothetical situation to prepare for.
なら picks up a topic just raised; 場合は presents a condition on its own terms.

meanings: even if; even though; even supposing ~
explanation: にしても grants a point and then pushes back against it — 'even if ~ / even supposing ~'. 行くにしても準備に時間がかかる ('even if we go, prep takes time'), 冗談にしてもひどい ('even as a joke, that's awful'). You accept the situation for the sake of argument, then state something that still holds.

related.note: にしろ〜にしろ pairs two cases 'whether A or B'; にしても concedes a single point.
いずれにしても means 'in any case, whichever it is'; にしても concedes one specific supposition.
にしては judges a result against a standard ('for ~'); にしても concedes 'even if ~'.

meanings: 気 expressions: mind, feeling, inclination (気がする, 気になる, 気にする, and more)
explanation: 気 ('mind, spirit, feeling') forms a large family of set expressions about one's mental state: 気がする (have a feeling), 気になる (be bothered or curious), 気にする (mind, worry about), 気をつける (be careful), 気が済む (feel satisfied). The noun 気 combines with a fixed particle and verb in each idiom to describe feelings and inclinations.

related.note: が気になる is one specific member: something weighs on your mind or draws your curiosity.
ような気がする is the fixed pattern 'have a feeling that ~', built from 気がする.
に気をつける ('be careful about ~') is another everyday idiom in the 気 family.

meanings: let's ...; why don't we ... (formal exhortation)
structure: Verb［volitional］＋ ではないか／じゃないか
explanation: 〜ようではないか is a formal, rhetorical exhortation built on the volitional — 'let us ~, shall we not ~'. The speaker calls on the listeners to join in an action, so it is common in speeches, editorials, and appeals. ようじゃないか is the more colloquial variant of the same call to action.

related.note: じゃないか seeks the listener's agreement ('isn't it?'); ようではないか builds on the volitional to urge joint action.
ようと思う is one's private intention to act; ようではないか openly rallies others to act together.

surface: そうもない・そうにない
reading: そうもない・そうにない
meanings: very unlikely to; showing no sign of (happening)
structure: Verb［stem］＋ そうもない／そうにない
explanation: This is the negative of the "looks like / seems" そう. Added to a verb stem, そうもない・そうにない says something shows no sign of happening — it looks very unlikely. 雨がやみそうにない = the rain doesn't look like it'll stop. It's your read of how things look, not a flat statement of fact.

antonyms.note: そうだ (appearance) says something looks likely to happen; そうにない is its "looks unlikely" negative.

related.note: そうな／そうに modifies with a "looks like ~" impression; そうにない is the negative "looks like it won't."
〜かねない warns something bad might well happen; そうもない says something looks very unlikely to.

meanings: already; now; (with a negative) no longer
explanation: もはや is a formal, somewhat literary adverb marking that a decisive, often irreversible point has been reached. With an affirmative predicate it means 'now, by this point, already' — もはや手遅れだ = it is already too late, もはや過去のものだ = it is now a thing of the past. With a negative it means 'no longer' — もはや戻れない = we can no longer go back. It is weightier and more formal than the everyday もう.

meanings: it's not that ~; it doesn't mean that ~ (partial denial)
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋ というわけではない
explanation: というわけではない softly denies a conclusion the listener might draw — 'it's not that ~ / it doesn't mean that ~'. 嫌いというわけではない = 'it's not that I dislike it (I just...)'. It corrects a likely misunderstanding without denying everything, so it is a hedged, partial negation.

related.note: からといって ('just because ~') often sets up the assumption that というわけではない then denies.
というものではない denies a general 'X always leads to Y' rule; というわけではない denies one specific conclusion.

explanation: Attached to a verb stem, 〜そびれる means you intended to do something but the timing slipped away, so it never got done — 言いそびれる = miss one's chance to say, 食べそびれる = miss out on eating. The nuance is regret over a lost opportunity rather than being unable in principle.

synonyms.note: 損なう also means 'fail to / miss doing', but additionally covers doing something incorrectly; そびれる is only about a missed chance.

meanings: if ~ (a bad result follows); whenever ~
explanation: ては joins the て-form with は to set up a condition whose consequence is usually undesirable — 急いでは失敗する = 'if you rush, you'll fail'. It presents the action as a recurring or ongoing cause and leads into a negative outcome. In casual speech it contracts to ちゃ (or じゃ after voiced sounds).

synonyms.note: たら is a neutral 'if / when ~'; ては specifically frames the condition as leading to an unwanted result.
と states a natural or automatic consequence; ては highlights the condition as the cause of something bad.

related.note: ていては is the ている version, stressing that a continuing action or state brings the bad result.

meanings: taking advantage of; exploiting (a favorable situation)
explanation: 〜をいいことに marks a favorable circumstance that someone exploits to do something they arguably shouldn't. It carries clear criticism: 親が留守なのをいいことに = taking advantage of the parents being out. A noun takes を directly; a clause is nominalized with の first (いないのをいいことに). The speaker disapproves of the person for seizing on the situation.

surface: ともなく・ともなしに
reading: ともなく・ともなしに
meanings: without particular intention; from no definite ~
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋ともなく／ともなしに＋（same verb）
explanation: 〜ともなく・〜ともなしに has two uses. With an action verb it repeats the verb to mean doing it without conscious intent — 見るともなく見る = look without really meaning to, absent-mindedly. With a question word it means 'from/at no definite ~': どこからともなく = from somewhere or other, 誰からともなく = from no one in particular. Despite the ない-like なしに, it is not a plain negative form.

meanings: even though; and yet (with blame or scorn)
structure: な-adjective ＋ な ＋ くせして
explanation: くせして is a colloquial, blunter variant of くせに. It joins two clauses where the second clashes with what the first would lead you to expect, and it carries criticism, contempt, or complaint aimed at the subject — 知っているくせして教えてくれない = knows it, and yet won't tell me. synonyms.note: くせに is the same critical 'even though'; くせして is the more colloquial, often blunter form.

related.note: ながらも is a literary concessive 'although' with no scorn; くせして adds blame or contempt.

meanings: even without doing; even if not
explanation: 〜ずとも is a literary concessive: even without doing the verb, the main clause still holds. 言わずとも分かる = you needn't say it — I understand anyway. It is the classical equivalent of 〜なくても, built from the negative ず plus concessive とも, and する becomes せずとも. Today it appears in written style, formal speech, and set turns of phrase, lending a dignified or aphoristic ring.

synonyms.note: 〜なくても is the everyday equivalent; ずとも says the same in classical, written style.

related.note: までもない judges an action unnecessary ('no need to'); ずとも concedes its absence and moves on.
ことなしに states that something happens without the action; ずとも concedes 'even if it doesn't happen'.

meanings: seeing as ~; given one's position before others
explanation: 手前 as a grammar pattern means 'because of one's standing or appearance in front of others, one has to ~'. Following a noun + の or a plain-form verb, it gives a reason rooted in pride, face, or obligation toward the people watching — 約束した手前 = 'having promised (and with others aware), I can't back out'. The following clause states what one must or cannot do to save face.

synonyms.note: 以上は gives a logical 'now that ~, naturally ~'; 手前 grounds the obligation specifically in appearances before others.
からには means 'now that / so long as ~', stressing resolve; 手前 stresses saving face in front of people.

related.note: 上は means 'now that ~ (I've done it), I must ~'; 手前 adds the specific motive of pride or appearances.

meanings: considering ~; for ~; despite ~ (more/less than expected)
explanation: 割に（は） compares something against a standard or expectation and points out that reality doesn't match it — X considering Y, or X despite Y. 値段の割においしい = tasty for the price. It weighs an amount or degree against what the first part would lead you to expect, and flags the gap.

synonyms.note: のに simply marks 'although X, unexpectedly Y'; 割に weighs the result against the level X would lead you to expect.
くせに also flags an unexpected mismatch but adds blame or scorn; 割に stays neutral.

antonyms.note: だけあって says the result fits the standard ('just as you'd expect from X'); 割に says it runs against that standard.

meanings: completely; (not) at all; utterly
explanation: まるっきり is a colloquial, emphatic adverb. Most often it pairs with a negative to mean 'not in the slightest' — まるっきり分からない = don't understand at all. With an affirmative it means 'completely, utterly', typically stressing total difference or total lack: まるっきり別人 = a completely different person, まるっきりの素人 = a total amateur. It is rougher and more spoken than まったく or まるで, and carries a note of exasperation.

synonyms.note: まるで also intensifies a negative ('not at all'), but additionally means 'as if ~'; まるっきり is purely emphatic and more colloquial.

related.note: とても〜ない says something is impossible/unthinkable; まるっきり〜ない simply denies it totally, without the 'no way could it' nuance.

meanings: the way one wants/expects (very often used in the negative)
explanation: 思うように means 'as one wishes / as one expects things to go'. In practice it appears most often with a negative verb — 思うようにいかない, 思うようにできない — to say that things are not going the way one had hoped, usually with a note of frustration.

synonyms.note: 通りに (as in 思った通り) also means 'as expected', but is neutral; 思うように leans toward whether things go as one wishes, often in the negative.

meanings: and; as well as (formal listing conjunction between nouns)
explanation: 及び is a formal conjunction that joins nouns or noun phrases in the sense of 'and'. It belongs to written, official registers — application forms, laws, notices, business documents — where と or や would sound too casual. It connects items in a list, not clauses.

related.note: 又は is the same formal register but means 'or' (choose one); 及び joins items together as 'and'.
あるいは offers an alternative ('or; or else'); 及び adds items to the same list.

meanings: setting ~ aside; apart from ~; leaving aside whether ~
structure: Sentence＋ かどうか ＋ は別として
explanation: は別として sets one matter aside as a separate issue so you can turn to the main point — 'putting X to one side, ...'. It attaches to a noun, and with a yes/no question it becomes 〜かどうかは別として ('leaving aside whether...'). It doesn't exclude members from a group; it just brackets off a topic for now.

synonyms.note: はともかく is very close in meaning ('setting aside'); は別として leans a little more on treating the matter as a distinct, separate issue.

related.note: 以外 excludes items from a set ('other than X'); は別として brackets a topic off to focus elsewhere.
ならともかく means 'if it were X, fine, but...'; は別として simply sets X aside without that conditional contrast.

meanings: i-adjective past tense
structure: い-adjective［drop い］＋ かった ＋ です［polite］
explanation: To put an い-adjective into the past, drop the final い and add かった: 高い→高かった (was expensive), 楽しい→楽しかった (was fun). It works both as the sentence predicate (楽しかったです) and when describing a past state. In polite speech, add です after かった — never でした.

related.note: 〜くない is the negative of the same い-adjectives (past: 〜くなかった).
だった・でした is the past for nouns and な-adjectives, where い-adjectives use 〜かった.
The same い-adjectives can modify a noun directly in their non-past form.

meanings: should; ought to (the right or proper thing to do)
structure: する → するべき／すべき
explanation: べきだ says something is the right, proper, or expected thing to do — a firm sense of what one ought to do, based on principle or common sense. It attaches to the dictionary form of a verb. With する, both するべき and すべき are used.

synonyms.note: 方がいい is a softer 'you'd better'; べきだ is a firmer statement of what is right or proper.

antonyms.note: べきではない is the negative — 'should not', the improper thing to do.

related.note: なければならない is unavoidable obligation ('must'); べきだ is about what is right or advisable.
はずだ is 'ought to be' as an expectation about facts; べきだ is 'ought to do' as a judgment about proper action.

meanings: in one's own way; in a manner fitting to ~
explanation: 〜なりに (adverbial) and 〜なりの (before a noun) mean 'in a way befitting the person or thing, within its own means': 私なりに考えた = I thought it over in my own way, 子供なりの理屈 = a child's own kind of logic. structure: Verb［dictionary form］／Verb［ない form］＋ ように ＋ Verb［て form］＋ ほしい

variants.explanation: Advises against doing something: attach ほうがいい to the ない form of a verb to say "it would be better not to do ~". It is a gentle recommendation, softer than telling someone they must not do something.

antonyms.note: ほうがいい recommends doing something; ないほうがいい advises against it.

related.note: てはいけない forbids an action outright; ないほうがいい only gently advises against it.

meanings: everything up to and including; (extending) even to ~
explanation: 〜に至るまで stresses that a range reaches all the way to an extreme, minor, or surprising endpoint — 'from ~ right down to ~'. It commonly pairs with から: 服装から言葉遣いに至るまで = everything from clothing down to word choice. The point is that even the far or trivial end is covered, which plain まで does not emphasize. It is a formal expression.

related.note: まで marks a plain endpoint; に至るまで adds that the range reaches even an extreme or unexpected far end.
から〜にかけて spans a rough range over time or space; から〜に至るまで stresses that even the extreme endpoint is included.

meanings: if; if it's the case that ~
explanation: なら sets up a condition by picking up something just mentioned or assumed: 'if (we're talking about) ~, then ...'. It attaches straight to a noun or to the plain form of a verb or adjective. Its special job is responding to a topic the other person raised — 'if that's what you mean, then here's my point'.

related.note: たら is a general 'if/when' about what happens next; なら takes up a topic and reacts to it.
と states an automatic result; なら frames a supposition raised in the conversation.
ば gives a hypothetical condition; なら responds to a premise you accept for the sake of argument.
