surface: にかぎったことではない
reading: にかぎったことではない
meanings: not limited to only ~; not something confined to ~
structure: Noun＋に限ったことではない
explanation: 〜に限ったことではない denies that a matter is unique to the named case — 'it is not something limited to ~'. 残業が多いのはこの業界に限ったことではない = heavy overtime is not something confined to this industry. It usually implies the phenomenon is in fact more widespread, and often carries a note that it is a broader problem. The noun is marked with に.

synonyms.note: に限らず means 'not just ~ but also (more widely)'; に限ったことではない flatly denies that the matter is exclusive to the named case.

antonyms.note: に限って pinpoints one case as special ('of all times/things, precisely ~'); に限ったことではない denies any such exclusivity.

related.note: のみならず means 'not only ~ but also'; に限ったことではない simply denies that something is unique to one case.

meanings: I heard that ~
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋ と聞いた／と聞いています
explanation: 〜と聞いた reports information you got from someone: 'I heard that ~'. The plain statement before と is what you were told, and 聞いた marks it as something you personally heard secondhand.

synonyms.note: 〜そうだ also relays hearsay; 〜と聞いた stresses that you yourself heard it.

related.note: 〜と言われている is what people in general say; 〜と聞いた is what you were told.
Both take a plain-form clause plus と; 聞いた reports hearing, 思う reports thinking.

reading: をつうじて・をとおして

meanings: causative-passive: to be made to do
structure: Godan verb［ない form: ない → せられる／される］
Ichidan verb［ない form: ない → させられる］
する → させられる ／ くる → こさせられる
explanation: させられる stacks the passive onto the causative to say the subject was made to do something by someone else, usually unwillingly: 食べさせられた = 'I was made to eat it'. The person who forces the action is marked with に.

related.note: せる・させる is the plain causative; させられる shifts the viewpoint to the person who is forced.
られる alone is the plain passive; させられる adds that the action was compelled.

meanings: quite; considerably; (with a negative) just won't ~
structure: なかなか ＋ Verb［ない form］
explanation: なかなか has two everyday jobs. Before an affirmative word it means 'quite / considerably', often with a touch of surprise that something beats your expectations — なかなかおいしい = surprisingly tasty. Before a negative verb (なかなか〜ない) it means the action is slow or hard to happen — 'just won't ~' — as in バスがなかなか来ない ('the bus just won't come'). Read the polarity of the sentence to tell the two uses apart.

synonyms.note: けっこう also means 'quite / fairly' but is plainer, without なかなか's note of pleasant surprise.

related.note: The dedicated negative pattern なかなか〜ない ('just won't ~'); here it is the affirmative 'quite' use.

meanings: being too absorbed in ~ (and neglecting other things)
explanation: 〜にかまけて marks being so preoccupied with one thing that other things get neglected — 'caught up in ~, too taken up with ~'. 仕事にかまけて家庭を顧みない = so absorbed in work that one neglects the family. It is inherently negative: the following clause states what was let slide. It attaches to a noun and belongs to a somewhat formal, self-reflective register.

related.note: にかこつけて uses something as a deliberate excuse; にかまけて is genuine over-absorption that causes unintended neglect.

meanings: when it comes to (this extreme case); as for (of all things)
explanation: 〜に至っては singles out the most extreme or worst example among several and comments on it, usually with dismay or criticism. After listing so-so cases, it picks the one that goes furthest — 兄はまだしも、弟に至っては = the older brother is one thing, but as for the younger one. What follows is typically how bad or hopeless that case is. It is a formal expression built on 至る ('to reach').

synonyms.note: となると shifts to 'when it comes to ~' neutrally; に至っては adds that this is the worst, most extreme case.

related.note: に至る is the base verb 'to reach (an extreme point)'; に至っては applies that framing to pick out one glaring example.
に至っても means 'even after reaching (that extreme), still ~'; に至っては instead singles out the extreme case for comment.

meanings: toward (a target); in contrast to ~
explanation: に対して has two jobs. It aims an action or feeling at a target — お客様に対して丁寧に話す ('speak politely toward customers'). It also sets two things in contrast — 兄が明るいのに対して弟は静かだ ('in contrast to the cheerful older brother, the younger one is quiet'). Before a noun, use に対する.

related.note: に比べて weighs one thing against a baseline; に対して sets two things side by side in contrast.
に反して means 'contrary to (what was expected)'; に対して's contrast sense is a neutral 'whereas'.
に向かって is aiming at a physical direction; に対して aims an action or attitude at a target.

meanings: can't help feeling ~; ~ terribly
explanation: てならない follows the て-form to say a feeling or impression wells up beyond the speaker's control — 気になってならない = 'I can't help worrying', 思えてならない = 'I can't help feeling that ...'. It often attaches to verbs of spontaneous thought and emotion. Similar to てたまらない, it leans somewhat formal and is especially common with 気がする, 思える, and the like.

synonyms.note: てたまらない stresses a feeling almost too strong to bear; てならない stresses a feeling that arises on its own and won't stop.
てしょうがない is the more casual 'can't help ~'; てならない is somewhat more formal and literary.

meanings: the height of; extreme (emotion); the utmost of
explanation: 〜の至り expresses that an emotion is felt at its utmost — 光栄の至り = the greatest of honors, 感激の至り = deeply moved beyond words. It attaches to a small set of emotion nouns and belongs to very formal, ceremonial or humble speech. The fixed phrase 若気の至り ('the folly of youth') is a notable exception, naming a rash act driven by youthful impulse.

synonyms.note: の極み marks a state pushed to its limit (贅沢・混乱); の至り is reserved for emotions at their peak in humble set phrases.
限りだ also expresses an emotion at its extreme (うれしい限りだ); の至り is more formal and attaches to emotion nouns.

meanings: as for why…; the reason is…
structure: なぜ ＋ Sentence［plain form］＋ かというと ＋ …からだ
explanation: なぜ〜かというと sets up a question — typically 'why?' — and then answers it, a smooth way to introduce an explanation. It usually closes with からだ／のだ. Think of it as 'if you ask why…, it's because…'.

related.note: Same shape, but that one hedges a choice ('if anything'); this one answers a 'why' question.
ので states a reason directly; かというと first raises the why-question, then answers it.

meanings: not only ~ but also ~
structure: Noun ＋ だけでなく（て）、＋ Noun ＋ も
Sentence［plain form］＋ だけでなく（て）、〜も
explanation: だけでなく(て)〜も adds a second, often bigger item onto the first — "not only X but also Y." The も marks the added item. The なくて form is a touch more conversational than the plain なく.

meanings: before long; in time; eventually
explanation: やがて is an adverb meaning 'before long, in time, eventually'. It presents something as coming about through the natural passage of time — the situation moves toward the stated outcome without much delay. It has a narrative, written flavor and describes an approximate near future rather than a fixed time.

related.note: ついに marks an endpoint reached at last, often after long effort; やがて is 'before long', stressing a smooth passage of time.
結局 sums up how things turned out in the end; やがて simply says the next stage arrives soon.

meanings: whether or not
explanation: 〜か否か is the formal, written equivalent of 〜かどうか — 'whether or not'. 実現できるか否か = whether or not it can be realized; 事実か否かを確かめる = verify whether or not it is true. 否 (いな) is a literary 'no', so the phrase reads as stiff and is common in essays, reports, and formal speech. It follows a plain form or a noun.

synonyms.note: 〜かどうか is the everyday 'whether or not'; か否か is its formal, literary equivalent.

meanings: and just then; thereupon; whereupon
structure: Sentence。＋ すると、＋ Sentence（and just then / thereupon）
explanation: すると links two events: right after the first, the second happened — often something the speaker observed, sometimes unexpected. ドアを開けた。すると、猫が飛び出してきた = I opened the door, whereupon a cat jumped out. It can also mean "if that's so, then…" in reaction to what was just said.

related.note: そうすると supposes doing "that" and gives the result; すると reports what actually followed.
The conditional と states a general "whenever A, then B"; すると connects two specific past events.
そこで is "and so" leading to a chosen next action; すると is "and just then" for what happened on its own.

explanation: 〜にくい attaches to the ます-stem and means an action is hard or troublesome to do — 食べにくい = hard to eat, 分かりにくい = hard to understand. It states the difficulty fairly neutrally and forms an い-adjective (にくかった, にくくない).

meanings: feel utterly ~; extremely (of an emotion)
explanation: 〜限りだ, after an emotion word, expresses that the speaker feels that emotion to the utmost — 'I couldn't be more ~'. 嬉しい限りだ = I couldn't be happier; 心細い限りだ = I feel utterly forlorn; 羨ましい限りだ = I'm terribly envious. It takes an い-adjective, or a な-adjective + な, of feeling and states the speaker's own emotion at its extreme. The tone is somewhat formal.

synonyms.note: 〜の至り expresses reaching the height of a feeling (formal, set phrases like 光栄の至り); 限りだ is a slightly less rigid 'utterly ~'.
〜の極み marks the extreme peak of a state (感激の極み); 限りだ centers the speaker's own emotion 'to the utmost'.

related.note: 〜極まりない says a quality is 'extreme beyond limit' (often negative); 限りだ voices a personal emotion at its height.

meanings: was; were (past copula)
explanation: The past tense of the copula: だった (plain) and でした (polite) turn "X is Y" into "X was Y". Attach it to a noun or な-adjective to describe how something was in the past. It is the natural counterpart to だ・です.

related.note: だ・です is the non-past copula "is"; だった・でした is its past form.
〜かった is the past of い-adjectives; でした follows nouns and な-adjectives.

It carries a pessimistic or self-deprecating coloring (どうせ私なんか = 'someone like me, after all'), but can also mean 'since it's going to happen anyway, might as well go all in'.

meanings: I wonder if ~; could it be that ~? (soft, polite question)
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋ のでしょうか
な-adjective／Noun ＋ なのでしょうか
explanation: のでしょうか softens a question by combining explanatory の with the tentative でしょう and question か. It makes you sound less blunt and more considerate — as if wondering aloud or gently seeking an explanation. どうして遅れたのでしょうか is a softer, more polite 'why were you late?' than 遅れたんですか. It is common when asking about reasons or circumstances.

related.note: でしょう alone guesses or seeks agreement; のでしょうか wraps a question in that same softness while asking for an explanation.
だろう is the plain-style guess; のでしょうか is the polite, question-form version used to ask gently.
explanatory の／んだ gives background or reasons; のでしょうか turns that explanatory tone into a soft question.

meanings: to concern; to affect; to have a serious bearing on
explanation: 〜に関わる means to have a weighty bearing on something important — life, honor, credibility, a future. 命に関わる = 'a matter of life and death'; 信用に関わる問題 = 'an issue that affects one's credibility'. It implies serious stakes, not a casual 'about', and often modifies the noun that follows.

related.note: に関して・に関する is the neutral 'concerning / about (a topic)'; に関わる implies a serious, high-stakes bearing.
について is a plain 'about ~'; に関わる means something critically affects the matter, not merely relates to it.
にかかわらず ('regardless of') shares the 関わ root but flips the grammar to 'no matter ~', not 'affects ~'.

meanings: a little less than; just under (suffix on a quantity)
explanation: Placed after a number, 〜弱 means 'a bit less than that figure'. It rounds up to a round number and signals that the true value sits slightly below it — 三千円弱 = just under 3,000 yen, 三割弱 = a little under 30%. Common in statistics and reports; its mirror is 〜強.

antonyms.note: 〜強 is the mirror suffix, marking a value slightly above the stated figure.

meanings: get by without doing; end up not having to do
structure: Verb［ない form］＋済む （〜なくて済む／〜ないで済む）
explanation: 〜なくて済む describes a situation that works out so that you are spared having to do something — usually a relief. 待たなくて済む = 'I don't have to wait after all'. It reports a fortunate outcome, not a decision or a rule; something about the situation removes the burden. The more formal written equivalent is 〜ずに済む.

synonyms.note: ずに済む carries the identical meaning in a more formal, written register.

antonyms.note: ずには済まない means you won't be able to get away without doing it; なくて済む means you are spared from having to.

related.note: なくてもいい grants permission not to do; なくて済む reports that circumstances happily removed the need.

meanings: one could even say that; it's not impossible to say ~
explanation: 〜と言えなくもない is a hedged, doubly-negative way of granting a point — 'you can't say it isn't ~, so in a sense it is'. It offers cautious, partial agreement: 成功と言えなくもない = you could, in a way, call it a success. The speaker admits the description has some validity while staying noncommittal, so it softens an assertion and usually implies reservations.

synonyms.note: ないでもない ('it's not that one doesn't ~') is the same reserved double negative applied to actions or feelings; と言えなくもない applies it to a description.

meanings: and; and then (verb linking)
explanation: The connective て form of a verb links it to what follows: "do A and (then) B". It joins actions in sequence within one sentence and is also the base for many other patterns (ている, てください, and more). Mastering how each verb group forms て is a core N5 skill.

related.note: てから stresses "after doing A, then B"; plain て just links the actions.
〜たり lists sample actions without order; て links them in sequence.
てください uses the て form to make a request; here て just connects clauses.

meanings: it doesn't (automatically) mean that ~; that doesn't make it ~
structure: Verb／Sentence［plain form］＋ ことにはならない

meanings: however; nevertheless; that said (formal)
structure: Sentence。 ＋ しかしながら、 ＋ Sentence
explanation: しかしながら is a formal conjunction meaning 'however / nevertheless'. It is a heavier, more written version of しかし, opening a sentence to introduce something that runs against what came before. Common in essays, speeches, and business correspondence.

related.note: ところが adds surprise ('but then, unexpectedly'); しかしながら is neutral, formal contrast.
したがって is the conclusive formal conjunction ('therefore'); しかしながら is its contrastive counterpart.

meanings: to fail to do; to miss doing; to do (something) wrong
explanation: Attached to a verb stem, 損なう / 損ねる / 損じる means you failed to complete an action or missed the chance — 乗り損なう = miss (fail to catch) the train, 言い損なう = fail to say. Note that 損なう / 損ねる can separately mean 'to damage or harm' (健康を損なう, 機嫌を損ねる).

synonyms.note: そびれる also means 'miss the chance to', but only for a missed opportunity; 損なう also covers doing something wrong.

related.note: かける means an action was begun but left unfinished; 損なう means it failed or misfired.

surface: なくはない・なくもない
reading: なくはない・なくもない
meanings: it's not that ... isn't; ... to some degree (understated affirmation)
structure: Verb［ない form → なく］＋は／も＋ない
explanation: 〜なくはない・〜なくもない is a reserved, hedged affirmation built from a double negative: 'it's not that there isn't ~', hence 'well, somewhat / I guess so'. 興味がなくはない = 'it's not that I have no interest'. The two negatives cancel into a mild, reluctant yes — weaker and more cautious than a plain affirmative.

synonyms.note: ないでもない is the same understated 'it's not that ... not', with the same reluctant nuance.

related.note: ないことはない leans toward 'it's not impossible / there is a way'; なくはない is more about a faint degree of feeling or agreement.
ないものでもない means 'it's not entirely out of the question'; both hedge, with ものでもない sounding more literary.

meanings: as soon as ~; depending on ~
explanation: 次第 has two jobs. After a verb stem it means "as soon as ~; the moment ~ is done" (連絡がつき次第 = as soon as I get in touch), and the following clause looks to the future — a plan or request. After a noun it means "depends on ~" (天気次第 = depends on the weather). It's a formal expression common in business and announcements.

related.note: 〜次第で extends the noun use to "depending on ~, the outcome varies."
次第に uses the same kanji but means "gradually" — a different point entirely.
〜たとたん is a spontaneous, often surprising past event; 次第 looks ahead to a planned action.

meanings: isn't there some way to ~? (a wistful, pondering wish)

explanation: 〜ないものだろうか expresses a heartfelt wish framed as quiet wondering: 'I wonder whether ~ couldn't somehow come about'. It attaches to a negated (usually potential-negative) predicate and often accompanies a wish the speaker feels is hard to realize but hopes for anyway.

surface: てもどうにもならない
reading: てもどうにもならない
meanings: it's no use even if ~; ~ won't help; nothing can be done even if ~

explanation: 〜てもどうにもならない says that even doing the stated thing changes nothing — the situation is beyond remedy. 今さら後悔してもどうにもならない = there's no use regretting it now. どうにもならない means 'nothing can be done about it', so the pattern declares the action futile against an unfixable situation. related.note: どうにも〜ない means '(cannot) ~ in any way at all'; てもどうにもならない is the fixed 'even if ~, nothing can be done'.

meanings: furthermore; in addition; even more
explanation: さらに adds more on top of what's already there. It has two uses: introducing an additional point ("furthermore, in addition") and raising a degree ("even more so"). さらに大きい = even bigger; 雨が降り、さらに風も出た = it rained, and on top of that the wind came up too.

synonyms.note: その上 also means "on top of that," but only adds a further item; さらに can also intensify a degree.

related.note: それに tacks on an extra point in casual speech; さらに is more formal and also does "even more."
〜に加えて adds "in addition to (a specific noun)"; さらに adds another clause on its own.

meanings: to do completely; to do (unfortunately, by accident)
structure: Verb［て form］＋ しまう／しまいます

explanation: てしまう adds one of two nuances: (1) completion — doing something fully, all the way through — or (2) regret — an action that turned out badly or happened by mistake. Context decides which. Casual contractions: 〜てしまう → 〜ちゃう, 〜でしまう → 〜じゃう.

meanings: as soon as; the moment that; no sooner ~ than
explanation: 〜や否や attaches to a dictionary-form verb to mean 'the instant that ~, no sooner ~ than': ベルが鳴るや否や = the moment the bell rang. The second clause reports what happened immediately and unexpectedly right after. It is a literary, written expression; the following clause states an actual past event, not a plan, request, or command.

synonyms.note: が早いか is likewise literary 'the moment ~', but stresses that the second action began almost before the first was even finished.
たとたん(に) also means 'the moment ~', often with surprise, but is less literary and follows the た-form.
〜なり means 'as soon as ~' where the same subject moves straight into the next action; や否や allows a different subject or an external event to follow.

related.note: と同時に means 'at the same time as ~' (simultaneity); や否や stresses immediate succession right after the first event.

meanings: now ~ now ~; alternately doing one thing and its opposite
explanation: A literary pattern that joins two verb stems (連用形) each with つ, describing two actions that alternate or play off one another — typically a pair of opposites. 行きつ戻りつ = pacing back and forth, 追いつ追われつ = chasing and being chased by turns. It survives mainly in set expressions, often pairing one active verb with its passive form. The tone is descriptive and literary, not everyday speech.

synonyms.note: 〜たり〜たり is the everyday way to list alternating or representative actions; つ〜つ is a frozen literary form confined to set opposite-verb pairs.

related.note: つつ ('while / although') marks one action accompanying another and is fully productive; the doubled つ〜つ is a separate fixed pattern for two alternating actions.

meanings: it is ~ that ~ (cleft sentence)
structure: Sentence［plain form］ ＋ の ＋ は ＋ Noun／Phrase ＋ だ
explanation: のは〜だ builds a cleft sentence that spotlights one part of the idea. Nominalize a clause with の, mark it with は as the known information, and end with the highlighted element plus だ: 私が生まれたのは北海道です = it was in Hokkaido that I was born. It answers 'which / where / who / when' by putting that answer in the だ slot.

related.note: The の in のは〜だ is the nominalizer, turning a whole clause into a noun that は can mark.
Explanatory んです explains a situation; のは〜だ instead singles out one element as the focus.

meanings: don't ~! (blunt, casual prohibition)
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋ んじゃない（よ）
explanation: Attached to a verb in the dictionary form, 〜んじゃない（よ） is a forceful, spoken way to tell someone not to do something — the tone a parent might use scolding a child. 泣くんじゃない = Don't cry! It is blunter and more emotional than a flat 〜てはいけない.

synonyms.note: 〜な (行くな) is the terse, blunt 'don't'; 〜んじゃない carries the same force with a more emotional, scolding tone.

related.note: 〜ちゃいけない states that something must not be done as a rule; 〜んじゃない is a heated, on-the-spot order to stop.
〜てはいけない is the standard 'must not'; 〜んじゃない is its rough, spoken, scolding cousin.

meanings: hard to bring oneself to; difficult (almost impossible) to do
explanation: 〜がたい attaches to the ます-stem and marks an action as hard, sometimes nearly impossible, to do — 信じがたい = hard to believe, 忘れがたい = unforgettable. It is formal and rather literary, and pairs with a limited set of verbs of thinking, feeling, and perception. The whole compound behaves like an い-adjective.

synonyms.note: 〜にくい is the everyday 'hard to do'; がたい is formal and limited to a few verbs of thought and perception.
〜づらい is 'hard/uncomfortable to do', often physical or social; がたい is a more abstract 'hard to bring oneself to'.

antonyms.note: 〜やすい 'easy to do' is the plain opposite of this difficulty family.

meanings: explanatory setup ＋ but; a soft lead-in
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋ んだけど／んですが

meanings: surely; how ~ it must be (empathetic conjecture)
structure: さぞ（かし）＋Adjective／Verb＋だろう／でしょう／ことだろう
explanation: さぞ introduces an empathetic guess about someone else's feelings or situation, imagining how intense it must be: さぞうれしかったことでしょう = how happy you must have been. It obligatorily pairs with a conjecture ending — だろう, でしょう, ことだろう — because the speaker is imagining, not asserting. さぞかし is an emphatic variant. The feeling guessed at is usually someone else's, and the tone is warm or sympathetic rather than analytical.

related.note: だろう is the plain conjecture さぞ must lean on; さぞ adds 'I can just imagine how much'.
に違いない draws a confident conclusion from evidence; さぞ〜だろう empathetically imagines degree.

meanings: the more ~, the more ~

meanings: taking ~ as the occasion/opportunity (for a change)
explanation: 〜を機に treats an event as the occasion that prompts a deliberate new action or change: 結婚を機に転職した = took marriage as the occasion to change jobs; 定年を機に = on the occasion of retirement. をきっかけに is the more colloquial 'triggered by'; を機に is more formal and leans toward a chosen life change.

related.note: を境に stresses a before/after dividing line; を機に stresses seizing the event as an opportunity to act.

meanings: once; formerly; (with a negative) never before
explanation: かつて is a formal adverb pointing to some time in the past: 'once, formerly, in days gone by'. かつて栄えた町 = a town that once flourished. It carries a literary, retrospective flavour and is common in writing and formal narration rather than casual chat.

meanings: to take on the look or quality of; -ish

meanings: although; even though; despite
explanation: This のに links two clauses that clash, adding a feeling of surprise, dissatisfaction, or complaint: 'even though A, B (unexpectedly)'. It follows the plain form; after nouns and な-adjectives, insert な (な-adjective な のに, Noun な のに). Unlike neutral けど, のに carries an emotional 'and yet' that things didn't go as they should have.

related.note: Same shape のに but 'in order to'; it follows a dictionary verb and shows no contrast.
けど is a neutral 'but'; のに adds surprise or dissatisfaction that the result went against expectation.
ても is 'even if' about a supposed case; のに is 'even though' about something that actually happened.

meanings: because of; as a result of (cause)

meanings: ~ that; to the effect that (quote modifying a noun)
explanation: 〜との links a quoted statement, report, or thought to a following noun of communication — 連絡・報告・知らせ・指示・話・うわさ. meanings: which exists only thanks to; made possible only by
structure: Noun［essential thing］＋あっての＋Noun［what depends on it］
explanation: 〜あっての joins two nouns: 'A あっての B' means B exists or holds true only because A is there — take A away and B collapses. 客あっての商売 = a business is nothing without its customers, 健康あっての仕事 = work only matters if you have your health. meanings: must be; surely; no doubt that ~

explanation: に違いない states a firm guess based on evidence — 'it must be ~ / surely ~'. 電気が消えているから、もう寝たに違いない ('the lights are off, so he must have gone to bed'). It is stronger than かもしれない but is still an inference, not a confirmed fact. It follows a noun, adjective, or plain verb.

meanings: not ~ and; because not ~
structure: Verb［ない form］ ＋ ［ない → なくて］
い-adjective ＋ ［くない → くなくて］

explanation: なくて is the negative て-form. It links two clauses where the first is a 'not' situation, either just joining ideas ('isn't ~ and ...') or giving the reason for the second clause ('because ~ isn't the case'). It attaches to い-adjectives (〜くない → 〜くなくて), to nouns and な-adjectives (〜ではなくて／じゃなくて), and to verbs (〜ない → 〜なくて), especially when the second clause is a feeling or state.

ので gives a plain 'because'; なくて states a negative cause that usually flows into a feeling.

meanings: tentatively; more or less; just in case; for now
explanation: 一応 marks that something is done only to a minimal or provisional degree — enough for now, not thoroughly. It has two shades: 'tentatively / more or less' (一応終わった = it's more or less done) and 'just in case / for form's sake' (一応確認しておく = check it just to be safe). Either way it signals a basic, non-exhaustive level rather than a complete or definitive one.

related.note: 一旦 means 'once (one does)' or 'temporarily'; 一応 means 'tentatively / just in case', stressing a minimal degree.

meanings: verb modifying a noun (relative clause)
explanation: Lets a verb describe a noun directly, the way a relative clause does in English: put a plain-form verb right before the noun it modifies, with no の or extra word in between. This is how Japanese builds phrases like 'the book I read' or 'the person who came'.

related.note: Modifying verbs usually take the plain non-past form.
い-adjectives modify nouns the same direct way, with no linking word.
な-adjectives need な before the noun; verbs attach with nothing in between.

meanings: covered in; smeared all over with
explanation: 〜まみれ marks a surface covered or smeared all over with something — almost always a dirty, wet, or unpleasant substance. 泥まみれ = covered in mud, 汗まみれ = drenched in sweat, 血まみれ = covered in blood. meanings: ended up (in a deplorable state); to top it all off
explanation: 〜始末だ caps off a chain of bad developments with the final, worst stage: 遅刻を繰り返し、ついには無断欠勤までする始末だ = he kept coming late, and to top it all off he started skipping work without notice. The speaker is exasperated or critical; the pattern almost demands set-up phrases like さんざん〜したあげく or ついには. It follows the dictionary form, and この始末だ ('look how it ended up') is a common set phrase.

synonyms.note: あげく marks 'after a long, trying process'; 始末だ goes further and condemns the final state it led to.

related.note: 末に is neutral about the outcome of a long process; 始末だ is reserved for outcomes the speaker deplores.
羽目になる laments the unlucky situation one falls into; 始末だ criticizes conduct that spiraled to a sorry end.

surface: とすれば・としたら・とすると
reading: とすれば・としたら・とすると
meanings: assuming that; supposing; if A (is the case), then B
structure: Sentence［plain form］＋ とすれば／としたら／とすると
explanation: These three attach to a plain-form clause to set up a supposition and draw a logical consequence — 彼の話が本当だとしたら、大変だ = supposing his story is true, that's a serious matter. You assume A for the sake of argument, then state what would follow. とすれば, としたら, and とすると are largely interchangeable; the second clause is usually a judgement, guess, or conclusion.

synonyms.note: なら also picks up a supposition to comment on; とすれば・としたら leans more toward reasoning out a logical consequence.

related.note: たら often means 'when/after' in time; としたら is purely 'supposing that', for hypothetical reasoning.
と言えば picks up a word to talk about it ('speaking of'); としたら assumes something is so and reasons from it.

meanings: to show signs of; to take on the air of; -like
explanation: The suffix めく attaches to a limited set of nouns to form a verb meaning 'to take on the atmosphere or signs of ~': 春めく = to grow spring-like, 謎めく = to become mysterious, 皮肉めく = to sound sarcastic. The adnominal past form めいた modifies a following noun — 謎めいた話 = a mysterious story, 冗談めいた口調 = a joking tone. It is a somewhat literary way to say something gives off a certain air without fully being that thing.

synonyms.note: らしい says something is typical of or behaves as befits its category; めく says it takes on the outward air of something it is not fully.
っぽい ('-ish') is colloquial and broadly productive; めく is literary and limited to set combinations.

meanings: the conjunctive (masu-stem) form used to link clauses in writing
explanation: The 連用形 — the ます-stem of a verb (書き, 食べ) and the 〜く form of an い-adjective (良く) — can join clauses much like the て-form, but sounds more formal and literary. 朝早く起き、顔を洗い、家を出た links the actions in a written-style sequence.

related.note: The て-form links clauses in everyday speech; the 連用形 does the same job in a more formal, written register.

meanings: even if; no matter (how) ~ (formal concession)
explanation: In formal, literary Japanese 〜とも expresses concession — 'even if / no matter (how) ~'. It attaches to a verb's volitional form (何が起ころうとも = 'no matter what happens') or an い-adjective's 〜く form (いかに苦しくとも). The outcome holds regardless of the condition.

synonyms.note: ても is the everyday 'even if / even though'; とも is its formal, literary equivalent, attached to the volitional or 〜く form.

related.note: たって is the casual spoken 'even if'; とも sits at the opposite, most formal end of the register scale.

meanings: na-adjective as a predicate (~だ/です)
explanation: Uses a な-adjective to end a sentence: add だ (plain) or です (polite) directly after the adjective, with no な. This is how you say "X is [adjective]" — the な only appears when the adjective sits in front of a noun.

related.note: The copula だ／です that turns the adjective into a full statement.
The same adjective takes な (not だ) when it modifies a following noun.

meanings: and also ~; moreover ~; ~ as well
explanation: In this pattern また works as 'moreover / also', introducing a further fact, and a later も marks that added item as one more thing that holds too — 彼は医者であり、また作家でもある = 'He is a doctor, and also a writer.' It stacks a second point onto the first and is common in explanatory or written style.

related.note: もまた marks one item as 'also, too'; また〜も leads with また ('moreover') and closes the added point with も.
それに ('besides, on top of that') adds a further point conversationally; また〜も does so in a more explanatory register.

meanings: still; even more; furthermore, in addition
structure: なお（一層） ＋ predicate ［still / even more］
explanation: なお has two written-language uses. As an adverb it means 'still / even now' or 'even more' — 今なお = still even now, なお一層 = all the more. As a sentence-initial conjunction it adds supplementary information to what was just said — 'note that; in addition'. Both belong to formal writing and announcements rather than casual speech.

synonyms.note: さらに means 'furthermore / even more' and is usable in speech; なお is more formal and typical of written notices.
に加えて adds one thing on top of another as 'in addition to ~'; なお loosely appends a supplementary remark.

meanings: ... too; ... as well (emphatic, literary)
explanation: もまた is an emphatic, somewhat literary version of the particle も 'too / also'. Adding また reinforces that the item belongs to the same category as something already stated — 私もまた = 'I, too (just like the others)'. It attaches to a noun that is the topic and appears mainly in written or formal speech.

synonyms.note: Plain も simply adds 'too'; もまた lends emphasis and a literary tone.

meanings: to end up in (an unpleasant situation); to get stuck having to ~
explanation: 羽目 is a tight spot, and 〜羽目になる marks ending up forced into an unwelcome situation — usually as a consequence of something one did or that went wrong. 払う羽目になった = ended up having to pay, 歩いて帰る羽目になる = get stuck walking home. The outcome is unwanted and often self-inflicted.

synonyms.note: ことになる reports a decision or arrangement neutrally; 羽目になる specifically means being stuck in an unwelcome predicament.

related.note: ざるを得ない focuses on being forced to do an action; 羽目になる describes ending up in the bad situation itself.

variants.explanation: 〜てしょうがない (and its twin 〜てしかたがない) says a feeling or sensation is so strong you can't do anything about it — you're overwhelmed by it. 眠くてしょうがない = unbearably sleepy; 気になってしょうがない = I can't stop worrying about it. It's mostly used about one's own feelings.

synonyms.note: てたまらない is a very close 'unbearably ~'; てしょうがない is slightly softer and more everyday.
てならない carries the same 'can't help feeling,' but sounds more written or literary.

meanings: can; to be able to
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋ ことができる
explanation: Verb［dictionary form］＋ことができる expresses ability or possibility — 'can do'. 弾くことができる = can play. It means the same as the potential verb form (弾ける) but sounds a touch more formal and is common in writing and announcements. The verb before ことができる stays in plain dictionary form.

synonyms.note: The potential verb form says the same 'can do' more casually; ことができる is a bit more formal.

related.note: This is the こと nominalizer plus ができる ('be possible').

meanings: and so; that being the case, I (deliberately) did ...
explanation: As a conjunction, そこで describes a situation and then introduces the action the speaker purposely took in response — roughly "and so" or "that's why I ...". The key point is that what follows is a deliberate step taken because of the circumstances, not an outcome that simply happened by itself.

related.note: その結果 states an outcome that follows on its own; そこで introduces an action the speaker deliberately takes.
そのため(に) gives the reason for what follows; そこで frames the action prompted by that situation.

surface: べからず・べからざる
reading: べからず・べからざる
meanings: must not; do not; prohibited (literary)
explanation: 〜べからず is a stiff, literary prohibition — 'must not ~, do not ~' — descending from classical grammar. 立ち入るべからず = no entry, 初心忘るべからず = never forget your original resolve. It follows a dictionary-form verb (する becomes すべからず or するべからず). The attributive 〜べからざる modifies a noun: 許すべからざる行為 = an impermissible act.

synonyms.note: な is the blunt spoken 'don't ~'; べからず is the written, formal, archaic equivalent.
てはならない is a formal 'must not' usable in modern prose; べからず is more archaic and sign-like.

related.note: まじき is the literary 'unbecoming of ~' that modifies a noun, much like べからざる.
べきだ states what one should do; べからず is the negative, prohibitive side of the same べし root.

meanings: since it's ~ (given what we know of them); knowing ~
structure: Noun［person／group］＋ の ＋ ことだから
explanation: 〜ことだから builds a prediction on the known character of a person or group. Because we know what they are like, we can guess how they will act — 几帳面な彼のことだから遅れないだろう = knowing how punctual he is, he surely won't be late. It attaches to a noun (usually a person) + の.

related.note: だけに draws a heightened result from a known fact ('all the more because'); ことだから predicts behavior from someone's character.
こともあって states a contributing reason ('partly because'); ことだから predicts an action from what someone is like.

meanings: if it's ~, then that's its own situation (things still work out / bring their own issues)
explanation: 〜なら〜で repeats the same word on both sides to say that even in that case, things resolve themselves — or throw up a different problem. あるならあるで = if you have it, then that's its own matter; ないならないで = if there's none, then we'll manage even so. It concedes a situation and shrugs that it too has its own way of playing out. The 〜ば〜で shape (なければないで) is common.

meanings: leaving something in a state (often through neglect); leaving it on/open/as-is
explanation: っぱなし attaches to the ます-stem and means leaving the result of an action in place — the light left on (つけっぱなし), the door left open (開けっぱなし). It usually carries a hint of carelessness: you did something and neglected to undo it. It can also describe an action that just keeps going without a break.

related.note: まま neutrally states a state left unchanged; っぱなし adds the nuance that leaving it that way was careless.

meanings: unbecoming of; that must not be (literary)
explanation: 〜まじき is a literary attributive meaning 'that must not be, unbecoming of' — it modifies a noun to condemn conduct as improper for a given role. 教師にあるまじき言動 = behaviour unbecoming of a teacher, 許すまじき罪 = an unforgivable crime. synonyms.note: べからず ends a clause as a prohibition; まじき modifies a noun attributively ('unbecoming ~').

related.note: べきだ ('should') is the affirmative; まじき functions as its literary negative counterpart.

surface: にむかって・にむけて
reading: にむかって・にむけて
meanings: toward; heading for; aimed at
structure: Noun ＋ に向かって／に向けて
explanation: に向かって and に向けて both mark a target that one moves or acts toward. に向かって is more physical and directional — facing or heading toward a place or person (海に向かって叫ぶ). に向けて leans toward a goal or aim — preparing or working toward a target, event, deadline, or audience (試験に向けて勉強する).

related.note: に対して marks the target of an action or attitude ('toward / against'); に向かって・に向けて marks physical direction or a goal aimed at.

surface: からある・からする・からの
reading: からある・からする・からの
meanings: as much/many as; no less than; upwards of
explanation: This pattern follows a number and stresses that the amount is impressively large — 'no less than, a good ~'. からある is used for size, weight, or quantity; からする for price or cost; からの comes before a noun for numbers of things or people. 五十キロからある荷物, 百万円からする品, 百人からの人. In every case the speaker is underscoring that the figure is at least that big.

meanings: was doing; had been doing (past progressive/state)
structure: Verb［て form］＋ いた／いました
explanation: ていた is simply the past of ている. It describes an action that was going on at some moment in the past (was ~ing), or a state that had come about and was still holding then. Casual ～ていた, polite ～ていました. Which reading applies depends on the verb, exactly as with ている.

related.note: ている places the ongoing action/state at the present; ていた places the same at a past reference point.
てきた traces a change continuing up to now; ていた just situates an action in the past.

meanings: if you ask ~; in ~'s opinion (as they would put it)
explanation: 〜に言わせれば introduces a person's subjective, often assertive verdict on something — 'the way ~ sees it, if you ask ~'. 私に言わせれば = if you ask me, 専門家に言わせれば = as the experts would put it. It frames what follows as that person's opinion, frequently a pointed or critical one, rather than neutral fact. The person is marked with に.

related.note: にしてみれば imagines how a situation feels from someone's standpoint; に言わせれば voices the opinion or verdict they would actually state.
にとって marks 'for ~ / to ~' as the one an evaluation matters to; に言わせれば introduces that person's own spoken judgment.

meanings: the fact is ~; explanatory
structure: Verb／い-adjective［plain form］＋ んです ／ のです
Noun／な-adjective ＋ な ＋ んです ／ のです
explanation: Frames a statement or question as an explanation — giving the reason or backstory behind a situation, or asking for one. Attach んです (spoken) or のです (formal, written) to the plain form of a verb or い-adjective; nouns and な-adjectives take な first (学生なんです). It signals "the thing is..." rather than a bare report of fact.

related.note: The casual explanatory の in questions (どうしたの) — same backstory function, softer register.
から states a reason directly; んです frames the whole sentence as the explanation.
ので attaches a reason clause; んです colours a standalone statement as explanatory.

meanings: ichidan (る) verb conjugation
structure: Verb［stem］＋ る ／ ない ／ た ／ ます
explanation: る-verbs (ichidan verbs) are the simpler verb group: to conjugate, just drop the final る and add the ending. Their dictionary form ends in -eる or -iる, like 食べる and 見る. This one regular pattern gives the polite, negative, past, and て forms.

related.note: う動詞 are the godan group, whose stem shifts sound before each ending.
ます attaches to the stem that dropping る leaves behind.
The dictionary (non-past) form is the starting point these conjugations build from.

meanings: some; several; a few (of a counted thing)
explanation: Putting 何 before a counter and か after it gives a vague 'some / several / a few' of that thing: 何回か = a few times, 何人か = several people, 何日か = a number of days. 何＋counter alone asks 'how many?'; the か turns that question into an unspecified small number.

related.note: 疑問詞＋か (だれか, どこか) is the same 'question word + か → some' idea applied to other question words.
だれか・どこか make 'someone / somewhere'; 何＋counter＋か makes 'some (number) of a counted thing'.

meanings: there is no way/means to; nothing one can do to
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋術（すべ）がない／術もない
explanation: 術 (read すべ, not じゅつ) is a literary noun meaning 'means' or 'method'. 〜術がない attaches to a dictionary-form verb and says there is simply no way to carry out that action — 真相を知る術がない = there is no way to learn the truth, なす術がない = there is nothing one can do. 術もない is a slightly stronger variant. The expression is formal and written, conveying helplessness in the face of a situation.

synonyms.note: ようがない also means 'no way to ~', but is far more common and everyday; 術がない is literary and formal.
べくもない means 'cannot possibly ~'; 術がない specifically says no method or means exists.

structure: らしくない／らしかった［conjugates like an い-adjective］
variants.explanation: This らしい is a suffix saying something has the ideal qualities of what it attaches to — 男らしい ('manly'), 子どもらしい ('fittingly childlike'), 春らしい ('spring-like'). It is praise for being a good, typical example of its kind, and it behaves like an い-adjective.

meanings: whatever ~ may be; no matter what ~ is

meanings: perhaps; maybe; possibly (it could be that ~)

explanation: もしかしたら opens a sentence to raise something as a possibility you are unsure about, and it usually pairs with かもしれない at the end — もしかしたら雨かもしれない = maybe it will rain. Variants もしかすると／もしかして carry the same feel.

meanings: starting with; as the first of an unfolding series
structure: Noun［first event］＋を皮切りに（して）／を皮切りとして
explanation: 〜を皮切りに marks X as the first instance from which a series spreads or expands — 東京公演を皮切りに全国ツアーが始まった = starting with the Tokyo show, a nationwide tour began. 皮切り literally means 'the first cut', and the following clause must describe a chain of events or a spreading development that grows out of that opening, not a single isolated act. meanings: that is how/why it came about (formal explanation)
explanation: 〜次第です closes a formal explanation of the circumstances that led to one's action: ご連絡を差し上げた次第です = and that is why I am contacting you. meanings: as was bound to happen; inevitably
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋べくして＋Verb［same verb, た form］
explanation: 〜べくして typically repeats the same verb — VるべくしてVた — to say that an outcome was bound to happen, the natural and inevitable result of the circumstances. 起こるべくして起こった事故 = an accident that was bound to happen. meanings: to be forced to; to have no choice but to (undergo)
explanation: 〜を余儀なくされる is the passive side of the pair: the person or organization affected is the subject, and outside circumstances leave them no choice but to accept some outcome. The unwanted outcome is an action noun (欠場, 閉鎖, 延期) marked with を. けがで欠場を余儀なくされた = was forced to sit out because of injury. It stresses that the situation was imposed from without, and it belongs to formal, written register.

synonyms.note: ざるを得ない attaches to a verb and voices personal, reluctant resignation; を余儀なくされる attaches to an action noun and stresses that external circumstances imposed it.
しかない plainly says 'there is nothing to do but'; を余儀なくされる is far more formal and frames the outcome as forced upon one from outside.

related.note: The causative counterpart: 〜を余儀なくさせる makes the cause the subject, while 〜を余儀なくされる makes the forced person the subject.

meanings: is not; am not (negative copula)

meanings: it's fine even if ~; I don't mind if ~
structure: Verb［て form］＋ もかまわない
explanation: 〜てもかまわない says that even if X happens, it doesn't bother the speaker — so it grants permission or shows willingness. 高くてもかまわない = I don't mind if it's expensive. 構わない literally means 'don't mind', giving it a softer feel than the blunter てもいい.

antonyms.note: てはいけない forbids the action; てもかまわない allows it.

related.note: ても is the bare 'even if'; てもかまわない adds the judgment that the case is acceptable.

meanings: even; so much as; not even
explanation: さえ singles out an extreme or surprising example to imply the rest follows — 子どもでさえ知っている (even a child knows), 時間さえない (I don't even have time). The idea is 'if even this, then surely everything else.' It is emphatic and often a touch more formal than も.

related.note: まで stresses reaching an unexpected extreme ('to the point of even'); さえ picks a minimal example to imply the rest.
さえ〜ば uses さえ to mark the one sufficient condition; plain さえ just highlights an extreme example.

meanings: contrast: A is ~, but B is ~
structure: Noun A ＋ は ＋ ～ ＋ が、＋ Noun B ＋ は ＋ ～
explanation: This pattern sets two things against each other in one sentence. Both A and B take the contrastive は, and the middle が works as the conjunction 'but', joining the two clauses. The result spotlights how A and B differ: 肉は食べますが、魚は食べません = I eat meat, but I don't eat fish.

related.note: けど is the casual 'but'; this pattern pairs it with double は to make the contrast explicit on both sides.
しかし is a formal 'however' that starts a new sentence; は～が～は draws the contrast inside one sentence.

meanings: like A, like B; both are (equally) at fault / just as bad
explanation: 〜が〜なら〜も〜だ is a set pattern that criticizes two parties at once by pairing them — 'if A is like this, then B is no better either'. 親が親なら子も子だ = with parents like that, no wonder the child is the same; 客が客なら店も店だ = the customers are bad, but so is the shop. The same noun is usually repeated in each slot, and the tone is one of paired disapproval.

meanings: cannot get away without doing; will have to

explanation: 〜ずには済まない says the matter cannot be settled unless the action is taken — social or moral circumstances leave no way out: 謝らずには済まない = an apology is unavoidable. 済む means 'to be settled', so the pattern literally reads 'it won't be settled without doing'. meanings: along; in accordance with

meanings: do ~ (firm, caring command)
explanation: なさい makes a firm command that is still gentler than the blunt imperative. Attach it to the verb stem (ます form minus ます): 食べます → 食べなさい. It is the tone a parent, teacher, or older person uses toward a child or student — instructive and caring, but clearly a command, not a request between equals.

related.note: The plain imperative (行け) is harsher; なさい softens a command into something instructive.
てください is a polite request among equals; なさい is a command directed downward.
なさい comes from the imperative of the honorific verb なさる.

meanings: not necessarily; it isn't always the case that ~

meanings: I hear that ~; apparently ~ (casual, spoken hearsay)
structure: な-adjective／Noun ＋ な ＋ んだって
explanation: 〜んだって passes along something you heard as casual, spoken news or gossip — 'apparently', 'I hear'. It is built from the explanatory のだ (→ んだ) plus the quoting って, so it reports the information with a 'the story is that ~' flavor. 田中さん、結婚するんだって = Apparently Tanaka is getting married.

synonyms.note: 〜そうだ reports hearsay in a neutral, often written tone; 〜んだって is its casual, spoken counterpart with an explanatory の flavor.
〜って quotes or reports speech bare; 〜んだって adds the explanatory んだ, framing it as 'the story is that ~'.
〜らしい reports with a touch of inference or distance ('it seems'); 〜んだって passes on what was actually said more directly.

related.note: んです is the explanatory のだ that 〜んだって is built on — んだ plus the quoting って.
んだけど・んですが is another colloquial extension of explanatory んだ, used to soften a lead-in rather than report hearsay.

meanings: no way; surely not; you must be joking; don't tell me ~
structure: まさか ＋ Sentence（〜とは／〜なんて／〜ない）
explanation: まさか flags something as too unexpected or unbelievable to be true — 'surely not', 'don't tell me...'. It often teams up with 〜とは or 〜なんて and a tone of surprise. As a standalone reply, まさか! means 'No way! / You're kidding!'.

related.note: はずがない is a reasoned 'there's no way it's so'; まさか is a gut reaction of disbelief at something unexpected.
わけがない flatly denies a possibility on logical grounds; まさか voices surprised doubt, often before it turns out to be true.
とは marks a surprising fact; まさか often introduces the sentence that ends in 〜とは.

surface: にしたところで・としたところで
reading: にしたところで・としたところで
meanings: even ~; even for ~; even supposing ~ (it makes no difference)
explanation: 〜にしたところで takes up a case and concedes that even it is no exception, or even supposing it, the conclusion still holds — usually that nothing would change. 専門家にしたところで = even the experts (are no different), 急いだとしたところで = even supposing we hurry. にしたところで attaches to a noun ('even ~ too'); としたところで often follows a verb ('even if we suppose ~'). surface: ともなると・にもなると

meanings: once it reaches (as much / as high as) ~
structure: Noun＋ともなると／にもなると
explanation: 〜ともなると・〜にもなると marks that once a subject reaches a notably high level — rank, age, amount, or occasion — a matching special situation naturally follows. 社長ともなると、責任も大きい = once you're a company president, the responsibility is great too. meanings: ended up never doing (and the chance is gone)
structure: Verb［ない stem］＋ずじまい（だった）
explanation: 〜ずじまい combines the negative ず with 仕舞い ('the end') to say a period closed with the action never done — and the speaker regrets it: 結局行かずじまいだった = in the end I never did go. The chance is understood to be lost now. It follows the ない-stem (する becomes せずじまい), almost always appears in the past (〜ずじまいだった), and pairs naturally with 結局 or とうとう.

related.note: 〜そこなう marks missing a particular chance to do something; ずじまい looks back on a whole period that ended without it.
ずとも is a concessive 'even without doing'; ずじまい reports that the doing never happened, with regret.

meanings: since; seeing as (one reason among others)
explanation: 〜ことだし offers one reason — while hinting there are others — as gentle grounds for a suggestion or decision: 雨も上がったことだし、出かけよう = the rain's stopped (among other things), so let's head out. The こと wraps the reason up as an established circumstance, and し adds the 'and other reasons too' flavor. It is conversational but slightly considered in tone, and the sentence usually ends with a proposal, intention, or request rather than a plain statement.

synonyms.note: Plain し also lists reasons; ことだし is softer and frames the reason as a settled circumstance leading to a proposal.

related.note: こともあって reports a partial cause of a fact; ことだし gives a reason for what the speaker proposes to do.
ことだから reasons from someone's known character; ことだし cites a circumstance as one reason among several.

explanation: 〜ものだから gives a reason, often as an excuse for something unexpected or beyond one's control — 'it's because…'. It stresses that the cause naturally led to the result, so the speaker isn't fully to blame. It is more emotive and self-justifying than a plain から.

synonyms.note: もので／ものですから is the same explanatory 'because', a touch softer and more polite; ものだから is more emphatic.
ので is a neutral, polite 'because'; ものだから adds an excusing, 'it couldn't be helped' tone.

related.note: ことから draws an objective conclusion 'from the fact that'; ものだから gives an emotive reason or excuse.

meanings: so that; in order to (a state comes about)
explanation: ように states the purpose behind an action — you do the main action so that some situation will come about. The clause before ように is usually a state or a potential / negative verb (something you cannot directly will), like 聞こえる, わかる, or 忘れない. It contrasts with ために, whose front clause is a deliberate action.

related.note: ために gives a purpose reached by deliberate action; ように, a state you aim to bring about.
ようにする turns such a goal into an ongoing effort to do something.
ようになる describes that aimed-for state actually coming about.

meanings: in other words; that is to say; in short
explanation: つまり introduces a restatement or summary of what was just said — you rephrase it more simply or boil it down to its point. 'In other words / that is to say / in short.' It links a fuller explanation to a tighter conclusion drawn from it.

synonyms.note: すなわち is a more formal, precise 'namely'; つまり is the everyday 'in other words.'

related.note: ということだ often closes a つまり restatement, summing up 'it means that ~.'

meanings: let alone; not to mention; to say nothing of
explanation: 〜はおろか says that not only the greater or more obvious thing but even a more basic one is (typically) not the case. 漢字はおろか、ひらがなも書けない = can't write even hiragana, let alone kanji. It attaches to a noun, and the second, more basic item is usually marked with も, さえ, or すら, in a generally negative sentence. This is formal, written Japanese.

synonyms.note: どころか can also reverse an expectation ('far from ~'); はおろか strictly builds a 'not even the basic thing' scale.
のみならず adds 'not only ~ but also' in positive statements; はおろか works in negatives ('let alone').

related.note: さえ ('even') often marks the second, basic item in a はおろか sentence.

meanings: as ~; just as ~; at the mercy of; letting it happen
explanation: ままに means 'just as (something is or tells you)', going along with a force or desire rather than acting on one's own will — 気の向くままに ('as the mood takes me'), 言われるままに ('just as one is told'). It conveys yielding to whatever drives the action.

related.note: まま states that a condition stays unchanged; ままに adds the sense of yielding to a force or instruction.
とおりに follows a specified way exactly; ままに passively goes along with whatever drives it.

meanings: to do (honorific)
explanation: なさる is the honorific (尊敬語) verb for する, used to raise the person whose action you are describing. Its polite form is irregular: なさる → なさいます (not なさります). Reach for it when a customer, teacher, or superior 'does' something and you want to show respect toward them.

antonyms.note: お〜する humbly lowers your own action; なさる honorifically raises someone else's.

related.note: お〜になる is the general honorific frame; なさる is the special honorific specifically for する.
いらっしゃる is the matching special honorific for いる・行く・来る.
なさい, the child-directed command, is historically the imperative of なさる.

meanings: with ~ as the dividing line/turning point
structure: Noun［time／event］＋を境に（して）／を境として
explanation: 〜を境に takes a time point or event as a boundary and marks a clear before/after contrast: あの日を境に彼は変わった = from that day on, as a dividing line, he changed. 境 means 'boundary', so the emphasis is on how noticeably different things are on either side of that point. It often pairs with life-changing events, ages, or seasons.

synonyms.note: を機に seizes an event as an opportunity for a chosen action; を境に marks a boundary with a clear before/after change.

related.note: を限りに marks a final endpoint after which something stops; を境に marks a point where things change from one state to another.

meanings: the best/foremost ~ in (a group, place, or field)
explanation: 〜きっての singles someone or something out as the very best within a defined group, place, or field. The noun before きって names the domain, and the noun after is what ranks number one in it: この業界きっての実力者 = the leading figure in this industry, 当代きっての名優 = the finest actor of the age. It is a set adnominal form (きって + の + noun) with a somewhat elevated, admiring tone.

related.note: ならでは points to a quality only that person or place could produce; きっての ranks someone as number one within a group.

meanings: however; even so; but (contrary to what was expected)
explanation: ところが begins a new sentence to introduce a result that runs against what you expected. You set up an expectation, then ところが flips it: 楽しみにしていた。ところが、当日は雨で中止になった = I'd been looking forward to it. But then it rained that day and it got cancelled. The surprise is a fact that happened, not something you planned.

synonyms.note: しかし is a neutral 'however'; ところが specifically marks a result that reverses what you expected.

related.note: けれども contrasts two clauses within a sentence; ところが starts a fresh sentence with a surprising turn.
Easy to confuse: ところで changes the topic ('by the way'); ところが marks an unexpected reversal ('however').

meanings: excessively; far too; so ~ (that)
structure: あまりに（も）＋ い-adjective ／ な-adjective ／ Verb
explanation: あまりに and あまりにも are adverbs placed directly before an adjective or verb to say something is excessive — 'far too ~'. あまりにも高い = far too expensive, あまりに忙しい = terribly busy. The も is optional and just strengthens the emphasis. It often leads into a result: 'so ~ that…'.

meanings: no comparison with ~; in a different league from ~
structure: Noun＋とは比べものにならない
explanation: 〜とは比べものにならない states that the gap between two things is so wide they cannot be measured on the same scale — 'no comparison with ~'. 昔のとは比べものにならないほど速い = incomparably faster than the old one. Context tells you which side comes out ahead. It often appears as 〜とは比べものにならないほど＋adjective to stress just how far apart they are.

surface: でもなんでもない・くもなんともない
reading: でもなんでもない・くもなんともない
meanings: not ~ at all; nothing of the sort; not in the least ~
explanation: 〜でも何でもない emphatically denies that something is the case — it's nothing of the kind. 友達でも何でもない = he's not a friend, not anything of the sort. meanings: in the end; after all (following a long, often troublesome process)
explanation: 〜あげく marks that after much time, effort, or trouble, a result finally comes — and that result is usually undesirable or regrettable. さんざん迷ったあげく = after hesitating a great deal, in the end. It follows a た-form verb or a noun + の, and often appears as あげくに or あげくの果てに. Use it to stress that a drawn-out process led to a (frequently bad) outcome.

synonyms.note: た末に also marks 'after much ~, finally', but is more neutral and can lead to a positive result; あげく leans negative.

related.note: 結果 states a neutral 'as a result of ~'; あげく adds that the process was long and trying and the outcome regrettable.

meanings: starting with ~; ~ and others like it; headed by ~

meanings: if it is (a case of); if it's for the sake of ~
explanation: 〜とあれば sets up a special condition and says that, given it, one will readily do something one otherwise might not — 'if it's for ~, then...'. 子供のためとあれば = if it's for the children's sake, 必要とあれば = if it should prove necessary. variants.explanation: くらい・ぐらい has two jobs: with quantities it means 'about, approximately' (千円くらい = about 1,000 yen), and after a clause it marks a degree by example — 'to the extent that…' (泣きたいくらい = to the point of wanting to cry). くらい and ぐらい are interchangeable.

synonyms.note: ほど also marks extent and approximation; it is a bit more formal and common in negative comparisons.

related.note: The standalone N5 くらい covers just the basic 'about' (approximation) sense.

meanings: even so; be that as it may; still
explanation: それにしても accepts what was just said but then comments that the degree of something is beyond expectation — often surprise or mild complaint at how extreme it is. 'Even allowing for that, still...'. It keeps the current topic rather than turning to an opposite result.

synonyms.note: それでも concedes and moves to a contrasting result; それにしても comments on an unexpected degree.

related.note: にしても attaches to a word or clause as 'even granting that'; それにしても stands alone at the head of a sentence.
それなのに reacts to a contradiction; それにしても reacts to something exceeding expectation.

meanings: to give (away, to someone else)
structure: Noun［receiver］＋ に ＋ Noun［thing］＋ を ＋ あげる
explanation: あげる means to give something, with the gift moving away from the speaker or the speaker's side toward another person. The giver is the subject, the receiver is marked with に, and the thing given with を. Reach for it whenever you or your in-group hand something over to someone else.

antonyms.note: あげる gives something away; もらう receives something.

related.note: くれる is also 'give', but toward the speaker's side, not away from it.
Verb＋てあげる does an action as a favor for someone, rather than handing over an object.

meanings: almost all; almost; hardly (with a negative)
structure: ほとんど ＋ Verb［ない form］
explanation: ほとんど means 'almost / nearly all' in positive sentences and 'hardly / almost never' when the verb is negative. As an adverb it comes before the verb: ほとんど終わった (almost finished), ほとんど分からない (hardly understand). Its meaning flips entirely with the polarity of the verb.

related.note: あまり〜ない means 'not very much'; ほとんど〜ない pushes further to 'hardly at all'.

meanings: probably; most likely; in all likelihood
structure: 恐らく＋Sentence（〜だろう／でしょう）
explanation: 恐らく marks the speaker's fairly confident conjecture — 'probably / most likely'. It usually pairs with a following だろう, でしょう, or に違いない. 恐らく間に合わないだろう = we probably won't make it in time. It is more formal than たぶん and often leans toward a serious or unfavorable guess. Despite the kanji 恐, it has nothing to do with fear.

related.note: に違いない expresses near-certainty; 恐らく is a weaker, more tentative 'probably'.

meanings: nothing beats ~; ~ is the best
structure: Noun／Verb［dictionary form］／Verb［ない form］＋ に限る
explanation: に限る states the speaker's opinion that nothing is better than the thing named — 'you can't beat ~ / ~ is best'. related.note: に限らず means 'not just ~ (but also)'; に限る means '~ is the best'.

meanings: it means (doing) ~; it comes down to ~; what it is, is ~
structure: Noun／〜というのは ＋ Verb［plain form］＋ ことなのだ／ことなの
explanation: ことなのだ (casual ことなの, polite ことなのです) restates a topic as what it fundamentally amounts to. It takes a plain clause, packages it as a こと — a matter or act — and equates the topic with it, explaining 'what X really is / what it means.' The な comes from こと being treated with the explanatory の.

synonyms.note: ということだ also restates a meaning ('that is to say'); ことなのだ frames the whole thing as one defining matter with explanatory の.

related.note: ことだ after a verb gives advice; ことなのだ defines or explains what something amounts to.

meanings: cannot stop doing; do nothing but

meanings: by the way; now then (changing the topic)
explanation: ところで begins a sentence to switch to a new, often unrelated topic — a spoken 'by the way'. It frequently leads into a question: そうですか。ところで、ご家族はお元気ですか = I see. By the way, is your family well? Use it to move the conversation somewhere new after finishing, or setting aside, the current subject.

related.note: Look-alike: ところが means 'however' and reverses an expectation; ところで just changes the subject.

か何か tacks 'or something' onto a noun — a different use of 何か.

meanings: sentence-final particle adding soft emphasis or feeling (stereotypically feminine)
explanation: Sentence-final わ attaches to the plain form and adds a gentle, emotive touch to a statement. Said with a rising intonation it is classic feminine 'role language' — the わ of fiction and older speech — and can sound affected in real modern conversation. A separate, flat or falling わ is gender-neutral and very common in casual and Kansai speech, where it marks a mild self-directed assertion (そろそろ行くわ = 'I'll head off now'). meanings: precisely; for sure; this very one (emphasis)
explanation: こそ spotlights the word right before it, singling it out as 'this one, precisely, and not another.' Attached to a noun or phrase it says 'this is the one that really counts' — 今度こそ (this time for sure), こちらこそ (no, thank YOU). It highlights rather than contrasts.

meanings: question particle
explanation: か placed at the very end of a sentence turns a statement into a question. In polite speech it stands in for a spoken rising intonation, so 学生です (is a student) becomes 学生ですか (are you a student?). No question mark is required, though casual writing often adds one.

かどうか embeds a question ('whether or not') inside a larger sentence.

meanings: て-form linking clauses: and (then); because
explanation: The verb て-form links clauses together: it can list actions in order ('do A, and then B') or give a light reason ('B because A'). The voiced で appears with certain verbs (読んで, 遊んで). The final verb carries the tense — the て-form itself stays tense-neutral.

related.note: い-adjectives and nouns link with 〜くて／〜で; verbs use the verb て-form.
〜と joins nouns ('A and B'); the て-form joins verbs and clauses.

surface: ごとく・ごとき・ごとし
reading: ごとく・ごとき・ごとし
meanings: like; as if; such as (literary)
explanation: ごとく is the literary counterpart of ように: 雪のごとく = like snow. It inflects like a classical auxiliary — ごとく modifies a verb or adjective, ごとき modifies a noun, and ごとし ends a sentence. After a noun it takes の (氷のごとく); after a verb it often appears as （かの）ごとく. Attached directly to a person, ごとき belittles that person — 私ごとき is humble, 彼ごとき is dismissive. Today it survives in essays, proverbs, and formal speeches; everyday speech uses ように・ような・ようだ.

synonyms.note: かのように is the standard modern way to say 'as if'; ごとく says the same thing in literary register.
ように・ような is the neutral everyday equivalent; ごとく・ごとき belongs to written and ceremonial style.

related.note: ことごとく ('without exception') looks similar but is an unrelated word — it comes from 悉く, not from 如く.

surface: ようが〜ようが・ようと〜ようと
reading: ようが〜ようが・ようと〜ようと
meanings: whether ~ or ~ (either way, it makes no difference)
structure: い-adjective［かろう］＋が／と＋い-adjective［かろう］＋が／と
explanation: Two volitionals in a row — 〜ようが〜ようが or 〜ようと〜ようと — list two contrasting possibilities and declare that neither affects the outcome: 笑おうが泣こうが = whether you laugh or cry. synonyms.note: ようが〜まいが spans a do/not-do pair; ようが〜ようが lists two positive alternatives, both irrelevant to the outcome.
〜ようが／ようと (single) means 'no matter (what/how)'; doubling it names two specific possibilities.

meanings: of all things/times; (that person) especially would not ~
explanation: Noun＋に限って singles out one specific noun with a nuance of irony or exception. With a following negative it defends a particular person or thing — うちの子に限ってそんなことはしない ('my child of all people would never do that'). With an event or time it complains that bad luck strikes at exactly the wrong moment — 急いでいる時に限って ('of all times, just when I'm in a hurry').

antonyms.note: に限らず broadens ('not only N'); に限って narrows in on one specific N — opposite directions from the same 限.

related.note: に限る recommends N as the best choice; に限って singles N out with an ironic or defensive nuance.

meanings: I'm glad that ~; it was good that ~

explanation: すでに says an action or state is "already" done or in place by a given point — 会議はすでに始まっていた = the meeting had already started. It's the more formal, written cousin of もう, and unlike もう it isn't used for "soon" or "not anymore."

synonyms.note: もう is the everyday spoken word for "already"; すでに is its formal, written equivalent.

related.note: とっくに stresses "already, and long ago"; すでに just states that it's already so.

meanings: as; in the role of; in the capacity of
explanation: Noun ＋ として names the role, position, or capacity in which someone or something acts — 医者として働く = work as a doctor; お礼として渡す = give it as a token of thanks. meanings: how about ~?
structure: Noun ＋ は ＋ どうですか
explanation: はどうですか offers something or asks for an opinion about it, like "how about ~?" or "how is ~?". You use it to suggest an option politely or to ask how something is going.

meanings: ~-looking; in a ~-seeming way
explanation: The appearance そう conjugates like a な-adjective, so そうな can modify nouns and そうに can modify verbs: 高そうな時計 = 'an expensive-looking watch'; 楽しそうに遊ぶ = 'play in a way that looks fun'.

related.note: そうだ is the predicate form; そうに・そうな are its adverbial and noun-modifying shapes.

meanings: next after ~; second to ~ (in order or rank)
explanation: の次に places one thing right after another in a sequence or ranking: 'next after ~' or 'second to ~'. Noun の次に names the reference point, and what follows is what comes immediately after it — the second-tallest after Mt. Fuji, or the thing you'll do next after English.

related.note: 一番 names the outright top; の次に names what stands immediately below it.
の中で marks the group; の次に orders items within such a ranking.

meanings: that much; so much (as that)
explanation: そんなに sets a degree at 'that much' — the amount just mentioned or shown by the person you're talking to. It very often teams with a negative to mean 'not that much / not so ~,' gently pushing back on an assumed level. Place it right before the verb or adjective.

related.note: とても marks a high degree plainly; そんなに measures against an assumed 'that much.'

meanings: instantly; reflexively; on the spur of the moment
explanation: とっさに describes an instinctive reaction made in a split second, before there is time to think — typically in response to something sudden. とっさに身をかわす = dodge reflexively, とっさに手が出る = one's hand shoots out on reflex. The emphasis is that the action was unplanned and immediate. The noun form とっさの also appears, as in とっさの判断 (a split-second decision).

related.note: つい is doing something you shouldn't without thinking (often a habit); とっさに is reacting instantly to something sudden.

meanings: to be (am, is, are)
explanation: The copula that links a noun or な-adjective to the subject: "X is Y". だ is the plain form and です the polite form, so which you pick sets the register of the whole sentence. It is one of the very first patterns a learner uses to introduce and describe things.

related.note: だった・でした is the past form "was"; だ・です is the non-past.
です makes noun sentences polite; ます does the same for verbs.

meanings: probably ~; ~ right? (polite conjecture)
structure: Verb ／ い-adjective［plain form］＋ でしょう
explanation: Expresses a guess or seeks agreement: place でしょう after a noun, adjective, or plain verb to say something is probably the case, or, with rising intonation, to check that the listener agrees. It is the polite counterpart of だろう.

related.note: かもしれない marks a weaker 'maybe'; でしょう sounds more confident about the guess.
と思う states your own opinion; でしょう offers a guess or invites agreement.

meanings: a noun that has ~ (modifying がある)
explanation: When 〜がある sits directly in front of a noun, it describes that noun as one that has or contains something: 窓がある部屋 = a room that has a window. The whole 〜がある clause modifies the noun with no の or extra particle. In this position the が may also be replaced by の (窓のある部屋).

related.note: The plain 〜がある just states that something exists, without modifying a noun.
The が here can become の (窓のある部屋) because it is a noun-modifying clause.
Use いる in the same pattern for a noun that has a person or animal (子どもがいる家).

meanings: or rather; I'd say ~, or maybe ~; how should I put it
structure: ［first phrase］＋というか＋［second phrase］＋というか
explanation: 〜というか〜というか lines up two ways of describing something when neither quite fits, letting the speaker grope toward the right characterization — '~, or should I say ~'. うれしいというか、ほっとしたというか = happy, or rather relieved. It conveys a mixed, hard-to-pin-down impression in a casual, thinking-aloud tone, and the two terms are often near-synonyms or two facets of one feeling.

synonyms.note: といおうか searches for wording in a shade more literary, reflective tone; というか〜というか is the everyday, spoken pairing.
というより corrects one label to a better one ('rather than A, B'); というか〜というか leaves both labels standing as approximations.

explanation: 〜ものがある says that something strongly possesses a certain quality, which the speaker senses — 心を打つものがある ('there is something moving about it'). It voices a heartfelt impression that X genuinely has some quality worth noting, warmer and more evaluative than a plain 〜だ.

meanings: what with ~ and ~ (a pile-up of, usually, troubles)
explanation: 〜わ〜わで lists two or more things — typically mishaps — that pile up at once, and the closing で leads into the resulting (bad) state. Each item ends in わ: 財布は落とすわ、電車は遅れるわで散々だった = what with losing my wallet and the train being late, it was awful. It conveys an exasperated 'one thing after another' feeling and is common in spoken complaints.

related.note: Shares the syllable わ but is unrelated: the feminine 〜わ is a single sentence-final softener, not a paired listing of troubles.

meanings: to be audible; can hear (spontaneously)
explanation: 聞こえる means a sound reaches your ears on its own, without you trying to listen — 'can hear' in the sense of 'is audible'. The sound is marked with が: 音が聞こえる. It's the hearing partner of 見える, and it's distinct from 聞ける, which is about having the chance or ability to listen to something on purpose.

related.note: 見える is the sight counterpart — something naturally coming into view.
聞ける is the plain potential 'can listen'; 聞こえる is sound reaching you on its own.

meanings: can get by with just; be settled by (only)
structure: Verb［て form］／い-adjective［て form］＋ 済む
explanation: 〜て済む means a situation can be settled or gotten through with only that much — often less trouble than you'd feared. 電話で済む = it can be handled with just a phone call. 済む means 'to be finished / settled,' so the pattern says 'doing that much is all it takes.'

related.note: ずに済む means getting by WITHOUT doing something; て済む means getting by with just doing that much.

meanings: setting ~ aside; leaving ~ aside for now
explanation: 〜はさておき sets one topic aside in order to move on to a more pressing or important one — 'leaving ~ aside, let's get to ~'. 冗談はさておき = joking aside, 建前はさておき = setting the official line aside. It attaches to a noun and is a common way to pivot from a lesser matter to the real point at hand.

synonyms.note: はともかく also brackets a matter off; はさておき leans more on 'setting it aside to move on to the main point'.

related.note: はそっちのけで is neglecting a duty to do something else and sounds critical; はさておき is a neutral shift of topic.

meanings: ahead of; before anyone else; taking the lead over ~
explanation: 〜に先駆けて marks doing something before others or before the usual time, taking the lead — 'ahead of ~, in advance of ~'. 他社に先駆けて発売する = launch ahead of rival firms, 桜に先駆けて咲く = bloom before the cherry blossoms. meanings: have not done ~ yet
structure: まだ ＋ Verb［て form］＋ いません
explanation: Says an expected action still hasn't happened, viewed as of now: pair まだ with the negative ている form (ていません). Japanese uses the negative present here, not the past, because you are describing the current unfinished state rather than a past event.

related.note: The adverb まだ on its own; this pattern pins it to the ている form.
The ている form that this pattern negates to express "not yet done".
もう plus a past verb is the affirmative counterpart: already done.

meanings: to want to (of a third person, shown outwardly)
explanation: たがる reports that someone else looks like they want to do something, judged from outside signs. It's built from the 〜たい stem plus がる, and conjugates like an u-verb. Use it for other people's desires; for your own, plain 〜たい is correct.

related.note: 〜たい states your own desire; たがる reports someone else's, seen from outside.
〜が欲しい wants a thing; 〜たがる wants to do an action.

meanings: whether ~ or not (the result is the same)
structure: Verb［て form］＋ も ＋ Verb［ない form → なくて］＋ も
explanation: Pairing a positive 〜ても with the matching negative 〜なくても for the same word says the outcome holds either way — 降っても降らなくても = whether it rains or not. You state the two opposite cases and then a result that does not depend on which one is true.

related.note: ても covers a single 'even if' case; 〜ても〜なくても lines up both cases to say it makes no difference.
てもかまわない grants permission for one case; 〜ても〜なくても says the result is fixed across both cases.

meanings: partly because; with ~ also being a factor
structure: な-adjective＋な／である＋こともあって
Noun＋という／である＋こともあって
explanation: 〜こともあって cites one contributing reason while openly signaling it is not the whole story: 駅から近いこともあって、いつも混んでいる = partly because it's near the station, it's always crowded. The も does the work — 'this factor, among others, exists'. It attaches to plain-form clauses (nouns take という or である) and suits neutral explanation in both speech and writing; the main clause states the resulting situation.

meanings: don't blame me if ~; I won't be responsible even if ~
structure: Sentence＋（どう）なっても知らない
explanation: 〜ても知らない is a warning that the speaker washes their hands of the consequences: 'even if ~ happens, that's not my problem'. そんなに食べたら、お腹を壊しても知らないよ = if you eat that much and get a stomachache, don't blame me. 知らない here means 'I take no responsibility', not 'I don't know'. It typically follows a hypothetical the speaker has advised against, and is casual and admonishing.

related.note: 〜たら最後 warns that once ~ happens an unavoidable bad result follows; ても知らない warns that the speaker won't take responsibility for such a result.

meanings: before one knows it; without noticing; at some unnoticed point
explanation: いつの間にか says a change took place at some point you never noticed — you only realize it after the fact. いつの間にか眠っていた = I had fallen asleep before I knew it. It emphasizes that the moment of change slipped by unobserved, and it pairs naturally with a resulting state such as 〜ていた. Use it for changes that quietly happened while your attention was elsewhere.

related.note: うちに frames doing something within a period ('while / before'); いつの間にか marks a change you failed to notice.

meanings: suddenly; without thinking; a thought or glance crossing one's mind unbidden
explanation: ふと is an adverb for something that happens suddenly and without intention — especially a thought, feeling, or glance that crosses your mind on its own. 'It just occurred to me...', 'I happened to glance up...'. It pairs naturally with verbs of noticing, thinking, and looking.

related.note: つい is doing something unintentionally despite yourself; ふと is a thought or glance arising on its own, with no action you 'gave in' to.
いきなり is an abrupt event with no warning; ふと is quieter — something gently crossing your mind.

meanings: not a few; quite a lot
structure: Noun ＋ は／が ＋ 少なくない
explanation: 少なくない is the negative of 少ない used as understatement: by denying that something is few, it asserts there are actually quite a lot. It has a slightly written, objective tone, common in reports and opinion statements.

synonyms.note: たくさん says 'a lot' directly; 少なくない says it by understatement.

related.note: 〜くない is the plain い-adjective negative this expression is built from.

meanings: simply because; all because of; on account of (leading to an unwelcome result)
structure: な-adjective＋ な／Noun＋ である ＋ ばかりに
explanation: ばかりに points to a single cause and blames an unfortunate outcome on it — 'all because of just this, that bad thing happened.' It carries a note of regret or frustration, so the result is almost always negative. Typically the clause before ばかりに is a plain-form verb, often in the past (忘れたばかりに = all because I forgot).

synonyms.note: せいで also blames a cause for a bad result; ばかりに stresses that it was just this one thing that caused it.

related.note: だけに means 'precisely because' and works for good or bad results; ばかりに points to a single cause and expects a bad one.

meanings: not worth ~ing over; not that serious a matter
structure: Verb［dictionary form］＋ほどのことではない
explanation: 〜ほどのことではない dismisses something as not serious enough to warrant a given reaction — 'it's not worth ~ing over, it's not that big a deal'. 泣くほどのことではない = not worth crying over, 病院に行くほどのことではない = nothing worth going to the hospital over. It plays the matter down as failing to rise to the level implied.

synonyms.note: ことはない says 'there's no need to ~'; ほどのことではない says the matter doesn't rise to that level of seriousness.

related.note: までもない says an action is unneeded because the point is self-evident; ほどのことではない downplays how serious the matter is.
